WASHINGTON — Today, Congressman Greg Casar (D-Texas) and Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) introduced the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act — legislation to stop artificial intelligence (AI) oligarchs from building machines humans cannot control and to pause advanced AI development until we have put in place rigorous federal testing and oversight to ensure AI does not harm humanity.

“Experts are warning that AI superintelligence, wielded by the wrong humans or by rogue AI, could kill countless numbers of people. But Donald Trump says he wants to encourage it. Something has to change,” Congressman Casar said. “Our bill bans the development of artificial superintelligence and pushes for international agreements so that no one, anywhere, builds AI too powerful for humans to control. Furthermore, our bill would immediately halt other dangerous AI capabilities, such as the capacity to develop biochemical weapons, or the capacity for AI to develop new AI instead of humans.”

“When you are racing towards a cliff, you don’t just ease up on the gas pedal. You hit the brakes. When the future of humanity is at stake, we need binding international safety rules, not voluntary standards from the industry,” Senator Sanders said. “Scientists have been clear: AI is an existential threat to humanity. It must be treated as such. This legislation will permanently ban the development of artificial superintelligence and would put in place an immediate pause on advanced AI development until we have clear safety rules in place — developed by the most knowledgeable scientists in our country. Congress must act now before it is too late.”

The Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act will protect humanity by:

Banning Artificial Superintelligence. No person or entity may develop or deploy Artificial Superintelligence — an AI that exceeds human cognitive performance and capabilities across most domains, or has sufficient capabilities to destroy or disempower humanity, including by overthrowing the federal government.

Pausing Advanced AI development until a new, federal AI regulatory body is up and running and has established clear rules and model review process to ensure safe and secure development and deployment of AI.

Establishing a new cabinet-level federal agency, the Department of Artificial Intelligence, to safeguard the public from the dangers of artificial intelligence, including by enforcing a prohibition on artificial superintelligence. This agency will be advised by the most knowledgeable scientists in our country to:

Monitor frontier AI systems at all stages of the lifecycle for dangerous capabilities.

Supervise the removal of dangerous capabilities like subverting shutdown commands or conducting unauthorized cyberattacks.

Supervise the destruction of artificial superintelligence.

Setting penalties for any person or entity that attempts to violate or circumvent the pauses and prohibitions laid out in this bill. Entities shall be subject to the corporate death penalty, and persons shall be subject to not more than 20 years in prison, which is similar to existing penalties related to unlawfully developing nuclear weapons.

Working to ban superintelligence around the world by setting the international policy of the United States to pursue international agreements, allied coordination, and policies such as export controls to prevent the development of artificial superintelligence anywhere in the world.

WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congressman André Carson (IN-07) questioned witnesses at a first-of-its-kind hearing calling for a U.S.-China agreement to responsibly pace the development of Artificial Intelligence (AI). This hearing was held by Democrats on the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party.

The hearing occurred after Speaker Mike Johnson canceled the previously scheduled legislative session, including votes and committee hearings, without taking action on AI. Congressman Carson previously joined 106 Democrats in calling on the speaker to hold a vote to address AI cybersecurity, surveillance, and rogue AI agent concerns.

“This administration is moving quickly to put advanced AI into our military and intelligence systems,” said Congressman Carson in today’s hearing. “Some decisions are simply too important to hand over to a machine…As AI moves deeper into our national security systems, where should we draw a hard line and say a human has to make the decision?”

Congressman Carson also raised the alarm on the potential need for new regulatory frameworks for AI in cyberattacks and biological weapons. “We already have laws and international agreements dealing with cyberattacks and biological weapons,” Congressman Carson said. “But we know that AI can make those threats easier to carry out and potentially much more dangerous.”

Witnesses included:

· Dr. Geoffrey Hinton, Professor Emeritus, University of Toronto and Nobel Laureate

· Lt. Gen. John (Jack) N.T. Shanahan (USAF, Ret.), Adjunct Senior Fellow, Center for a New American Security

· Matt Sheehan, Senior Fellow, Asia Program and Co-Director, China AI Initiative, Carnegie Endowment for International Peace

· Miriam Vogel, President and CEO, EqualAI

· Seán Ó hÉigeartaigh, Professor and Director of the AI: Futures and Responsibilities Programme, University of Cambridge

Pressley Has Repeatedly Pressed Trump Admin. to Support an Exemption, Highlighting Harmful Impact on Families with Babies and Young Children

Treasury and Trump Have Said Exemption Was “Under Consideration,” and Bessent Affirmed That Last Week After Questioning from Pressley

BOSTON – Today, ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to the United States, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), a member of the House Financial Services Committee, renewed her calls for the Trump Administration to support an exemption to tariffs on baby products and other items that parents need to care for their kids, such as car seats. Congresswoman Pressley has repeatedly pressed Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to support an exemption, highlighting the harmful impact of Trump’s tariffs on families with young children.

Last week, during questioning from Congresswoman Pressley, Secretary Bessent told the Congresswoman to “watch this space after President Xi’s visit.”

“Donald Trump’s reckless and chaotic tariff policy is continuing to wreak havoc on our economy, and families with young children are no exception. With the cost of essential baby products like car seats, strollers, and highchairs skyrocketing due to Trump’s tariffs, it’s time for the Trump Administration to stop hurting America’s families and create an exemption for these essential goods,” said Congresswoman Pressley in a statement. “We don’t need any more lip service from this Administration—we need action.”

In a May 2025 House Financial Services Committee hearing, after sharp questioning from Congresswoman Pressley, Secretary Bessent conceded that such an exemption was “under consideration,” which was later reaffirmed by President Trump.

In February 2026, Congresswoman Pressley demanded Secretary Bessent commit to his prior support for exempting baby products from Trump’s tariffs.

In April 2025, Congresswoman Pressley joined 45 colleagues in sending a Congressional letter to the Trump Administration imploring them to end tariffs on essential baby goods.

title: Ahead of Xi Visit, Pressley Renews Calls for Tariff Exemption on Essential Baby Products

WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Representative Jamie Raskin (MD-08), House Foreign Affairs Committee Ranking Member Gregory Meeks (NY-05) and Representative Jim McGovern (MA-02) called on President Donald Trump to express the United States’ opposition to China’s sweeping new law to repress ethnic minorities and silence critics around the world, including U.S. citizens, during his meetings with President Xi Jinping at this week’s U.S-China summit. The Ethnic Unity and Progress Law grants Chinese officials broad authority to prosecute transnational dissidents as well as Tibetans, Uyghurs and other ethnic and religious minority groups that it classifies as detrimental to “national unity and Communist Party ideology.”

Xi’s visit to the U.S. is scheduled to begin on September 24. The State Department has previously expressed opposition to China’s Ethnic Unity and Progress Law.

“During your meeting with Xi Jinping, it is imperative that you continue to voice your administration’s disapproval of this affront to the fundamental freedoms of minority communities, human rights advocates and U.S. citizens,” the lawmakers wrote to President Trump.

Enacted in March, the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law furthers the Chinese government’s efforts to systematically persecute ethnic and religious minorities and attack critics under the guise of protecting ‘social harmony.’

The law allows China to target dissidents around the world, including U.S. citizens living outside of China. In recent years, China has sought to silence pro-democracy voices through monetary bounties on Hong Kong advocates, cyberhacking campaigns and other intimidation tactics. Absent a repeal of the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law, the use of such tactics will only become more frequent.

“We greatly appreciated the State Department’s earlier statement expressing concerns about the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law,” the lawmakers continued. “A president’s personal advocacy, however, has unparalleled power to elicit meaningful change.”

The lawmakers specifically cited the case of Min Zin, a U.S. citizen detained in June while visiting China for an academic conference, to illustrate the government’s repressive practices. Min was an active voice for democracy in Southeast Asia. He remains in Chinese custody.

The Chinese government has a long and troubling history of subordinating and forcefully assimilating religious and ethnic groups that it deems a threat to state security. As the lawmakers noted, Chinese authorities have sought “to destroy the shrines of Uyghur Muslims, remove Tibetan Buddhist statues from monasteries, censor the holy texts read in Christian churches and otherwise purge houses of worship…”

Raskin, Meeks and McGovern are among the most vocal advocates in Congress for human rights around the world. They have sought and obtained the release numerous of prisoners of conscience, including through the Tom Lantos Commission’s Defending Freedoms Project, an effort to bring attention to international human rights abuses. Tibetan writer Kunchok Tsephel and Vietnamese climate activist Dang Dinh Bach—two political prisoners sponsored by Raskin—were later released from prison.

The letter is also signed by Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi (CA-11) and Representatives Jake Auchincloss (MA-04), Ami Bera (CA-06), André Carson (IN-07), Kathy Castor (FL-14), Steve Cohen (TN-09), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), Lloyd Doggett (TX-10), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Al Green (TX-09), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), George Latimer (NY-16), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), Grace Meng (NY-06), Jerry Nadler (NY-12), Richard Neal (MA-01), Eleanor Norton (DC-AL), Ilhan Omar (MN-05), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Brad Schneider (IL-10), Brad Sherman (CA-32), Tom Suozzi (NY-03), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Dina Titus (NV-01), James Walkinshaw (VA-11) , Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25) and Maxine Waters (CA-43).

The letter is endorsed by the International Campaign for Tibet, Uyghur Human Rights Project and Committee for Freedom in Hong Kong Foundation.

Read the full letter here and below.

President Donald J. Trump

The White House

1600 Pennsylvania Avenue NW

Washington, DC 20500

Dear President Trump,

As you engage with President Xi Jinping this month, we urge you to express profound opposition to the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law recently implemented by the Chinese government.

This law grants Chinese authorities sweeping authority to prosecute Tibetans, Uyghurs and other ethnic and religious minority groups that it broadly accuses of undermining national unity and Communist Party ideology.

Moreover, the extraterritorial scope of the law means that it will dramatically accelerate China’s transnational repression of critics living in the U.S. The State Department has itself recognized these ramifications in a statement calling the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law “problematic.” During your meeting with Xi Jinping, it is imperative that you continue to voice your administration’s disapproval of this affront to the fundamental freedoms of minority communities, human rights advocates and U.S. citizens.

Enacted under the guise of promoting “social harmony” on March 12, 2026, the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law is in fact an insidious declaration of China’s intent to further repress religious freedom and the freedom of group association. One of the most troubling provisions of the law would require religious activities to undergo “Sinicization,” a process championed by Xi Jinping and used in reference to the complete subordination and assimilation of religious and ethnic groups to the political ideology of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP). Well before the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law came into effect on July 1, 2026, China had already embarked upon a concerted campaign to destroy the shrines of Uyghur Muslims, remove Tibetan Buddhist statues from monasteries, censor the holy texts read in Christian churches and otherwise purge houses of worship in the name of “Sinicization.” With the additional legal cover provided by their new law, Chinese authorities are escalating their systemic persecution of minority faith communities.

Elsewhere in the text of the law, the Chinese government asserts the alarming power to extend its repressive tactics into U.S. borders and against U.S. citizens. Article 63 plainly states that organizations and individuals outside China will be held legally accountable for activities that China deems are undertaken in opposition to national unity and progress. In codifying this language, China thus purports to exercise jurisdiction over people who are neither Chinese citizens nor residents of the country and who are merely exercising their freedom of expression. For dissidents who fled China in pursuit of the rights and freedoms we enjoy in America, the clause amounts to a promise that they will continue to be pursued by an oppressive state adamant about suppressing their speech and beliefs.

To grasp the consequences of such a promise, one need only examine the tactics China has increasingly deployed against its U.S.-based critics, including U.S. citizens. In the last couple of years alone, the federal government determined conclusively that Chinese officials intimidated student activists who spoke out against its rule, imposed monetary bounties on Hong Kong activists, launched a cyber-hacking campaign targeting dissidents and employed other sophisticated strategies to silence pro-democracy voices in the U.S. Just this summer, Chinese authorities detained Min Zin, a U.S. citizen and doctoral candidate, upon his arrival in the country for an academic conference. Today, Min Zin, who actively promoted democratization in Southeast Asia, remains in Chinese custody. Absent robust efforts to contest the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law, he will be just one of many more targeted U.S. citizens.

Min Zin’s story, along with the broader trends indicating an intensification of China’s crackdown on religious minorities and dissent abroad, should serve as a warning to us all. If left in place, the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law will expedite ongoing transnational repression, religiously motivated and identity-based persecution and other anti-democratic maneuvers of the Chinese government. In fact, emerging evidence suggests that China has actively begun to leverage the measure against the communities it has historically sought to marginalize. Uyghur-language signs are reportedly being removed from city streets, and during a recent tour of Tibet, a top CCP leader pressed authorities to “adapt” Tibetan Buddhism in accordance with the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law.

We greatly appreciated the State Department’s earlier statement expressing concerns about the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law. However, a president’s personal advocacy has unparalleled power to elicit meaningful change. During your upcoming meeting with Xi Jinping, we therefore urge you to ask for the repeal of the Ethnic Unity and Progress Law.

At stake are our national security, sovereignty and basic human rights all over the world.

###
title: Ahead of U.S.-China Summit, Raskin, Meeks, McGovern Urge Trump to Condemn CCP Law Designed to Repress Religious Minorities and Attack Critics Around the World

U.S. Representatives Chellie Pingree (D-Maine) and Robin Kelly (D-Ill.) are leading a group of their Democratic colleagues in demanding that Prime Healthcare end alleged intimidation and retaliation against nurses engaged in federally protected union activity at its hospitals in Maine, Illinois, and Nevada. In a letter to Prime Healthcare Chairman and CEO Dr. Prem Reddy, the lawmakers cite reports of dozens of nurses being suspended or fired, police being called on nurses and organizers lawfully distributing information outside a hospital, and hospital-branded materials urging employees to vote against union representation.

The letter comes as nurses at Central Maine Medical Center in Lewiston, Maine; Olympia Fields Hospital in Olympia Fields, Illinois; and Saint Francis Hospital in Evanston, Illinois, seek representation through the National Nurses Organizing Committee. At Central Maine Medical Center alone, Prime Healthcare has suspended or fired at least 20 nurses during the organizing campaign—actions the nurses and the union allege are retaliation for advocating for safer staffing, adequate resources, and improved patient care. Olympia Fields Hospital has also reportedly suspended six nurses.

“Registered nurses at these Prime facilities are fighting to ensure they can provide the very best care to the communities they serve, including concerns about cuts to vital services that patients rely on. As you are aware, just last year, Senators Duckworth and Durbin contacted you about reversing Prime’s decision to reduce services in several newly acquired hospitals across Illinois,” the lawmakers wrote. “We remain deeply concerned about warnings from these workers that recent changes to services and designations will impact standards and delivery of care in our communities.”

The lawmakers also highlight alleged retaliation at other Prime Healthcare facilities, including the firing of six nurses at Saint Mary of Nazareth Hospital in Chicago ahead of a June union election and two nurses at Saint Mary’s Regional Medical Center in Reno, Nevada. They are urging Prime Healthcare to comply fully with the National Labor Relations Act, allow employees to decide freely whether to unionize, and negotiate in good faith with workers who choose union representation.[CI3]

“All workers should have the free choice to join a union, should they choose to form one, without interference or intimidation,” they said. “[...] We will continue to monitor Prime Healthcare’s actions closely and, should nurses at those facilities form a union, expect you to negotiate a fair contract in good faith with workers in accordance with the law.”

The letter is available here and is copied below.

Joining Pingree and Kelly on the letter are: Reps. Gilbert Cisneros (D-Calif.), Jesús "Chuy" García (D-Ill.), Jared Golden (D-Maine), Jared Huffman (D-Calif.), Jonathan Jackson (D-Ill.), Ro Khanna (D-Calif.), Mike Quigley (D-Ill.), Delia Ramirez (D-Ill.), Jan Schakowsky (D-Ill.), Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), Lauren Underwood (D-Ill.), and Maxine Waters (D-Calif.).

The offices of Rep. Sewell and Senator Britt will host a joint information session on Tuesday, September 29 at the Marion Military Institute

Birmingham, AL — Today, U.S. Rep. Terri Sewell (AL-07) announced that her office is now accepting applications from eligible students in Alabama’s 7th Congressional District seeking nominations to attend one of the nation’s military service academies.

“Nominating young people from Alabama’s 7th Congressional District to attend our nation’s military service academies is one of my most rewarding responsibilities as a Member of Congress,” said Rep. Sewell. “Our service academies offer an exceptional education, unparalleled leadership development, and the opportunity to serve our country. I encourage all eligible students who are committed to public service and interested in pursuing this path to apply. I look forward to supporting the next generation of Alabama leaders as they answer the call to serve.”

To be considered for a nomination, applicants must meet the eligibility requirements established by law and be legally domiciled within the boundaries of Alabama’s 7th Congressional District. As of July 1 of the year of admission, applicants must be at least 17 years old but not yet 23, be a U.S. citizen, be unmarried, not be pregnant, and have no legal obligation to support children or other dependents. Applicants must also meet the academic, medical, and physical requirements established by the academy to which they are applying.

Students seeking a congressional nomination must complete the nomination process through Rep. Sewell’s office in addition to completing the admissions application for the service academy or academies they wish to attend. A completed nomination packet includes the required application materials, standardized test scores, three letters of recommendation, a high school transcript, and an official college transcript, if applicable. Applicants are encouraged to include their academic achievements, extracurricular activities, leadership experience, awards, honors, and other accomplishments.

Completed nomination applications must be submitted to Rep. Sewell’s Birmingham office and postmarked no later than Wednesday, November 18, 2026.

Office of Congresswoman Terri A. Sewell

Attn: Military Service Academy Nominations

Two 20th Street North, Suite 1130

Birmingham, AL 35203

Following the application deadline, a selection committee will review completed applications and conduct interviews before making recommendations for nominations. Receiving a congressional nomination does not guarantee admission to a service academy; the academy itself makes the final determination regarding appointments.

There are five U.S. service academies: the United States Military Academy at West Point, the United States Naval Academy, the United States Air Force Academy, the United States Merchant Marine Academy, and the United States Coast Guard Academy. Congressional nominations are required for all except the U.S. Coast Guard Academy, which conducts its own admissions process.

Service Academy Information Session

To help students and their families learn more about the service academy admissions and congressional nomination process, the offices of Congresswoman Terri Sewell and Senator Katie Britt will host an information session on Tuesday, September 29, at the Marion Military Institute.

Tuesday, September 29, 2026

Registration: 4:00 p.m. | Program Begins: 5:00 p.m.

Marion Military Institute

Special Events Room of the Mess Hall

1101 Washington Street

Marion, AL 36756
title: Rep. Sewell Accepting Applications for Military Service Academy Nominations

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) delivered remarks at a press conference with members of the Federal Workforce Caucus and federal employee union leaders to highlight the impact of President Donald Trump's proposed 2027 pay freeze on the federal workforce. Below is a transcript of his remarks:

"Congressman Walkinshaw, thank you very, very much. Congressman Walkinshaw is a new Member of the Congress of the United States. He's not a new member of representing, literally, hundreds of thousands, over the years, federal employees. He is not somebody who is not experienced at running a government who can make sure that you can recruit and retain the best, so that we can give people the best service possible. He is not new to the challenge that he met when he came to Congress of the United States with this Administration, with Russell Vought, whose intent, as he pointed out, was to visit Trump on federal employees. And to the federal employees who may be watching, our president reported $2.2 billion of income. Do any of you think when he goes to the grocery store – I don’t think he goes to the grocery store – and he picks up a piece of pizza, says, ‘That may be too expensive for me.’ Or that when he goes to a gasoline station – of course, we know he doesn’t – that he worries about either diesel or gasoline products being $2, $3, or $4 higher than they were six months ago? Of course you don't. Americans are struggling to pay their bills. Americans are struggling to reach an economy that is affordable for them and their families. By the way, federal employees are Americans, and they are consumers, and they are struggling. And while the President says, ‘Zero for the federal employees,’ if you're not a federal employee, he's saying 'Zero' to you as well. How is he saying that? He’s saying, ‘I don't care what inflation is. I don't care [that] costs are going up. I'm going to keep this war going.’ A war of choice. I'm making some signs up, it's going to be at number of gas stations in my district that’s going to say, ‘Pay Trump's War Tax Here.’

"I was the sponsor of the Federal Employee Pay Comparability Act. It passed in 2010 or thereabouts – I think it was 2010, a couple of decades ago – and what that bill said [was], ‘We're going to pay somebody in the federal government who does a job that is done in the private sector, comparable.’ Why do [we] want to pay them more comparable? Because we want to compete, so that when DOGE wipes out a couple hundred thousand positions and then, by the way, hires back because, 'Oh, we needed those people,' and you need to hire competent, capable people who have the skills to do the jobs that Americans need them [done] and their families. That's why we're here. That's why we're saying, ‘Yes, the sergeant over at the Pentagon who is sitting there at the computer and doing a job needs to be compensated in a fair and effective way. But by the way, the person sitting next to that sergeant in a civilian guard, not in the military, who is doing exactly the same thing, exactly the same thing, ought to be comparably compensated.' This president said, ‘Zero, Mack. You're on your own. Take a hike. I don't care that you're having problems getting food. I don't care that you're having problems paying $6 a gallon if you had a diesel vehicle, or $4.50 if you got a gasoline vehicle.’ And then you have to make a choice between that and your rent, between that and your groceries, between that and your medical costs. ‘I don't care because I made $2.2 billion, so why do I care? And my son had his wedding paid for.' Although he's worth not a billion, perhaps, but hundreds of millions of dollars himself. His cost of living, of course, is the interest he gets every day, which exceeds what that sergeant makes in a year. So, he apparently doesn't care.

"So, I’m pleased to join my friend, Congressman Walkinshaw, and my friend, Senator Van Hollen. The civilian pay freeze announced by the Administration is just the latest example of how he traumatized Americans – not just federal employees, Americans – why he doesn't care about your costs, why he hasn't offered a policy to help them. They’re trying to create tension and an artificial divide between civilian [employees] and those who wear a uniform. I have been for comparability since I came to the Congress of the United States 45 years ago, and we've been largely successful – not completely, there were a lot of years where we took a pass, some because things were tough for everybody. And by the way, the Pay Comparability Act says, ‘Civilian employees in the federal government cannot get a raise if the private sector economic cost (inaudible). That’s what the law says. And, Mr. Walkinshaw, it's about 3.2- 3.3% and going up, and inflation is outstripping – even in the private sector [salary increases].

"So, I'm very hopeful that our Members of Congress – we’ll see what the election results [are], we’re hopeful. The fact of that is, most Members of Congress are dispersed, two weeks before we were supposed to. Somehow, we thought our work was done, while people are struggling, while gas prices are spiraling, while health care costs and housing costs are driving people to distraction, and worse. I want to thank Representative Walkinshaw, I want to thank you Senator Van Hollen, I want all of you for supporting this effort. I want to thank the federal employee unions who have been so active. I congratulate all of them for keeping the faith for the American people and making sure that people who work for the government are still able to afford to work for the government. I’m sure I have some other great remarks, but I'm afraid I’ve probably talked too long. But we need all of you who are watching, just say to your representatives, say to the Congress of the United States, say to the President of the United States, ‘We value the people for helping us at the federal, state and local level and we need to make sure they don't fall through the floorboards,’ because that’s what’s happening. With the rising costs and the lack of affordable in the American economy, the average working man and woman cannot make $2.2 billion a year. I now yield to my dear friend, and our senior senator from Maryland, who has been, himself, a very strong, consistent, and faithful voice on behalf of federal employees. Of course, being faithful to our federal employees is being faithful to our country, to our state, and to our people. Senator Van Hollen."
title: Hoyer: People Who Work for the Government Should Be Able to Afford to Work for the Government

Ryan – an Army combat veteran and member of the Congressional Gun Violence Prevention Task Force – has been a consistent advocate for gun violence prevention throughout his time in Congress

Guns remain the leading cause of death for children and teens in the United States; Ryan is a proud co-sponsor of the Assault Weapons Ban and has championed legislation promoting universal background checks and safe gun storage

Roundtable participants included representatives from Moms Demand Action, Family Services, local elected officials and more

POUGHKEEPSIE, NY – Last week, Congressman Pat Ryan – an Army combat veteran and member of the Congressional Gun Violence Prevention Task Force – joined Hudson Valley community leaders and gun violence prevention advocates for a roundtable discussion in Poughkeepsie. As violent crime rates continue falling in the Hudson Valley, advocates and leaders discussed efforts to build upon that progress and keep communities safe.

Guns remain the leading cause of death for children and teens in the United States; in 2026, there have already been 83 incidents of gunfire on school grounds, resulting in 27 deaths and 47 injuries nationwide.

Ryan is a proud co-sponsor of several bills curtailing the gun violence epidemic, including the Assault Weapons Ban.

Roundtable participants included representatives from Moms Demand Action, Family Services, local elected officials and more.

“I’m so grateful to everyone who gathered for today’s conversation. From local law enforcement, to elected leaders, to nonprofits dedicated to keeping our communities safe, this coalition has done amazing work toward ending the scourge of gun violence in Dutchess County and beyond. Tackling this epidemic requires all-hands-on-deck, and we recommitted to working together to save lives.,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “There is nothing more important than keeping our communities – especially our kids – safe. As a combat veteran I know the weapons I carried in war have no place on our streets or in our schools. That’s why I proudly co-sponsor the Assault Weapons Ban, and support legislation promoting red flag laws, safe firearm storage, and universal background checks. We’ve made encouraging progress, but there’s still more work ahead. While the Trump administration tries to roll back our efforts, I’m continuing to fight for commonsense gun safety legislation and to help make sure the people doing the work to keep our communities safe have the resources they need.”

“At Family Services we see firsthand the devastating impact that violence has on children, families, and entire neighborhoods, and we also see the incredible strength and resilience of the people working to create safer communities,” said Leah Feldman, CEO, Family Services, Poughkeepsie. “That is why sustained investment in community violence intervention is so important. Programs like SNUG provide a critical connection between communities and the resources, support, and opportunities that can prevent violence. We are grateful for leaders like Congressman Ryan who recognize the importance of this work and continue to bring attention and resources to the effort to build safer communities.”

When young people experience violence in their neighborhoods, schools, or homes, the impact can extend far beyond the immediate moment, affecting their sense of safety, their ability to learn, and their vision for what is possible for their future,” said Jill Gomez, ED, Poughkeepsie Children’s Cabinet. “As a Children’s Cabinet, we believe every young person deserves to grow up surrounded by adults, institutions, and systems that work together to create safe, connected communities. Preventing gun violence requires that same collective commitment: listening to young people and families, strengthening the places and relationships that protect them, and aligning our community’s resources around the conditions that allow every child to thrive.”

“I am a Survivor Lead working out of MOMS Demand Action in the Hudson Valley. MOMS Demand Action continues to support initiatives that afford for our voices to be raised on Gun Violence prevention legislation and supporting candidates who wear GunSense on their sleeves. Boots on the ground advocacy for the support of Gun violence prevention is crucial, Gun Violence does not discriminate and we have to STAND ten toes down on electing those in office that will advocate endlessly to end Gun Violence. MOMS Demand Action will continue to advocate, be visible and support those entities that are working in sync to END GUN VIOLENCE,” said Kenya Gadsden. “Statistics often mention that on average 130 people are killed by guns every day in the U.S. with 200 shot and wounded. Guns are the leading cause of deaths among children and teens in this country. We can be the change!”

Congressman Ryan is a proud member of the Gun Violence Prevention Task Force and co-sponsor of the Assault Weapons Ban of 2025, which makes it illegal to import, sell, manufacture, transfer, or possess semiautomatic assault weapons or large-capacity ammunition feeding devices. Existing owners of these weapons must store them securely. It also authorizes the use of Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant funds to run buyback programs to compensate people who surrender their covered weapons or large-capacity magazines.

In addition to the Assault Weapons Ban of 2025, Congressman Ryan proudly co-sponsors:

H.R.2368 – Raise the Age Act of 2025 raises the minimum age to buy a semiautomatic firearm from 18 to 21 and prohibits a licensed gun dealer, importer, collector, or manufacturer from selling or transferring a semiautomatic center-fire shotgun to an individual under 21.

H.R.18 – Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2025 requires background checks for firearm transfers between private parties (i.e., unlicensed individuals) and prohibits the transfer of firearms between private parties unless a licensed gun dealer, manufacturer, or importer takes possession of the firearm first and conducts a background check.

H.R.1564 – Ethan’s Law creates a framework to regulate firearm storage on residential premises at the federal, state, and tribal levels. At the federal level, it establishes requirements for firearms on residential premises to be safely stored if a minor can gain access or if a resident is ineligible to possess a firearm. Individuals who violate this rule face criminal penalties, and firearms stored in violation of the requirements are subject to seizure and forfeiture. At state and tribal levels, the bill requires the Department of Justice to award grants for the safe storage of firearms.

H.R.3018 – Federal Extreme Risk Protection Order Act authorizes federal courts to issue federal extreme risk protection orders, which allow certain individuals (such as law enforcement officers and family members) to petition a court for a temporary order prohibiting an at-risk individual from purchasing or possessing firearms.

H.R.4261 – Stopping the Fraudulent Sales of Firearms Act makes it illegal to sell or attempt to sell firearms or ammunition under pretenses. It strengthens regulations on the sale and distribution of firearms to improve overall safety and accountability in the firearms market.

Congressman Ryan also knows that the intersection of gun violence and domestic abuse cannot be ignored. Women in the United States are five times more likely to be murdered if their abuser has access to a firearm, and someone is shot and killed by a current or former intimate partner every 12 hours. In May, Ryan introduced groundbreaking domestic violence legislation to protect victims and their families. Ryan’s bill works to expand New York State’s Melanie’s Law nationwide. Melanie’s Law, signed into law in New York in 2024, is named for Wappingers Falls woman Melanie Chianese. In 2022, Melanie was killed by her mother’s abuser after an egregious gap in the law left her unable to obtain an order of protection. Ryan’s legislation incentivizes states to adopt laws similar to Melanie’s Law through the creation of a new federal grant program.

NORWICH, CT – Today, Congressman Joe Courtney (CT-02), Ranking Member of the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee, issued the following statement after sending a letter to his colleagues on the Armed Services Committee in response to the recent Government Accountability Office (GAO) report on Navy submarine repairs. “I agree that the past track record of submarine repairs is unsatisfactory and that GAO’s recommendation to create more efficient ways to decommission submarines without interfering with maintenance of operational submarines is extremely helpful,” Courtney said. “My letter to my colleagues on the Armed Services Committee includes more up-to-date information regarding of the latest inventory of Virginia-class submarines and corrects the report’s omission of Seawolf submarines, which, as the original follow-on to the Los Angeles-class fleet, are a premier cohort the U.S submarine attack fleet.

“My letter also noted that because of Congress’ swift authorization of the AUKUS security agreement, the U.S. Navy’s submarine fleet will have new intermediate repair capacity forward-deployed in the Indo-Pacific at a new repair facility in Western Australia. That capacity is joined by an $8.5 billion Australian investment in repair availability for Virginia-class submarines and the future SSN-AUKUS submarines,” Courtney continued. “It is indisputable that the Navy needs to organize a submarine repair plan that achieves its stated goal of 80% availability. Congress and the Navy’s commitment of over $21 billion to upgrade public shipyards through Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program will go a long way to help achieve this goal.”

Pearsall, TX — Today, staff from the Office of Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20) shared the following statement on behalf of Congressman Castro, after members of his staff and Congressman Greg Casar (TX-35) visited Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez at the South Texas ICE Processing Center (STIPC) in Pearsall, Texas:

"My apologies for not being with you today. An hours-long flight delay kept me from joining Congressman Casar in visiting Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez. As the Congressman for Austin, Wilber's home, Greg's unyielding pursuit of truth and justice in this matter has been admirable. Thank you, Congressman, for that work.

“ICE's treatment of Wilber thus far has amounted to torture. That is not an exaggeration in this case. After being shot in the back and handcuffed without first aid, he was allowed to stay in the hospital for only a few hours before being taken to a detention center while in excruciating pain and made to lie on the floor. The medical facilities at the South Texas ICE Processing Center (STIPC) in Pearsall are not equipped to handle a patient who has experienced that kind of trauma. ICE knew this but took him there anyway. It got so bad that he had to be taken back to the hospital, but again he was allowed to remain only hours before being returned to STIPC. He told ICE agents about his excruciating pain and told them that he could no longer move the left side of his body. Yet they let him suffer with their bullet still in his body.

“This immigrant man, a Venezuelan, fled a regime that President Trump himself declared a terrorist one, just as millions of Venezuelans have fled over the past several years. He had permission to enter the United States and to work. And that's what he was doing when ICE shot him in the back, delivering food for DoorDash to support himself and his family. In fact, he told my staff that he had been working in the area for quite some time and that all the restaurants in the area know him. He also asked my staff to tell his wife and mother that he was doing okay, as not to worry them. This is who ICE is targeting.

“ICE has shot and killed people before, including U.S. citizens, and lied about it. They have discredited themselves. There must be an independent investigation, and the ICE officers who shot Wilber in the back should be held accountable. Finally, this system known as ICE, which has allowed a man to be tortured, should be disbanded.”

Stanton Calls for AI Safeguards Ahead of Trump-Xi Meeting
WASHINGTON D.C. – Ahead of Trump’s meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, U.S. Representative Greg Stanton (AZ-04) joined his Democratic colleagues on the House Select Committee on Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party to call for the United States and China to reach an agreement on basic artificial intelligence safeguards.
Stanton emphasized that AI should be a major part of the two leaders’ conversations and stressed the need for the two countries to work together to prevent catastrophic misuse of the rapidly developing technology, drawing attention to the risks Washington and Beijing share.
This follows Stanton’s efforts ahead of the summit to ensure AI safety receives the immediate attention in Washington it deserves. Last week, he joined 26 of his Democratic colleagues on the House Foreign Affairs Committee in calling on Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to urge the administration to pursue sustained, substantive U.S.-China dialogue on AI safety risks and prioritize those issues in the upcoming bilateral summit.
Stanton also joined 106 of his colleagues in urging Speaker Mike Johnson to bring the House back into session to address the risks posed by advanced AI, including mass cybersecurity breaches and the development of biological or chemical weapons.
Full text of Stanton’s remarks as prepared is below, and video is HERE.
—
Thank you to our witnesses for joining us today.
Tomorrow, leaders of the two most powerful AI nations on earth will sit across from each other. They’ll talk about trade, tariffs and Taiwan. . . but if they walk away without real progress on AI, they will have missed the mark.
I believe America can and will win the AI race, and I believe we have a duty to do so in a way that protects the interests of the American people. In America, innovation and safety go hand in hand. We can and must do both.
But President Trump’s full steam ahead, safety be damned approach to AI has to change. The consequences of inaction are incredibly serious.
Here at home, American workers are unprotected as AI rapidly transforms entire economies. American intellectual property is open to theft through distillation and other unauthorized use.
Beijing has their own concerns. But where our two nations need to come to a common understanding is the threats posed by a rogue actor using this technology for malicious ends.
Our critical infrastructure . . . including our energy grid . . . are exposed to AI-powered cyberattacks that could have catastrophic consequences for our communities.
That is why an agreement on basic safeguards between Trump and Xi is so critically important. And a promise to keep talking is not an agreement. Every month we wait to act, these problems get harder to fix.
I recognize it won’t be easy. In just the past few weeks, the Trump administration has accused Chinese AI companies of stealing intellectual property by distilling leading U.S. AI models . . . threatening sanctions. Beijing, for its part, has accused Washington of deliberately hindering Chinese AI development, seeing appeals for a slowdown as a way for the U.S. to lock in American companies’ lead.
But neither Washington nor Beijing wants a rogue actor using AI to launch a cyber attack that takes down the global economy, or to build and release a bioweapon. That shared concern is where cooperation has to start.
Question 1: Mr. Sheehan, tell us more about what you call “AI safety in parallel,” where the U.S. and China develop their own safeguards while sharing information and best practices. What are two or three concrete standards you believe both countries could find common ground, and what would meaningful cooperation on those standards look like?
Thank you. There is a contradiction between Trump’s safety be damned approach and his decision to ease access to advanced American chips. If China’s progress is the reason we supposedly cannot slow down for safety, why is the administration helping supply the technology that supports their progress?
That’s why I have been clear that we must prohibit the sale of the most advanced chips to China and apply those same prohibitions to all arms-embargoed nations.
Question 2: Mr. Sheehan, you’ve been engaged in Track II discussions with Chinese counterparts for years. How do we design export controls so that they protect our national security and technological advantage while also creating incentives for companies to invest in responsible development?
Thank you.
title: Stanton Calls for AI Safeguards Ahead of Trump-Xi Meeting

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Co-Chairs Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10) and Congressman Jerrold Nadler (NY-12), led the Congressional Jewish Caucus, in calling on Secretary of State Marco Rubio to preserve the office of the Special Envoy for Holocaust Issues (SEHI) as a permanent and distinct entity within the Department of State and not for SEHI to be absorbed under the Special Envoy to Monitor and Combat Antisemitism (SEAS). This letter highlights that SEHI is the only office in the federal government solely devoted to pursuing justice for Holocaust survivors and advocating on their behalf, and the need to appoint a career official as the next SEHI, with the seniority, diplomatic experience, and specialized expertise necessary to negotiate complex restitution and compensation matters.

“Since its establishment in 1999, the Office of the Special Envoy for Holocaust Issues has been the only office in the federal government solely devoted to pursuing justice for Holocaust survivors and advocating on their behalf,” the members wrote. “The office has also been supported on a bipartisan basis in Congress and administrations of both parties have actively affirmed its importance. For decades, SEHI has worked with foreign governments, international institutions, and Jewish organizations to pursue restitution and compensation for survivors and their families, recover Nazi-looted property, preserve Holocaust memory, and address unresolved Holocaust-era obligations. As the number of living Holocaust survivors continues to decline, this work is only becoming more urgent.”

“That is why we oppose any effort to consolidate or eliminate SEHI and are troubled by the reported plan for the Office of the Special Envoy to Monitor and Combat Antisemitism (SEAS) to absorb the SEHI office. SEHI and SEAS have clearly distinct mandates and responsibilities,” the members continued. “Both are full-time responsibilities that require full-time principals with unique areas of focus and full-time staff with unique expertise. Combining them would not streamline efficiency or eliminate any meaningful duplication; it would risk diminishing the focus, experience, and institutional capacity necessary for each.”

“The SEHI portfolio requires deep institutional knowledge, advanced diplomatic acumen, and sustained relationships with governments and international organizations,” the members added. “We ask that you appoint, as soon as possible, a senior career State Department official whose sole and full-time responsibility is serving as Special Envoy for Holocaust Issues. That official should have the seniority, diplomatic experience, and specialized expertise necessary to negotiate complex restitution and compensation matters and to maintain the relationships that SEHI has built over decades.”

Signers of the letter include Reps. Jake Auchincloss, Becca Balint, Suzanne Bonamici, Steve Cohen, Lois Frankel, Laura Friedman, Dan Goldman, Josh Gottheimer, Sara Jacobs, Greg Landsman, Mike Levin, Jared Moskowitz, Jerrold Nadler, Jamie Raskin, Jan Schakowsky, Brad Schneider, Kim Schrier, Eugene Vindman, and Debbie Wasserman Schultz.

View the full letter here and below.

Dear Secretary Rubio,

As members of the Congressional Jewish Caucus, we write to urge you to immediately appoint a new Special Envoy for Holocaust Issues (SEHI) and to preserve SEHI as a distinct, permanent office led by a dedicated career State Department official.

Since its establishment in 1999, the Office of the Special Envoy for Holocaust Issues has been the only office in the federal government solely devoted to pursuing justice for Holocaust survivors and advocating on their behalf. The office has also been supported on a bipartisan basis in Congress and administrations of both parties have actively affirmed its importance. For decades, SEHI has worked with foreign governments, international institutions, and Jewish organizations to pursue restitution and compensation for survivors and their families, recover Nazi-looted property, preserve Holocaust memory, and address unresolved Holocaust-era obligations. As the number of living Holocaust survivors continues to decline, this work is only becoming more urgent.

That is why we oppose any effort to consolidate or eliminate SEHI and are troubled by the reported plan for the Office of the Special Envoy to Monitor and Combat Antisemitism (SEAS) to absorb the SEHI office.

SEHI and SEAS have clearly distinct mandates and responsibilities. SEAS is responsible for confronting contemporary antisemitism around the world, while SEHI focuses on Holocaust-era restitution, historical justice, remembrance, and accountability. These missions are complementary, but they are not interchangeable. Both are full-time responsibilities that require full-time principals with unique areas of focus and full-time staff with unique expertise. Combining them would not streamline efficiency or eliminate any meaningful duplication; it would risk diminishing the focus, experience, and institutional capacity necessary for each.

The effort is also especially troubling given the highly specialized nature of SEHI’s work and the longstanding success of having it led by a career diplomat with the expertise and continuity necessary to conduct sensitive restitution negotiations. The SEHI portfolio requires deep institutional knowledge, advanced diplomatic acumen, and sustained relationships with governments and international organizations. This unique mandate needs an independent office, fully integrated within the Bureau of European and Eurasian Affairs, and without additional or perhaps superseding agenda items both with external interlocutors and internal stakeholders.

Strong institutions must outlast individual officeholders and administrations. We are troubled by the suggestion that the plan to merge these offices may be motivated, at least in part, by a desire to expand the influence of certain personnel within the State Department.

Jewish organizations across the ideological and institutional spectrum have recognized the importance of maintaining a dedicated SEHI. In their letter to you, leading organizations including the Conference on Jewish Material Claims Against Germany, World Jewish Restitution Organization, American Jewish Committee, Anti-Defamation League, B’nai B’rith International, and more urged you to appoint a senior diplomat promptly and preserve the uniqueness of this important office. Their concern is shared by former SEAS and Holocaust experts who understand that preserving the distinct mission of SEHI is not bureaucratic duplication—it is an essential part of the United States’ commitment to Holocaust survivors and their families.

We urge you to heed their call and to reject any effort to eliminate, consolidate, or dual-hat the SEHI position. Instead, we ask that you appoint, as soon as possible, a senior career State Department official whose sole and full-time responsibility is serving as Special Envoy for Holocaust Issues. That official should have the seniority, diplomatic experience, and specialized expertise necessary to negotiate complex restitution and compensation matters and to maintain the relationships that SEHI has built over decades.

This appointment should be made with urgency. The recent departure of Special Envoy Germain creates a vacancy at precisely the moment when continuity is most important. There are fewer Holocaust survivors with each passing year. Every delay risks losing opportunities for restitution, accountability, and historical preservation that may never return.

The United States created SEHI because Holocaust survivors and their families require a dedicated advocate within our government. That need has not diminished. It has become more urgent. We urge you to put an end to the effort to consolidate these offices and to appoint a new, dedicated, career Special Envoy for Holocaust Issues without delay.
title: CONGRESSIONAL JEWISH CAUCUS URGES SECRETARY RUBIO TO PRESERVE SPECIAL ENVOY FOR HOLOCAUST ISSUES AS A DISTINCT AND PERMANENT OFFICE

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, September 23, 2026, as momentum builds in Congress behind a national film tax credit, U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) released a record of her work to create a national film tax credit and bring film and television production jobs back to the United States.

“I started working on this as soon as I got to Congress. Now, because of the effort we’ve put in alongside incredible Members of Congress like Rep. Brian Jack and Senator Adam Schiff, we’re closer than ever to getting it done,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30). “Sixty-five other countries decided to compete for these jobs, and no single state can outbid a foreign government. These are carpenters, electricians, drivers, and camera operators in all 50 states, and I won't stop until we bring their work home.”

Built the coalition behind this effort starting in 2025: Variety reported in May 2025 that Friedman was drafting the House bill and recruiting Republicans to build a bipartisan coalition behind it. Since then, she has worked with Rep. Brian Jack, Senator Adam Schiff, Jon Voight, industry unions, studios, producers, and more to make the case for a national film tax credit before the issue had political momentum.

Co-founded the Congressional American Film & TV Production Caucus in September 2026 with Reps. Brian Jack (GA-03), Nathaniel Moran (TX-01), Linda Sánchez (CA-38), Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11), and Tom Suozzi (NY-03), giving the effort a bipartisan home in the House. Release here.

Convened a roundtable with the Directors Guild of America Leadership Council in August 2025 on bringing production back to the United States, building on an earlier roundtable with local businesses and community leaders and a rally of entertainment labor unions. Release here.

Brought the job losses on the record in the district, joining Sen. Adam Schiff’s March 2026 Spotlight Hearing in Burbank, “Lights, Camera, Competition: Promoting American Film Production.”

Making the Case Early in 2025:

Los Angeles Times, May 2025 – Named Friedman and Sen. Adam Schiff among the lawmakers who had been advocating a national program to put the United States on equal footing with countries offering more generous incentives. Read here.

Variety, May 2025 – Friedman said she wanted to refocus the conversation around a national film tax credit, and was drafting the House bill while recruiting Republicans to build a bipartisan coalition behind it. Read here.

Spectrum News 1, May 2025 – Friedman said she was already negotiating with colleagues on a national film tax credit to help every state with film production, and welcomed conversations with the administration. Read here.

The Hollywood Reporter, September 2025 – Friedman, a former film producer, redirected the tariff conversation to a national film tax credit, arguing it works in California and will work across the country. Read here.

Building the Coalition 2026:

NPR, September 2026 – Friedman told Weekend Edition that the country is losing an industry employing people across a wide range of crafts and occupations, and that she wants the United States to lead the world in entertainment and content. Listen here.

Los Angeles Times, September 2026 – Friedman said she would put American crews and talent against any in the world, and that productions will come back if they have a level playing field to shoot on. Read here.

Variety, September 2026 – Reported that Friedman and Sen. Schiff were among the first to call for federal action to supplement state tax credits. Read here.

The Hollywood Reporter, September 2026 – On the caucus launch, Friedman made the case that bringing production back to the United States is not a partisan fight. Read here.

Deadline, September 2026 – Confirmed Friedman as one of the members spearheading the effort in the House. Read here.

The Washington Times, September 2026 – Friedman called it a major mistake that the United States has nothing to compete with at the federal level. Read here.

Select Committee Democrats Urge Trump to Address AI Risks with Xi
WASHINGTON — All eleven Democratic Members of the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party today urged President Donald Trump to make artificial intelligence a central topic of his upcoming meeting with General Secretary Xi Jinping.
In a letter to the White House, the entire Democratic roster of the Select Committee emphasized that “it is essential that [President Trump] use the opportunity at this Thursday’s meeting with General Secretary Xi to discuss AI.” The letter highlights the escalating risks posed by AI, the importance of maintaining America’s innovation edge, and the role of diplomacy in addressing common interests of the U.S. and the People’s Republic of China, like preventing the loss of human control.
“America’s AI advantage depends on being leaders in both AI technology and governance,” the Members wrote.
The Members pointed to growing calls from AI researchers and industry for safeguards around the development of increasingly advanced models, including concerns about the potential loss of human control over AI and the possibility of AI-enabled biological or chemical attacks.
The Members further noted that discussions with the PRC on these risks need not undermine U.S. technological leadership. Instead, they said, the United States should identify areas where Washington and Beijing may have shared interests while maintaining clear mechanisms for verifying any commitments made by the PRC.
Among the issues raised in the letter was the growing conversation about the possibility of a binding, enforceable, and verifiable international agreement addressing the most serious risks associated with advanced AI.
“Especially when engaging with the PRC, the U.S. cannot assume commitments will be upheld unless there are clear mechanisms for verifying compliance,” the Members wrote.
The Members also underscored the importance of establishing open diplomatic channels on AI risks, arguing that the consequences of failing to responsibly navigate the rapid advancement of the technology could extend beyond the U.S. and the PRC.
The Members requested that the Administration provide Congress with a briefing following President Trump’s meeting with General Secretary Xi, including details about any discussions concerning artificial intelligence.
“Just as humans must be kept in the loop of this technology, Congress must be kept in the loop of your diplomacy,” the Members concluded.
The letter came ahead of a Select Committee shadow hearing on diplomatic negotiations between the U.S. and China on AI, where world-leading experts discussed potential outcomes from the Trump-Xi summit and key provisions of any U.S.-China accord.
The letter’s signatories – the entire Democratic roster of the Select Committee – are as follows:
Ranking Member Ro Khanna (CA-17)
Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08)
Rep. Kathy Castor (FL-14)
Rep. André Carson (IN-07)
Rep. Seth Moulton (MA-06)
Rep. Haley Stevens (MI-11)
Rep. Ritchie Torres (NY-15)
Rep. Shontel Brown (OH-11)
Rep. Greg Stanton (AZ-04)
Rep. Jill Tokuda (HI-02)
Rep. Tom Suozzi (NY-03)
Read the letter in full HERE.

title: Select Committee Democrats Urge Trump to Address AI Risks with Xi

SALINAS, CA — On Tuesday, Congresswoman Zoe Lofgren (CA-18) visited Hartnell College’s Child Development Center to deliver a $250,000 check as one of her 13 community projects she submitted for the Fiscal Year 2026 congressional appropriations cycle. These funds will be used to renovate the Center’s outdoor learning environment and make essential safety upgrades.

“It’s great to visit Hartnell College again and celebrate this win for the children of Salinas,” said Rep. Zoe Lofgren. “The Child Development Center here has provided great programming for kids and has helped parents with young children pursue their educational goals. Every parent wants their child to be able to play outside safely, and I’m happy to help deliver this funding to help renovate the outdoor learning environment."

"We're thankful for this investment, which will finally allow us to give our youngest students a space that matches the quality of learning we want to provide every day,” said Michael Gutierrez, Superintendent/President of Hartnell College. “The Child Development Center has always been about supporting Salinas families. We thank Congresswoman Lofgren for recognizing that investing in early childhood education is investing in our entire community."

The Child Development Center at the main campus of Hartnell College serves the larger Salinas community by providing a quality preschool program that facilitates the transition to kindergarten for children 2 through 5 years of age. It includes educational development, health services, social services, and nutritional services.

During 3-hour sessions, children spend between 2 and 2.5 hours in the Center’s outdoor learning environment. The outdoor climbing structure was installed in 1995, and a priority of the renovation will be to remove this structure. Currently, children need to cross a bike path to reach the play structure, another safety concern that will be addressed by the renovation. The redesign will also enhance access to gardening, outdoor dramatic play, art and construction, and a variety of natural experiences.

###
title: Lofgren Secures $250k for Hartnell College’s Child Development Center

Northwest Aurora’s proposed flood-control work is tied to about $15.6 million in federal support under the Water Resources Development Act. The House passed the measure Tuesday by a 415-9 vote, but it still needs Senate approval. Even if approved, the authorization alone would not provide all the funding needed for construction.

A Long-Awaited Fix for Chronic Street Flooding

The bill, as reported by Sentinel Colorado, sets aside funding for Aurora to construct new storm sewers and expand the city's stormwater capacity, with planned improvements expected to help prevent flooding on East 11th Avenue, Alton Street and East 14th Avenue in northwest Aurora. Among the specific projects called out is a new storm sewer at the intersection of East 14th Avenue and Yosemite Street, an area residents have watched flood repeatedly.

Rep. Jason Crow advocated for the Aurora funding, according to the same report. He said the investment would address aging sewer infrastructure and flood-related safety problems, while helping the city respond to climate change. Crow also said he would continue seeking federal resources for Colorado communities.

What Else Is Riding on the Bill

Aurora is one part of a broader water-resources package. The legislation dedicates $150 million to protect rural water infrastructure nationwide, a provision noted in the article and by CPR. It also includes funding for several Colorado projects, and Colorado’s House members voted for the measure.

Separately, Crow has introduced the Protect the West Act, which would invest in wildfire mitigation, and sponsors the bipartisan Championing Local Efforts to Advance Resilience Act, which would let states establish and maintain resiliency offices to address climate-change effects. Neither measure was part of Tuesday’s House vote.

Next Stop: The Senate

For now, the Water Resources Development Act awaits approval from the Senate, and the article notes the National Association of Counties reported on both the House passage and the bill's pending Senate status. Whether Aurora's flood-prone streets get their new storm sewers ultimately hinges on what happens next in that chamber.

Authorization Is Not the Final Funding Step

U.S. Army Corps of Engineers guidance explains that authorization alone is not enough for a project to proceed; congressional appropriations are also required. So even after Senate approval, Aurora would still need appropriated funding for the construction work to move forward, according to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.
title: Hoodline: Aurora Could Land $15.6M to Fix Flood-Prone Northwest Streets

WASHINGTON, DC — Ante la discusión pública sobre el financiamiento de Medicaid en Puerto Rico, el Comisionado Residente Pablo José Hernández encabezó una sesión informativa que reunió a expertos en salud, personal congresional de ambos partidos y representantes de sectores vinculados a Medicaid, para elevar la urgencia del tema en Washington y adelantar el trabajo necesario para atender el precipicio fiscal de 2027.

La sesión reunió en una misma mesa a expertos del Congressional Research Service (CRS), la Medicaid and CHIP Payment and Access Commission (MACPAC), el Center on Budget and Policy Priorities (CBPP) y la Universidad de Puerto Rico. Además contó con representantes de la Asociación de Hospitales de Puerto Rico, el Colegio de Médicos Cirujanos de Puerto Rico, la Medicaid and Medicare Advantage Products Association of Puerto Rico (MMAPA) y otros representantes de la industria de salud en Puerto Rico. La sesión también contó con la participación del exgobernador Luis Fortuño, Dr. Carlos R. Mellado López, exsecretario del Departamento de Salud de Puerto Rico, Eduardo Bhatia, expresidente del Senado de Puerto Rico, y representantes de la Administración de Asuntos Federales de Puerto Rico (PRFAA).

La sesión también contó con la participación de los representantes: Héctor Ferrer, portavoz del Partido Popular Democrático (PPD) en la Cámara de Representantes de Puerto Rico; Domingo Torres García del Distrito 25 y portavoz alterno del PPD; Sol Higgins Cuadrado del Distrito 35 y miembro de la Comisión de Salud; y Estrella Martínez Soto del Distrito 27.

Los panelistas explicaron al personal congresional qué está en juego de cara al precipicio fiscal de 2027, desde el impacto sobre pacientes y proveedores hasta la información que el Congreso necesitará para evaluar una solución legislativa.

“Estamos priorizando lo básico: la salud. Necesitamos que el Congreso entienda que está en juego el acceso a la salud de más de un millón de puertorriqueños. Por eso reunimos a expertos, proveedores y representantes del sector de salud de Puerto Rico con personal congresional de ambos partidos.”, dijo el Comisionado Residente.

El financiamiento actual de Medicaid sostiene gran parte de Plan Vital, que brinda cubierta de salud a alrededor de 1.2 millones de personas en Puerto Rico. Las disposiciones vigentes, que incluyen un pareo federal de 76%, vencen el 30 de septiembre de 2027. Sin una nueva acción del Congreso, la asignación federal podría caer de aproximadamente $3,800 billones al año a cerca de $500 millones y el pareo regresaría a 55%.

Las posibles consecuencias de ese escenario han sido documentadas por distintos sectores. Un análisis de Espacios Abiertos estima que entre 700,000 y un millón de personas podrían perder su cubierta de Plan Vital si no se reautorizan los fondos, mientras representantes del sector hospitalario han advertido sobre el impacto que tendría una reducción de esa magnitud sobre la capacidad de prestar servicios de salud en Puerto Rico.

El reto no se limita a evitar una reducción de fondos, sino a lograr que cualquier propuesta ante el Congreso esté sustentada por datos sólidos sobre gastos, matrícula, necesidades del sistema y proyecciones futuras. El Comisionado Residente continúa trabajando con colegas en legislación para atender el precipicio mientras recopila la información necesaria para sustentar ese esfuerzo.

La falta de acción también podría tener consecuencias fuera de Puerto Rico. El Medicaid and CHIP Payment and Access Commission (MACPAC) ha advertido anteriormente que una insuficiencia de fondos de Medicaid en la isla puede aumentar el gasto federal sí beneficiarios elegibles se trasladan a los estados, donde Medicaid no está sujeto al mismo límite federal que enfrenta Puerto Rico.

Haz clic AQUÍ para ver fotos y videos del evento.

RELEASE

Hernández Elevates Puerto Rico Medicaid Crisis Before Congress Ahead of 2027 Funding Cliff.

WASHINGTON, DC — With new estimates warning that Puerto Rico could lose nearly 90 percent of its federal Medicaid funding after September 2027, Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández convened congressional staff and health policy experts to put the Island’s looming Medicaid funding cliff before Congress and begin building the groundwork for action.

The briefing brought together experts from the Congressional Research Service (CRS), the Medicaid and CHIP Payment and Access Commission (MACPAC), the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities (CBPP), and the University of Puerto Rico. It also included representatives from the Puerto Rico Hospital Association, the Puerto Rico College of Physicians and Surgeons, the Medicaid and Medicare Advantage Products Association of Puerto Rico (MMAPA), and other leaders from Puerto Rico’s health care sector. The briefing also included participation from former Puerto Rico Governor Luis Fortuño, Eduardo Bhatia, former President of the Puerto Rico Senate, and Dr. Carlos R. Mellado López, former Secretary of the Puerto Rico Department of Health, and representatives from the Puerto Rico Federal Affairs Administration (PRFAA).

The session also included the participation of Representatives Héctor Ferrer, spokesperson for the Popular Democratic Party (PPD) in the Puerto Rico House of Representatives; Domingo Torres García of District 25 and alternate spokesperson for the PPD; Sol Higgins Cuadrado of District 35 and a member of the House Health Committee; and Estrella Martínez Soto of District 27.

Panelists briefed congressional staff on what is at stake ahead of the 2027 Medicaid funding cliff, including the potential impact on patients and providers and the information Congress will need to evaluate a legislative solution.

“We are prioritizing the basics: health care. Congress needs to understand that access to health care for more than one million Puerto Ricans is at stake. That is why we brought together experts, providers, and representatives from Puerto Rico’s health care sector with congressional staff from both parties,” said Hernández.

Current Medicaid funding supports a significant portion of Plan Vital, which provides health coverage to approximately 1.2 million people in Puerto Rico. The current funding provisions, including a 76 percent federal matching rate, expire on September 30, 2027. Without further congressional action, annual federal funding could fall from approximately $3.8 billion to roughly $500 million, while the federal matching rate would return to 55 percent.

The potential consequences of such a reduction have been documented by multiple stakeholders. An analysis by Espacios Abiertos estimates that between 700,000 and one million people could lose Plan Vital coverage if current funding is not reauthorized, while representatives of Puerto Rico’s hospital sector have warned that a reduction of this magnitude could significantly affect the health care system’s ability to provide services.

The challenge extends beyond preventing a funding reduction. Any proposal brought before Congress will need to be supported by reliable data on expenditures, enrollment, the needs of Puerto Rico’s health care system, and future projections. Hernández continues working with colleagues on legislation to address the 2027 funding cliff while gathering the information necessary to support that effort.

Inaction could also have consequences beyond Puerto Rico. MACPAC has previously noted that insufficient Medicaid funding in Puerto Rico could increase federal Medicaid spending if eligible beneficiaries move to the states, where Medicaid is not subject to the same federal funding cap that applies to Puerto Rico.
title: Comisionado Residente prioriza gestiones en el Congreso para evitar precipicio de Medicaid en Puerto Rico
