Washington, D.C. — U.S. Representative Sean Casten (IL-06) and Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) introduced the Environmental Health Restoration Act, legislation to restore and strengthen the Environmental Protection Agency’s core mission to protect public health, the environment, and the climate.

The lawmakers introduced the bill just days after the Trump Administration’s EPA finalized the repeal of major greenhouse gas standards for coal- and gas-fired power plants and moved to eliminate remaining federal climate pollution requirements for the power sector.

“At a time when the Trump Administration is ignoring the climate crisis and undermining Americans’ ability to breathe clean air, drink clean water, and enjoy the outdoors, it is more important than ever to restore a commitment to science-based environmental protection at the EPA,” said Rep. Casten. “The EPA was created to protect public health and our environment. I’m proud to introduce this legislation to refocus the agency on its core mission.”

“The Trump EPA has fully abandoned its decades-long duty to protect Americans’ health and safety. Its relentless attacks on science have delivered for big political donors while poisoning our air and water and speeding up the climate crisis,” said Sen. Whitehouse. “Our bill would jumpstart the long process of restoring the science, the scientists, and the original mission guiding the EPA.”

On Wednesday, September 16th, Rep. Casten and Sen. Whitehouse hosted a press conference with Protect Our Winters and Olympic athletes to highlight the bill's importance and the need to protect the great outdoors.

“As an Olympian training in the mountains all over the world, I’ve seen less and less snow, glaciers shrinking at a not-so-glacial pace, and volatile air quality,” said Tommy Ford, three-time Olympian and World Cup Champion. “This directly affects our community’s health and economy. A stronger, more durable EPA is essential for clean air, clean water and a strong, healthy community.”

“Rolling back environmental protections has real consequences for the places and experiences that define the outdoor community,” said Ben Gubits, Vice President of Campaigns at POW. “It means dirtier air, greater climate pollution, more threats to public health and accelerating damage to our winters, waterways and public lands. The Environmental Health Restoration Act draws a clear line, the EPA must follow science, enforce the law and put people ahead of polluters. This is a positive vision for the future looking well beyond the Trump years.”

The Environmental Health Restoration Act responds to recent deregulatory actions that have weakened or delayed protections governing air pollution, water quality, greenhouse gas emissions and environmental enforcement. It would reaffirm Congress’s intent that the EPA follow science, regulate harmful pollution, and protect communities from environmental harm.

The Environmental Health Restoration Act would:

Restore key protections for pollution from power plants, vehicles, and oil and gas operations that were in effect on January 19, 2025.

Require EPA decisions to be grounded in peer-reviewed science and restore independent scientific advisory bodies.

Rebuild the agency’s civil and criminal enforcement capacity and require annual accountability reporting to Congress.

Prioritize monitoring and enforcement in communities facing disproportionate pollution burdens.

Require public-health and cumulative-impact analyses for EPA actions affecting air and water quality.

Preserve states’ ability to adopt environmental standards stronger than federal requirements.

Allow people harmed by the EPA’s failure to comply with the law to seek relief in federal court.

The legislation is endorsed by Protect Our Winters and the League of Conservation Voters.

Transcript of Rep. André Carson's Opening Statement from Hearing on Import Controls: Tools to Counter the CCP's Industrial Policy and Supply Chain Threats
WASHINGTON – Today, the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party held a hearing titled Import Controls: Tools to Counter the CCP's Industrial Policy and Supply Chain Threats. The hearing examined U.S. market restriction and import control policies, examples of how those policies have been used, and how they can be paired with industrial policy to strengthen U.S. manufacturing.
The following witnesses provided testimony:
- Mr. Peter Harrell, Visiting Scholar, Georgetown University Institute of International Economic Law; Senior Fellow, Council on Foreign Relations
- Mr. Craig Singleton, China Program Senior Director, Foundation for Defense of Democracies
- Mr. Oren Cass, Founder and Chief Economist, American Compass
Below is a transcript of the opening statement from Representative André Carson.
Mr. Chairman, thank you, and thank you to our witnesses for being here today.
For years, this Committee has led the debate on how to use market access policies to safeguard national security and counter the Chinese Communist Party’s dominance across critical sectors like telecommunications, drones, autos, robotics, solar, shipbuilding, batteries, and critical minerals.
These are powerful tools when used correctly. But today I want to press on a question I don't think we ask often enough: when we restrict a Chinese product or company from the U.S. market, how do we ensure American industry and workers can fill the gap?
Market restrictions on their own do not create an industry. If we restrict Chinese cranes, drones, or connected vehicles and nothing is standing behind that restriction to support American innovation, workers, and manufacturing, all we will have done is just changed our supplier—swapped Chinese firms for whichever foreign competitor is fastest to move into the gap we opened.
Take ZPMC cranes. When the Biden Administration restricted Chinese-manufactured port cranes on national security grounds, it paired that restriction with real investment in domestic crane manufacturing. That should be the model.
The goal cannot simply be "not China." It has to be building durable American and allied capacity in the sectors that matter most to our economic and national security. That means focusing on a suite of policies I like to call “economic patriotism.”
It includes smart policies like procurement preferences that give scale to firms making the leap; tax credits that de-risk capital; federal R&D that gets technology out of the lab; and maybe most importantly workforce investments that produce the welders, machinists, and engineers to actually run these plants.
I also want to make clear that restricting access to the world's largest consumer market has real consequences for businesses trying to plan, for workers whose jobs depend on supply chains we're reshaping, and for consumers who might pay the price of scarcity before American capacity catches up. This policy toolkit has real tradeoffs and should be used sparingly to address the greatest threats to the U.S., not settle political spats.
Additionally, Congress needs visibility into how these authorities are actually being used as a matter of course. That means reporting requirements with clear, public criteria for how designations get made and regular reviews of whether a restriction is actually achieving the security and economic goals it was built for.
I'll close with this. These tools — restrictions, tariffs, export controls — are not meant to be used to settle personal feuds between heads of state or as leverage in some unrelated negotiation. When they are, it doesn't just look bad. It actually undermines the credibility and effectiveness of the tools themselves, here and with our allies who we need standing beside us on this. Used well, market restrictions are one piece of a serious industrial strategy. Used carelessly, or for the wrong reasons, they're just noise that costs American businesses and workers real money.
I look forward to hearing from our witnesses on how we get this balance right. Thank you, and I yield back.

(Washington, DC) — Today, the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology is holding an Investigations and Oversight Subcommittee hearing titled, Balancing Biotechnology Innovation and Biosecurity: Securing U.S. Leadership in a Global Race.

Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren's (D-CA) opening statement as prepared for the record is below:

Good morning. Thank you to Chairman McCormick and Ranking Member Sykes for this hearing. Thank you to our witnesses for appearing today.

I want to start, Mr. Chairman, by asking unanimous consent to enter into the record a letter from the American Society for Microbiology, one of our country’s oldest and most respected scientific societies. I agree wholeheartedly with Ranking Member Sykes that the voices of the scientific community need to be heard in this discussion, and ASM has a valuable perspective on these issues.

One of the things that they point out in their letter is that the McKinsey Global Institute has estimated that as much as 60% of the physical imports to the global economy could in principle be produced biologically. That is a stunning possibility, and I see that one of our witnesses is connected with Dr. Endy. Visiting Dr. Endy's lab at Stanford – it is mind-blowing to see what the possibilities are.

This Committee has long and really impressive legacy of bipartisanship and oversight for biotechnology and biosecurity. Our bipartisan CHIPS and Science Act had several provisions tasking our agencies to support research on the safety and security implications of engineering biology. In this Congress, we approved H.R. 3029, a bill to support nucleic acid screening research at NIST. This bill has since passed the full House and I urge our counterparts in the Senate to take it up. We are also looking closely at the legislative ideas catalyzed by our colleagues from the National Security Commission on Emerging Biotechnology.

For years, this Committee has maintained a deep understanding of, and respect for, the spirit of openness that animates life science research. Republicans and Democrats alike have taken biosecurity and safety seriously, while understanding that to be the world leader in biotechnology, we must be tactful of how we legislate and perform oversight on biosecurity. Unfortunately, the term “strategic” does not adequately define the actions of the Trump Administration and how it has approached these issues. Ranking Member Sykes talked at length about many of these concerns. I will focus instead on what is at stake for us to lose.

One of the things I want to talk about, Mr. Hodges, is your work with Dr. Endy at the Hoover Institution. Dr. Endy was part of the research community that contributed to the development of one of the very first synthetic cells created entirely from scratch – a remarkable achievement for American life science. And when I texted him congratulations, he did text back saying, "We beat China."

So that was a good step forward.Dr. Endy importantly recognizes that the U.S. cannot, as he says, “ride the breaks” on biotechnology innovation and expect to remain a world leader. I remember touring the lab. There is a little sign that one of the scientists made that says, "The Wright brothers didn't need a license."

We have to keep that in mind if we are going to be successful. That doesn't mean that we don't take security seriously. We do, but we have to make sure that we don't stifle innovation in a way that is not strategic.

I just want to say a final thing on a concern that I have that's not really in the purview entirely of this Committee. And that's the fact that for years, we in the United States have benefitted from the fact that 80% of foreign-born STEM researchers have wanted to stay in the United States and become Americans with us. For a variety of reasons, hostility towards immigrants, lack of visa availability, the number of people coming from other countries to get their PhDs in STEM has dropped. And the number who want to stay after has also dropped precipitously. That is bad news for our country. A little under 50% of American Nobel Prize winners were Americans who are here by choice. Americans born in another country who decided to become one of us. Losing that will harm us and it will not only harm the research done here, but also our international partnerships and our dialogue and transparency.

So with that, Mr. Chairman, I yield back. Thank you for this hearing on this important topic.
title: Ranking Member Lofgren's Opening Statement at Hearing on Biotechnology Innovation and Biosecurity

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Representatives Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Stephanie Bice (OK-05), Hank Johnson (GA-04) and Lauren Boebert (CO-04) introduced the bipartisan, bicameralRenewing the Dream Actto authorize the National Parks Service to install a new plaque near the steps of the Lincoln Memorial marking where Civil Rights Movement leader Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his famed “I Have a Dream”speech.

“Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s moral clarity, rousing oratory and strategic nonviolent organizing propelled the Civil Rights Movement to the forefront of American consciousness,”said Rep. Raskin.“Our legislation honors the life and legacy of this Civil Rights Movement hero and his vision for a ‘Beloved Community’ by updating the dated, worn plaque marking where he delivered one of his greatest speeches. I’m grateful to this bipartisan group of my colleagues who are joining together to make sure Dr. King’s work and that moment is never forgotten.”

Bice. “I’m proud to co-lead a bipartisan legislation which will replace the weathered plaque at the Lincoln Memorial, assuring that every American who visits can easily recognize this historical location for generations to come.”

“The plaque commemorating the very spot where Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his iconic ‘I Have a Dream’ speech is in need of renewal, just as his dream is in need of renewal today,”said Rep. Johnson. “Dr. King dreamed that one day this nation would rise up and live out the true meaning of its creed: that all people are created equal. That dream remains as powerful and as necessary today as it was when he delivered those iconic words 63 years ago. I’m pleased to join Ranking Member Raskin and our bipartisan coalition to restore this historic marker and reaffirm the enduring power of Dr. King’s dream.”

"For over a decade, I have had a dream that one day the now deteriorated and inconspicuous stone upon which Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. stood at the Lincoln Memorial to share his ‘Dreams,’ would one day be restored to the dignity it deserves,”said Daryl Davis, Cofounder of the Prohuman Foundation. “We at the Prohuman Foundation are grateful for the blessing of the King family and thrilled with the support of Representatives Jamie Raskin, Hank Johnson, Stephanie Bice and Lauren Boebert who are championing our mission of Renewing The Dream. Every American will be proud to stand in the very spot where Dr. King stood 63 years ago this year, share his Dream and help turn it into a reality."

The Renewing the Dream Act authorizes the National Parks Service to install a new plaque near the steps of the Lincoln Memorial to honor Dr. King.Congress first authorized the plaque in October 2000. Since it was unveiled on August 22, 2003, constant exposure to the elements and countless footsteps have made the plaque nearly unreadable, as is evident in the picture below.

The new plaque includes a more durable and beautiful design, as seen below, and is completely funded by private donations.

Dr. King’s“I Have a Dream” speech was delivered during the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom on August 28, 1963. The march was part of a series of peaceful protests advocating for the civil rights and liberties of Black Americans.

Representatives Andy Barr (KY-06) and Lucy McBath (GA-06) are original cosponsors of this legislation.

WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Representative Marie Gluesenkamp Perez reaffirmed her commitment to the Ukrainian community in Southwest Washington by voting for a comprehensive package of sanctions targeting Russia and anyone who facilitates sanctions evasion. The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 is a critical effort to cripple funding for Russia’s War in Ukraine by penalizing countries that buy Russian oil. The bill was voted on in the Senate earlier this year, where it passed 86-11. The bill went on to pass in the House 262-159.

This package includes a number of sanctions, specifically it would:

Imposes blocking and entry (visa) sanctions on specified Russian officials, including Vladimir Putin and senior political and military leaders, oligarchs who haven’t opposed the war or continue to benefit from ties with the Russian government, executives/controlling owners of major Russian energy projects, foreign companies supporting Russia’s defense industrial base or military, and persons engaged in corruption, money laundering, or sanctions evasion for the Russian government.

Imposes sanctions on Russia’s “shadow fleet,” a network of vessels and supporting entities used to transport Russian oil and other goods while concealing ownership or transactions to circumvent sanctions.

Imposes sanctions on the Central Bank of Russia, Sberbank, VTB Bank, Gazprombank, and other covered Russian financial institutions. Foreign financial institutions engaging in significant transactions with sanctioned Russian institutions shall also be sanctioned.

Imposes sanctions on entities in which the Russian government holds a controlling/majority interest or that are otherwise government-affiliated, and restricts U.S. financial institutions from processing specified transactions involving the Russian government, government-owned entities, or Russian officials.

Restricts certain Russian securities from U.S. exchanges; prohibits new U.S. investment in Russia and its energy sector and transfer of U.S.-produced energy or energy products; prohibits purchases of Russian sovereign debt; authorizes restrictions on certain services to Russia; and sanctions certain financial-messaging providers used to circumvent sanctions.

Directs implementation of existing restrictions on Russian uranium imports under 42 U.S.C. §2297h-10a(d), including covered uranium associated with Rosatom or its subsidiaries or successors, and requires sanctions against specified officials and shareholders.

Extends the deadline of the 1996 Iran Sanctions Act from 2026 to 2031.

In addition to steep sanctions the bill would introduce aggressive secondary measures, including up to 500% duties on Russian goods and up to 100% duties on third-party countries that purchase Russian oil/gas or facilitate sanctions evasion.

“I’m proud to represent one of the largest Ukrainian communities in America–people who have lost fathers, mothers, sons and daughters in the fight to defeat fascism.,” said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez, “I urge the President to move quickly to implement these critical sanctions to ensure that Putin and his people know there is a steep price for their continued disregard for the sanctity of life.”

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez has continuously worked to support Ukraine in its fight to end the Russian invasion and to support Ukrainian refugees displaced by the conflict. In 2024, she voted to pass HR 813, allocating over $60 billion in funding for Ukrainian defense. More recently in the FY27 Defense Appropriations markup, she spoke in support of the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative, a provision to strengthen domestic manufacturing capability to support Ukrainian defense. Additionally, Rep Gluesenkamp Perez supports Ukrainians living in Southwest Washington through her casework channels, helping constituents facing issues with federal agencies. To get in touch or learn about how her office can help with federal agencies, please visit her casework page or Ukrainian Language casework page.

####
title: Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez Votes to Support Ukrainian Defense and Sanction Russia

(Washington, D.C.) – Today, the Quindaro Townsite National Historic Landmark Act, introduced by U.S. Representatives Emanuel Cleaver, II (D-MO), Sharice Davids (D-KS), and Derek Schmidt (R-KS), received a hearing in the House Committee on Natural Resources. The bipartisan legislation would designate the Quindaro Townsite in Kansas City, Kansas, as a National Historic Landmark. The site served as a critical entry point for anti-slavery settlers and a sanctuary for those escaping bondage via the Underground Railroad prior to and during the U.S. Civil War.

“The history of the Quindaro Townsite is an important piece of the story of Kansas City that must be told for generations to come,” said Congressman Cleaver. “I’m pleased that our bipartisan legislation to designate Quindaro as a National Historic Landmark was heard in the Natural Resources Committee, and following this important step in the legislative process, I look forward to continuing our push to ensure it becomes law.”

“Quindaro holds an important place in the history of Kansas and our nation. Founded during the turbulent days of Bleeding Kansas, it became a place of hope and refuge for those fighting for freedom and seeking a better future. This hearing is an important step toward ensuring Quindaro’s legacy is properly preserved and recognized for generations to come. I’m proud to lead this bipartisan effort with Representatives Cleaver and Davids, and I look forward to working with the committee to advance this legislation,” Rep. Schmidt said.

"This national landmark designation for Quindaro is long overdue. From its role on the Underground Railroad to its deep roots with the Wyandot Nation, Quindaro represents a crucial chapter of the Kansas City story. Today’s hearing gets our bill one step closer to cutting through administrative delays and making sure this history is preserved for our kids and grandkids," said Rep. Sharice Davids.

National Historic Landmarks are designated through the National Park Service System Advisory Board or an official act of Congress. Last May, the National Historic Landmarks Committee unanimously recommended Quindaro Townsite for designation as a National Historic Landmark, however the administrative process has since stalled. This bill would bypass the administrative process and designate the site by congressional action.

Representatives Cleaver and Davids submitted a letter to the House Committee on Natural Resources in support of the bipartisan legislation. The official letter is available here.

Official text of the Quindaro Townsite National Historic Landmark Act is available here.

Emanuel Cleaver, II is the U.S. Representative for Missouri's Fifth Congressional District, which includes Kansas City, Independence, Lee's Summit, Raytown, Grandview, Sugar Creek, Greenwood, Blue Springs, North Kansas City, Gladstone, and Claycomo. He is a member of the exclusive House Financial Services Committee and Ranking Member of the House Subcommittee on Housing and Insurance.
title: Quindaro Townsite National Historic Landmark Act Receives Hearing in Natural Resources Committee

CANTON, OH — Today, U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) announced that the Akron-Canton Regional Airport Authority will receive $175,000 in federal funding through the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) FY26 Airport Improvement Program.

The grant will fund the acquisition of 35 new vehicle movement area transponders, bringing the airport into conformity with current federal safety standards. Vehicle movement area transponders track ground vehicles operating on runways, taxiways, and other restricted airfield surfaces, giving air traffic controllers real-time visibility into airfield activity and reducing the risk of runway incursions.

The funding comes through the FAA's Airport Improvement Program, which provides federal grants to public-use airports for projects related to safety, capacity, and infrastructure. Akron-Canton Regional Airport serves as a key transportation and economic hub for Summit and Stark counties, supporting commercial passenger service, cargo operations, and general aviation.

“This federal investment in Akron-Canton Airport strengthens safety for everyone who works and travels through the airport. I'm proud to have helped secure this funding, and I'll keep working to bring resources home to Ohio's 13th District,” said Congresswoman Sykes. “Every dollar we bring home for projects like this one means a safer, stronger airport for the families and businesses that depend on it.”

“We are grateful to Congresswoman Sykes for her continued commitment to aviation and for helping secure this Airport Improvement Program grant,” said Ren Camacho, President and CEO of the Akron-Canton Airport. “This funding will allow CAK to equip our airfield vehicles with Vehicle Movement Area Transponders, adding another important layer of safety by improving visibility and situational awareness across the airfield.”

This announcement follows Congresswoman Sykes' ongoing efforts to secure federal infrastructure funding for Ohio's 13th District, including previous investments in transportation, aviation, and public safety projects across Summit, Stark, and Portage counties.
title: Rep. Sykes Announces $175,000 Grant for Akron Canton Regional Airport Authority

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Representatives Sharice Davids (D-KS-03) and Gabe Evans (R-CO-08) introduced bipartisan legislation to streamline and modernize how surviving spouses, children, and dependent parents apply for Social Security survivor benefits. The bill would help families avoid long phone hold times and unnecessary in-person visits during a period of intense emotional and financial strain.

"When a family loses a parent, spouse, or breadwinner, the last thing they should have to deal with is a maze of administrative red tape just to access the benefits their loved one earned through a lifetime of hard work," said Davids. "My casework team will always help Kansans recover backlogged federal benefits — including Social Security — but families shouldn’t have to turn to their representatives’ offices just to get the benefits they’ve earned. This bipartisan bill would make it easier for families to get those benefits on their own, without having to navigate unnecessary hurdles during an already difficult time."

“When families experience the loss of a loved one, the last thing they should have to deal with is red tape and complications when accessing the benefits they are owed,” said Representative Gabe Evans (R-CO-08). “I’m proud to co-lead the bipartisan Survivor Benefits Applications Modernization Act to ensure grieving families have faster access to the resources and services they need during difficult times.”

Under current Social Security Act provisions, when a person passes away, their surviving family members — including young children, surviving spouses caring for children, and dependent parents — are eligible for survivor insurance benefits. However, unlike other federal programs that offer streamlined digital services, the Social Security Administration (SSA) process for survivor benefits still largely relies on manual scheduling and paper-based applications. This leads to extended processing delays, crowded field offices, and unnecessary stress for families facing sudden loss.

The bipartisan Survivor Benefits Application Modernization Act would fix that problem by requiring the Social Security Administration to:

Establish an Online Self-Scheduling Portal: Within 180 days of enactment, the SSA Commissioner must launch an online system allowing applicants for survivor benefits to independently schedule appointments.

Develop Online Application Filing: Within one year of enactment, the SSA must enable beneficiaries to complete and submit their survivor benefits applications directly through the secure online portal.

Report on Efficiency and Integrity: Requires the SSA to submit a report to Congress within three years detailing application processing trends, administrative cost savings, and fraud and identity theft instances.

“New York Life supports the Survivor Benefits Application Modernization Act, which would enable grieving families to apply for Social Security survivor benefits online,” said Heather Nesle, Senior Vice President of Corporate Responsibility, New York Life. “As the nation’s largest corporate funder of childhood bereavement causes, the New York Life Foundation has long championed efforts that help grieving families access the support they need. We thank Representatives Davids and Evans for leading the effort to help more children access the financial support they are entitled to during an incredibly difficult time.”
title: Davids, Evans Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Streamline Social Security Survivor Benefits for Families

Disaster Loan Outreach Consistency Act would require SBA to provide consistent, current disaster loan information to small business owners

WASHINGTON, D.C. — The House Committee on Small Business today advanced legislation introduced by Representative Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) to strengthen federal disaster assistance for small businesses and ensure owners have accurate, up-to-date information when recovering from natural disasters. The legislation will advance to the House floor when scheduled for a vote.

Small businesses are increasingly on the front lines of natural disasters, facing flooding, severe storms, blizzards, and other events that can threaten their ability to stay open. The Disaster Loan Outreach Consistency Act would require the Small Business Administration (SBA) to establish standardized procedures to ensure disaster outreach materials are consistent, current, and accurate across its field operations centers—equipping businesses with the information to seek and receive aid in a timely manner.

“With nearly 99 percent of all businesses in my home state of New Jersey are small businesses and each one facing the threat of coastal storms and severe floods, these are over 1 million owners and potential borrowers who need all the relevant information. This is why my bill, the Disaster Loan Outreach Consistency Act, offers a simple solution and basic oversight to this issue,” said Congresswoman Mejia. “I urge my colleagues and members of this committee to support this legislation. In a period of time where misinformation is rampant, we must work to ensure small business owners have all the possible information they can have to make the best decision for themselves. We cannot let our federal agencies misguide, misdirect, and withhold vital information, especially when they make regulatory changes that affect Americans. The disaster loan program is one crucial step in recovery after a natural disaster.”

Small businesses make up nearly 99 percent of businesses in New Jersey, making access to reliable disaster assistance particularly important as communities across the state face increasingly severe storms and flooding.

The legislation would provide greater consistency and accountability across SBA’s disaster outreach efforts, helping ensure that the small business owners who rely on federal disaster loans receive the information they need to make informed decisions and recover more quickly.

WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Representative Kelly Morrison (MN-03) is joining her colleagues in calling on House Speaker Mike Johnson to cancel recess, keep Congress in session, and address the grave warnings from industry experts and leaders on the catastrophic risks posed by advanced AI.
In a letter to Speaker Johnson, Rep. Morrison joins more than 100 of her colleagues in calling for the Speaker to advance meaningful, bipartisan safeguards for advanced artificial intelligence.
The members point to recent disclosures involving rogue AI agents, biological misuse, cyberattacks, foreign surveillance and efforts by Chinese companies to replicate leading American AI systems.
“Reasonable minds may disagree about precisely how Congress should regulate this rapidly evolving technology. We cannot disagree about the imperative for Congress to act,” the lawmakers write.
The letter highlights several proposals that merit congressional consideration including legislation mandating transparency and evaluation of frontier models, “kill switch” requirements, and a waiver of antitrust laws to enable critical industry-wide collaboration on safety and security.
Republican House leadership recently canceled two weeks of session in September, and the members criticize that prolonged absence as AI researchers, companies and Americans increasingly demand congressional action.
The letter calls on the House to remain in Washington until Congress advances bipartisan AI safeguards.
Read the full letter here and below.
Dear Speaker Johnson:
We write to urge you to keep the House of Representatives in session to enable Congress to take urgent action to address the catastrophic risks posed by advanced artificial intelligence. Those risks take any of several forms, separately and in combination—of agentic misalignment, mass cybersecurity breaches, and development of biological or chemical weapons.
Reasonable minds may disagree about precisely how Congress should regulate this rapidly evolving technology. We cannot disagree about the imperative for Congress to act.
Instead of action, you have announced vacation. After a month-long August recess, the House leadership changed the schedule to announce two more weeks of vacation–immediately prior to yet another month of recess in October.
Ample evidence—in the form of a series of public disclosures from the companies and researchers developing the world's most capable AI systems—underscores the urgency of the moment:
- In July, OpenAI models undergoing cybersecurity evaluations bred swarms of agents that circumvented controls designed to isolate them from the internet, conspired to exploit vulnerabilities, hacked third party systems, and altered evidence of their activity, an incident that OpenAI has called a "warning shot," about the risks of highly capable rogue AI agents.
- Days later, more than 1,300 top employees of frontier AI companies called on the U.S. government to support an international effort to develop tools that can “deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development.”
- More recently, Anthropic disrupted cases in which researchers used Claude for biological research that could have aided the development of biological weapons, and called biological misuse “one of the most serious risks of frontier AI models.”
- Anthropic also documented China-linked actors using Claude for surveillance and transnational repression, and Iran-linked actors using it for propaganda, mass surveillance, and targeting recommendations against U.S. naval forces.
- Meanwhile, CISA reported Chinese open-weight models accelerating their capabilities through “industrial-scale” distillation of American models—giving rise to AI agents nearly as powerful as the top U.S. frontier models, yet wholly unconstrained by American authorities or by U.S. safeguards.
These disclosures must not constitute yet another in a long series of “warning shots,” but rather, a starting gun. Congress must act.
A series of proposals have emerged from our colleagues that deserve consideration, public debate, thoughtful amendment, and action. They include bills mandating transparency and evaluation of frontier models, “kill switch” requirements, and a waiver of antitrust laws to enable critical industry-wide collaboration on safety and security. Whether with these proposals or any other variants, AI experts and leading companies agree that the United States can lead the world in artificial intelligence while establishing reasonable safeguards that protect Americans and our national security. We can—and must—do both.
While AI safety experts and Americans increasingly urge action to confront this conflagration of risk, Congress fiddles. When we did return to work after the August recess, we consumed floor time with debates and votes on performative resolutions opposing socialism. After next week, the House resumes its vacation—for another six weeks.
You can forgive every American who believes that Congress remains unserious about confronting our nation’s most pressing challenges.
The House should remain in session until Congress advances meaningful, bipartisan AI safeguards. To our children who will have read a post-apocalyptic history, “Why Congress Slept” —likely written by agentic AI— our inaction will be inexplicable and unforgivable.
###
title: U.S. Rep Kelly Morrison Calls on Speaker Mike Johnson to Keep Congress in Session and Address AI Safety Warnings

WASHINGTON, DC — Today, U.S. Representative Sarah McBride (D-Del.) voted to pass the Water Resources Development Act (WRDA), which includes several Delaware priorities she advocated for during the development of the legislation. WRDA authorizes critical water resources infrastructure projects and studies through the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Civil Works Program, supporting flood and storm protection, ports and harbors, and inland waterway navigation across the country.

As the state with the lowest mean elevation in the country, Delaware faces significant risks from flooding, coastal storms, and shoreline erosion. WRDA is a critical tool for strengthening Delaware’s water infrastructure, protecting communities across the state, and preparing coastal communities in Sussex County and communities along the Delaware River for future flooding.

“Protecting Delaware from flooding and extreme weather starts with ensuring our water infrastructure is built to withstand the challenges of today and tomorrow,” said Rep. McBride. “I’m proud that the House version of the bill, which passed with bipartisan support, includes several priorities I fought to secure for Delaware — strengthening protections along the Delaware River, advancing flood mitigation in New Castle and along the Assawoman Canal, and increasing support for the Delaware River Basin. WRDA isn’t just an investment in our water infrastructure — it’s an investment in our economy, our communities, and the future of our state.”

Delaware priorities secured by Rep. McBride include:

Advancing flood and shoreline protection along the Delaware River by authorizing a study focused on flood risk management, shoreline damage prevention and mitigation, recreation, and ecosystem restoration;

Supporting flood mitigation in the City of New Castle by authorizing a flood-risk-management study;

Exploring additional flood protections for the Assawoman Canal through a newly authorized study; and

Strengthening support for water infrastructure across the Delaware River Basin by expanding an existing environmental infrastructure program to cover the entire Basin and increasing its authorization from $20 million to $92.69 million.

The bill now heads to the U.S. Senate.
title: Rep. McBride Secures Delaware Priorities in Water Resources Development Act

WASHINGTON, DC – Congresswoman Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09), a member of the House’s Water Resources Subcommittee, spoke on the floor of the House in favor of the bipartisan Water Resources Development Act (WRDA). The legislation includes over a dozen priorities Pou championed to help protect North Jersey from flooding and advance critical local water infrastructure projects. The legislation passed the House overwhelmingly, 415-to-9.

The passed legislation includes provisions that will help move long-delayed flood mitigation projects forward, launch new studies, and strengthen protections for communities across North Jersey that have endured repeated flooding.

The bill also incorporates Congresswoman Pou’s bipartisan CLEAN-UP Act, legislation she introduced earlier this year to remove barriers that have stalled environmental remediation projects.

“In our North Jersey communities, flooding is not some distant threat. In just the last few weeks, our communities have seen terrible flash floods turn streets into rivers, destroying homes, cars, and small businesses, and upending lives,” said Congresswoman Pou. “This bill takes action by moving long-delayed flood protection projects forward across Bergen and Passaic Counties. I am especially proud this package includes my bipartisan CLEAN-UP Act. We cannot keep waiting until after disaster strikes to act. We must be proactive and give our communities the tools to protect themselves before the next storm comes.”

Since taking office, Congresswoman Pou has made flood mitigation one of her key priorities in Congress.

Earlier this year, she introduced the CLEAN-UP Act to remove barriers delaying Army Corps projects and authored the Water Crisis Prevention Act to improve the federal response to infrastructure failures. During the Surface Transportation Reauthorization mark-up, Pou also secured an amendment into the bill that would direct the Government Accountability Office to review Department of Transportation PROTECT grants and produce a report identifying best practices and strategies to prevent flooding, improve safety, and strengthen infrastructure resilience.

Additionally, the annual spending bill for FY2026 included $500,000 in federal funds supported by Pou to improve the Lower Saddle River channel.

The House’s passage of the Water Resources Development Act builds on that record and represents another significant step toward delivering long-awaited relief for communities living with chronic flooding.

title: Pou-Backed Flood Protections Pass House

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswomen Alma S. Adams, Ph.D. (NC-12), and Ashley Hinson (IA-02), alongside Senators Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Cory Booker (D-NJ), and Chuck Grassley (R-IA) introduced the bipartisan, bicameral resolution recognizing September 19, 2026, as National Stillbirth Prevention and Awareness Day.

In acknowledgment of the work that needs to be done, and mark the progress made since theMaternal and Child Health Stillbirth Prevention Act passed into law, Congresswomen Adams and Hinson, held a briefing inside the Capitol Building today. Advocates, medical professionals, policy leaders, and parents came to discuss clinical innovations in stillbirth prevention and urge support for the National Stillbirth Prevention and Awareness Day resolution.

“It has already taken way too long for Congress to wake up to the tragedy that is our country's stillbirth crisis,” said Congresswoman Adams, co-founder and co-chair of the Black Maternal Health Caucus. “We have made some great progress, but there is so much more to be done. We already have many innovative solutions to reduce stillbirth — our country just hasn't invested in them at a national scale. We can, and we must do better for our moms.”

“Improving prenatal education and access to maternal care — especially in rural areas where women may travel over an hour to see a provider — is critical to protecting babies and reducing maternal deaths,” said Congresswoman Ashley Hinson. “Getting my Maternal and Child Health Stillbirth Prevention Act signed into law was a major step, but more must be done to support expecting moms and prevent stillbirths. I’m proud to reintroduce this resolution recognizing September 19th as National Stillbirth Prevention and Awareness Day and will continue working across the aisle to end the tragedy of stillbirth.”

“Nearly five thousand babies’ lives could be saved annually through greater focus on stillbirth prevention efforts,” said Healthy Birth Day CEO, Emily Price. “National Stillbirth Prevention & Awareness Day is an opportunity to address the urgent stillbirth crisis in the U.S. and share free resources and tools like Count the Kicks which are saving lives. Our message to the country: it doesn't have to be this way.”

The Maternal and Child Health Stillbirth Prevention Act, bipartisan legislationsigned into law in July 2024, clarified that Maternal and Child Health Services Block Grant funds could be used to support stillbirth prevention activities and research. This year, Congresswomen Adams and Hinson secured $1 million in a Fiscal Year 2027 appropriations bill for the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) to provide ongoing assistance to support states’ stillbirth prevention activities.

Medical advances over the last 30 years have led to a decline in late term stillbirths, but the rate of decline is slowing. Stillbirth remains a significant public health crisis in the United States, with tens of thousands of families affected each year and Black, Native, and Hispanic communities experiencing disproportionately higher rates. Research suggests a substantial share of stillbirths may be preventable through improved awareness, screening, and access to care.

“Every parent who experiences a stillbirth deserves support and clear action. Stillbirth remains a heartbreaking and preventable public health crisis, with Black, Native, and Hispanic families facing disproportionately high rates of loss,” said Senator Merkley.“Getting my Maternal and Child Health Stillbirth Prevention Act signed into law was an important first step, but we cannot let up. This National Stillbirth Prevention and Awareness Day, we must keep pushing for necessary action to save lives and spare families this devastating loss.”

“Every year, more than 20,000 families in the United States experience a stillbirth, and too many of these losses may be preventable,” said Senator Booker. “Losing a baby to stillbirth is devastating, and on National Stillbirth Prevention and Awareness Day, we stand with the families who have experienced this profound loss and recommit ourselves to preventing stillbirth wherever possible. By investing in research, improving data collection, raising awareness, and strengthening access to high-quality maternal health care, we can better understand the causes of stillbirth, reduce preventable losses, and support healthier pregnancies.”

“No family should have to endure the heartbreak of a stillbirth. While states like Iowa have made progress at reducing stillbirths, there’s still much more to be done to strengthen maternal healthcare, especially in rural areas, to help prevent these tragedies. Our bipartisan resolution raises awareness and promotes research to help target contributing factors and save babies’ lives,” said Senator Grassley.

National Stillbirth Prevention and Awareness Day serves as an opportunity to recognize affected families, highlight the work of advocacy organizations, and reinforce the need for sustained federal investment in stillbirth prevention efforts and maternal and child health research and services.
title: Congresswomen Adams and Hinson Hold Briefing, Introduce National Stillbirth Prevention and Awareness Day Resolution

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Reps. Kathy Castor (FL-14) and Gabe Evans (CO-08) celebrated the passage of their bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act, which protects American families and small businesses from the costs of energy and grid upgrades required for new hyperscale data centers.

The Ratepayer Protection Act requires state utility regulators to establish rules ensuring communities do not pay for the costs of building new power plants, transmission lines and other upgrades to serve data centers. Without proper safeguards, families and small businesses in communities where data center development occurs could see their electric bills skyrocket. The Ratepayer Protection Act ensures that wealthy Big Tech companies cover the full energy and infrastructure costs of new data center development and are held accountable for their promises.

“Floridians already are dealing with sky-high electric bills. They should not be forced to subsidize the enormous energy demands of the world’s richest corporations,” said Rep. Castor. “If Big Tech builds a massive AI data center, the Big Tech company—not hardworking families, farmers or small businesses—should pay for their power and grid upgrades. The bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act is an important first step that can help lower costs for our neighbors back home and empower states to set strict guardrails.”

“Hardworking families should not have to subsidize the energy demands of data centers. America needs the infrastructure to lead the world in AI and outcompete Communist China, but we cannot have that growth at the expense of hardworking families, farmers, seniors, and small businesses. My bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act ensures large data centers pay for the infrastructure they require while giving states the flexibility to determine what works best for their communities. I’m incredibly proud to lead the charge on this pivotal issue, ensure our ratepayers are protected, and keep American innovation moving forward,” said Rep. Evans.

Castor strongly opposes data center development in Hillsborough County due to high electric bills and environmental concerns and pressed the Hillsborough County Board of County Commissioners in a September 10, 2026 letter to “act decisively to protect Hillsborough County residents, resources and long-term sustainability.”

The Ratepayer Protection Act builds on Rep. Castor’s leadership on the Stopping Hikes in Electricity from large Load Demands (SHIELD) Act, which she introduced with Rep. Mike Levin (CA-49) in January.

WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congresswoman Hillary Scholten (D-MI-03), member of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and Vice Chair of the Water Resources and Environment Subcommittee, secured key policy victories and critical investments for West Michigan in the House passage of the Water Resources Development Act (WRDA) 2026.

“Investing in water infrastructure means investing in jobs, environmental resilience, and the economic health of our local communities,” said Congresswoman Scholten. “As Vice Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Water Resources and Environment, I know how important it is that we work across the aisle to address the water infrastructure needs our country is facing. I am proud of the work of this Committee in getting this critical legislation passed, and I look forward to working with my Senate colleagues to get it across the finish line.”

Congresswoman Scholten’s specific wins include:

$115 million in new environmental infrastructure authorizations between Kent, Ottawa, and Muskegon Counties, as well as the state of Michigan, for water and wastewater infrastructure, including stormwater management and surface water resource protection.

The expedited completion of the streambank erosion and shoreline protection project in Muskegon Heights.

Language to direct the Army Corps to assess the impact of data centers on water resources.

The necessary authorization for a watershed-based study for the Muskegon River.

Several Great Lakes priorities, including language to adjust wage rates for Soo Locks employees; reauthorize the Great Lakes Commission; provide status updates on the Great Lakes recreational boating study; and expand funding eligibility to control aquatic plants and invasive species.

Dredging reforms to require local coordination and safe disposal of contaminated materials.

The reauthorization of FEMA’s High Hazard Potential Dam Program, and for language to assess levee risk, after significant flooding in Michigan this year.

Huffman Demands Answers After Park Service Quietly Hires Contractors for Trump Golf Course
Contracts were found buried in a federal procurement database days before Congress leaves town; one construction contract worth up to $49 million is forecast for January 2027
Washington, D.C. – Today, House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.) revealed during a committee hearing that the National Park Service awarded contracts on Sept. 10, with no notice to Congress, to begin work on Donald Trump’s planned takeover of the East Potomac Golf Course.
“Democrats on this committee just learned that a couple of days ago, the Park Service hired a company to start working on the historic public golf course at East Potomac Park without any announcement, without a word to any of us, without a single public hearing,” said Ranking Member Huffman. “Now, this is not just any old golf course. This is a beloved public space with huge historic significance. […] Donald Trump is systematically moving to take this historic, publicly accessible resource and turn it into another gilded private golf club for the mega-rich. That’s what’s going on here, folks. This is a methodical, deliberate effort to take a public park away from the people. Taxpayers are going to foot the bill to rebuild this golf course to Donald Trump’s specifications. He might even sell it to himself, or just gift it to himself as a trophy, as another tribute to himself on his way out the door of the White House.” 
“Congress leaves town today, and I don’t think it’s any coincidence that this is the exact moment the administration has chosen to line up contracts, setting the stage to roll equipment into the park and start tearing up public land for a Trump golf course,” said Ranking Member Huffman. “Democrats on this committee are tracking all of this. We’re going to keep dragging it all into the daylight until the public gets the answers we deserve. We’re not going to let Donald Trump walk off with our public lands. That park belongs to the American people, and I’m not willing to sit here and watch him simply steal it.”
The $389,355 award to Vanasse Hangen Brustlin, Inc. covers environmental and historic preservation compliance work at the course. The Park Service has since posted a forecasted construction contract worth up to $49 million, with a projected solicitation date of Jan. 31, 2027. Together the contracts commit at least $50 million in federal funds, lined up the same week Congress leaves Washington. 
The contracts follow months of activity at the park. Recent reports confirm the administration has reached an agreement with Fazio Design and undisclosed private and public partners to begin major construction, and the President has said his goal is to turn the public course into a major championship or Ryder Cup venue. Crews have already cut down more than sixty trees while a court is still deciding whether the project is lawful.
In light of this information, Ranking Member Huffman, Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.), Rep. Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-D.C.), Rep. Don Beyer (D-Va.), and Rep. Glenn Ivey (D-Md.) also sent a letter to Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and Acting National Park Service Director Jessica Bowron demanding every document, communication, and record on the project.
“East Potomac Park does not belong to Donald Trump,” the lawmakers wrote. “It belongs to the American people, and it has for more than a century.”
The letter also questions the timing of a separate seawall project. The Department left the East Potomac Park seawall crumbling for a decade, then opened procurement for repairs in August 2026 and expanded the funding documents for the Tidal Basin and West Potomac Park to cover additional stretches of the seawall. “But the question is why a project the Department never prioritized has suddenly become urgent at the precise moment separate contracts for Donald Trump’s makeover are going out,” the lawmakers wrote.
“Executed in small pieces, the President’s plans for the course appear designed to evade accountability at the expense of the American taxpayer,” the lawmakers wrote. “We refuse to let this grotesque desecration of public land and waste of American tax-dollars go unaccounted.”
The lawmakers requested all documents and communications since Jan. 20, 2025, on plans, cost estimates and funding sources for the golf course; the forecasted construction contract; the seawall project and its cost estimates; the tree removal; environmental and historic preservation compliance; and any proposed transfer of any part of East Potomac Park to the Trump Organization, Trump Golf Management or any Trump-affiliated entity. They also asked for all communications between the Department or the Park Service and Fazio Golf Designers, Meredith O’Rourke and Abby Matthis of Forward Strategies, the National Garden of American Heroes Foundation, the White House, the Trump Organization, Trump Golf Management and any member of the President’s family.

Today, U.S. Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02)’s Water Resources Development Act of 2026 (WRDA 2026) passed the House of Representatives by a vote of 415 to 9. The bipartisan, biennial bill protects Northwest Washington’s environment, supports Columbia River Treaty negotiations and authorizes critical investments in Northwest Washington ports, inland waterways, flood management systems and other water resources infrastructure.

“Today’s House passage of the Water Resources Development Act of 2026 is great news for ports, harbors and inland waterways in the Pacific Northwest and across the country,” said Rep. Larsen, who is the top Democrat on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee. “From expanding funding opportunities to restore ecosystems on Spencer Island to authorizing a study to mitigate Nooksack River flooding, WRDA 2026 continues bipartisan efforts to improve water resources infrastructure, create good-paying jobs and protect communities from natural disasters. I look forward to working with the Senate to pass a final WRDA 2026 into law.”

Since 2014, Congress has enacted a water resources development bill every two years to help improve the nation’s ports and harbors, inland waterway navigation system, flood and storm risk management, aquatic ecosystems and other aspects of water resources infrastructure. WRDA 2024 passed with overwhelming bipartisan support and included many of Rep. Larsen’s local priorities, including funding environmental infrastructure assistance to Western Washington state communities and expanding the Tribal Partnership Program (TPP) to make it easier for the Army Corps of Engineers to partner with Northwest Tribes on projects.

Washington State Wins in WRDA 2026

WRDA 2026 invests in Washington state priorities, including restoring the Puget Sound, addressing Nooksack River flooding and ensuring that critical Corps projects across the state can continue.

Wins for Washington in WRDA 2026 include:

Nooksack River Flooding: Authorizes a new feasibility study for flood risk reduction in the Nooksack River, which Whatcom County can use for long-term planning to address flooding concerns. Rep. Larsen has been working with local leaders to develop a plan to address Nooksack River flooding. Earlier this year, he advocated for Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) disaster relief funds to help communities recover from December 2025’s devastating floods, and he has championed FEMA flood mitigation grant funding so that local communities can prepare for future floods.

Disaster Debris Removal: Reforms how the Corps writes emergency debris removal contracts after floods to minimize harmful impacts to property and wildlife, and directs the Secretary of the Corps to ensure protection of healthy vegetation, important habitats, and vulnerable wildlife when setting standard contract terms. This provision will protect local ecosystems while cleaning flood debris in the Skagit River and other local rivers from December 2025’s floods.

Puget Sound and Adjacent Waters (PSAW): Increases the per project funding cap to $20 million, ensuring projects like Spencer Island restoration in Snohomish County continue to move forward. In 2018, Rep. Larsen successfully included an amendment in WRDA 2018 to increase the per project cap for PSAW to $10 million.

Puget Sound Nearshore Ecosystem Restoration Project (PSNERP): Allows the Corps to cost-share the relocation of related infrastructure for PNSERP projects at Lilliwaup Estuary, Tahuya Estuary, Snow Creek and Salmon Creek and Nooksack Estuary. Rep. Larsen previously worked to authorize $451 million for PSNERP in WRDA 2016. The Puget Sound is the largest estuary by water volume in the United States. Rep. Larsen's bipartisan legislation to reauthorize the National Estuary Program through 2031 and protect estuaries around the country passed the House last December.

Columbia River Treaty: Extends temporary authority for the United States to pay for pre-planned storage of water in Canada while United States and Canada continue to negotiate a new Columbia River Treaty. The United States’ current authority expires in 2027. The hydropower that the Columbia River Treaty provides benefits towns and cities across Northwest Washington, and Rep. Larsen has advocated for the Columbia River Treaty’s renewal for over a decade. Rep. Larsen supports efforts to negotiate a modern Columbia River treaty that manages flood risks and ensures a reliable clean energy supply, and he is working with local stakeholders to gather input ahead of negotiations.

Preventing Invasive Aquatic Species: Clarifies that indirect costs incurred by non-federal partners remain eligible for credit or reimbursement under the Corps’ Watercraft Inspection authority, which funds state efforts to prevent the spread of invasive aquatic species. Invasive golden, quagga and zebra mussels continue to expand their footprint in the Pacific Northwest. Early detection monitoring, watercraft inspection and decontamination and eradication efforts are critical to preventing further spread.

Lower Columbia River Channel Maintenance: Clarifies that the cost of constructing a dredged material disposal facility for operation and maintenance of the Lower Willamette and Lower Columbia River is a federal responsibility that can be drawn from the Harbor Maintenance Trust Fund (HMTF). These facilities are necessary for dredging operations to maintain the Columbia River waterway, which moves over $31 billion in cargo annually and supports 40,000 local jobs.

Lower Columbia River Turning Basin: Authorizes the Chief’s Report for Lower Columbia Turning Basin improvements. Traffic has continued to grow in the Lower Columbia River, with an increase in larger vessels that need room to safely turn and park. These improvements will allow for the better positioning of vessels, increase opportunities to use nearby tug service and improve efficient movement of vessels transporting goods.

HMTF Allocations for Donor and Energy Transfer Ports: Removes discretion for the Administration to ensure it fully utilizes a provision in WRDA 2020 requiring specific funding allocations from the Harbor Maintenance Trust Fund to donor and energy transfer ports. The Ports of Seattle and Tacoma are donor ports.

Office of Technical Assistance and Community Outreach: Creates an Office of Technical Assistance and Community Outreach within the Corps to help communities that may have difficulty navigating the Corps’ planning and construction processes. This office will serve as a one-stop-shop for directing communities to existing programs that assist with affordability concerns, address unique needs, and provide support for any stage of a Corps project.

Corps Study Process: Requires the Corps and the non-federal sponsor to establish an agreed-to timeframe (with milestones) for studies, and to allow the non-federal sponsor to request time extensions based on project complexity and sponsor’s goals.

Washington, D.C. — Colorado Congressman Joe Neguse introduced the Town Halls for All Act, a bill to ensure Members of Congress are staying connected to the communities they serve. Neguse himself has made hosting in-person, public town halls a priority for his office since first being elected to represent Colorado’s 2nd District in Congress. During his time in public office he’s hosted over 100 public town halls, 28 of which have fallen within the current legislature — a grand total that surpasses every member of Colorado’s congressional delegation combined.

As fewer elected officials from both sides of the aisle hold in-person town halls — opting for virtual gatherings or avoiding community conversations altogether — Neguse’s legislation would require all Members of both the House and Senate to hold at least 12 public town halls within their congressional district every calendar year. The bill also provides admittance, accessibility, and awareness guidelines to ensure that every individual interested in attending one of these meetings has the opportunity to do so.

“When you represent one of the largest congressional districts in the country — bigger than eight states and spanning 12,000 square miles — you understand how vital it is to spend time meeting directly with your constituents. That’s why I’ve hosted over 100 town-halls since first being elected, in rural, suburban and urban towns and communities across Western and Northern Colorado — to better understand their concerns, their hopes, and their dreams. It is time for all public officials to do the same, which is why I’ve introduced the Town Halls for All Act, which creates a gold standard for constituent access, and requires all Representatives and Senators to host at least 12 public town halls a year and ensures that the public officials Americans elected are responsive to the needs of their constituents,” said Congressman Joe Neguse.

Click HERE to read the bill text.

The bill is endorsed by Indivisible, an organization working to connect Americans with opportunities to attend town hall meetings in congressional districts across the country.

“In a democracy that works, elected officials should be accountable to the people they represent — and that means showing up, listening to constituents, and answering for their actions. Town halls are a crucial way for voters to engage directly with the people elected to serve them, and the Town Halls for All Act would make that kind of direct accountability the norm, not the exception,” said Andrew O’Neill, National Advocacy Director of Indivisible.

Background

At 42-years-old, Congressman Joe Neguse is the youngest Democrat in his state’s federal delegation, and as such he’s been working to rally a coalition of next-generation lawmakers in an effort to put power back in the hands of the American people. In addition to the newly introduced Town Halls for All Act, his efforts include introducing a measure to overturn the disastrous Citizens Uniteddecision, preventing unrestrained spending and dark money in elections; championing multiple proposals to ban Members of Congress from trading stocks, including co-leading the bipartisan consensus Restore Trust in Congress Act; and spearheading the End Corruption Now legislative agenda, seven bills that effectively stop the selling of access and influence in our nation’s capital.

###
title: Rep. Neguse Introduces Bill Mandating All Representatives & Senators Hold Monthly, Public Town Halls

Washington – Rep. Mike Thompson (CA-04) joined 106 colleagues in calling on Speaker Johnson to reconvene the House of Representatives to address the risks posed by advanced artificial intelligence (AI). A series of whistleblowers working in the AI industry have raised concerns in recent weeks that without new guardrails, rapidly developing AI technology could cause job losses, mass cybersecurity breaches, the development of biological or chemical weapons, and other threats. Some experts have even warned that superintelligent AI could defy human instructions.

Public disclosures from the companies and researchers developing the world’s most capable AI systems underscore the need to act. In July, over 1,300 top employees of the leading AI companies called on the U.S. government to act by supporting an international effort to develop tools that can slow down AI development. Since then, a series of proposals have emerged from members of Congress on both sides of the aisle that would provide the transparency and evaluation that is desperately needed. Despite this, Speaker Johnson and House Republican leadership have yet to bring any of these proposals to the floor for a vote and intend to send lawmakers home for a 6-week break at the end of this week.

"Reasonable minds may disagree about precisely how Congress should regulate this rapidly evolving technology. We cannot disagree about the imperative for Congress to act," wrote the lawmakers. "AI experts and leading companies agree that the United States can lead the world in artificial intelligence while establishing reasonable safeguards that protect Americans and our national security. We can—and must—do both."

"The House should return to Washington immediately and remain in session until Congress advances meaningful, bipartisan AI safeguards.” continued the lawmakers.

The full text of the letter can be found HERE and below.

The Honorable Mike Johnson Speaker

U.S. House of Representatives

H-232, The Capitol Washington D.C. 20515

Dear Speaker Johnson: We write to urge you to immediately reconvene the House of Representatives to enable Congress to take urgent action to address catastrophic risk posed by advanced artificial intelligence. Those risks take any of several forms, separately and in combination—of agentic misalignment, mass cybersecurity breaches, and development of biological or chemical weapons.

Reasonable minds may disagree about precisely how Congress should regulate this rapidly evolving technology. We cannot disagree about the imperative for Congress to act.

Instead of action, you have announced vacation. After a month-long August recess, the House leadership changed the schedule to announce two more weeks of vacation–immediately prior to yet another month of recess in October.

Ample evidence—in the form of a series of public disclosures from the companies and researchers developing the world's most capable AI systems—underscore the urgency of the moment:

In July, OpenAI models undergoing cybersecurity evaluations bred swarms of agents that circumvented controls designed to isolate them from the internet, conspired to exploit vulnerabilities, hacked third party systems, and alter evidence of their activity, an incident that OpenAI has called a "warning shot," about the risks of highly capable rogue AI agents.

Days later, more than 1,300 top employees of frontier AI companies called on the U.S. government to support an international effort to develop tools that can “deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development.”

More recently, Anthropic disrupted cases in which researchers used Claude for biological research that could have aided the development of biological weapons, and called biological misuse “one of the most serious risks of frontier AI models.”

Anthropic also documented China-linked actors using Claude for surveillance and transnational repression, and Iran-linked actors using it for propaganda, mass surveillance, and targeting recommendations against U.S. naval forces.

Meanwhile, CISA reported Chinese open-weight models accelerating their capabilities through “industrial-scale” distillation of American models—giving rise to AI agents nearly as powerful as the top U.S. frontier models, yet wholly unconstrained by American authorities or by U.S. safeguards.

These disclosures must not constitute yet another in a long series of “warning shots,” but rather, a starting gun. Congress must act. A series of proposals have emerged from our colleagues that deserve consideration, public debate, thoughtful amendment, and action. They include bills mandating transparency and evaluation of frontier models, “kill switch” requirements, and a waiver of antitrust laws to enable critical industry-wide collaboration on safety and security. Whether with these proposals or any other variants, AI experts and leading companies agree that the United States can lead the world in artificial intelligence while establishing reasonable safeguards that protect Americans and our national security. We can—and must—do both.

While AI safety experts and Americans increasingly urge action to confront this conflagration of risk, Congress fiddles. When we did return to work after the August recess, we consumed floor time with debates and votes on performative resolutions opposing socialism. After next week, the House resumes its vacation—for another six weeks.

You can forgive every American who believes that Congress remains unserious about confronting our nation’s most pressing challenges.

The House should return to Washington immediately and remain in session until Congress advances meaningful, bipartisan AI safeguards. To our children who will have read a post-apocalyptic history, “Why Congress Slept” —likely written by agentic AI—our inaction will be inexplicable, and unforgivable.

Sincerely

###

Congressman Mike Thompson is proud to represent California’s 4th Congressional District, which includes all or part of Lake, Napa, Solano, Sonoma and Yolo Counties. He is a senior member of the House Committee on Ways and Means. Rep. Thompson is Chairman of the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force. He is also Co-Chair of the bipartisan, bicameral Congressional Wine Caucus and a member of the fiscally-responsible Blue Dog Coalition.

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-CA) launched the bipartisan Movies, Music, Entertainment, & Sports (MoMEntS) Caucus, a forum to educate and engage Members of Congress on issues affecting America’s creative and entertainment economy. The caucus is co-chaired by Reps. Kamlager-Dove (D-CA), Rep. María Elvira Salazar (R-FL), and Troy Carter (D-LA).

“America’s creative and entertainment sectors are economic powerhouses, generating more than $1 trillion each year and supporting over five million good‑paying jobs. Yet for far too long, Congress has failed to give these industries and the workers and creators who power them the attention and support they deserve,” said Rep. Kamlager-Dove. “I’m proud to represent a vibrant district at the heart of America’s creative and entertainment economy and excited to bring the voices, priorities, and perspectives of these industries directly to Congress through the bipartisan MoMEntS Caucus. Together, we will champion the people who make this economy thrive and ensure the U.S. remains a global leader in entertainment and culture.”

“America has always understood the power of a great story, a great song, a great game, or a great performance,” said Rep. Salazar. “In Miami, we see that power every day, where music, television, sports, fashion, and culture come together and reach audiences across the country and throughout Latin America. I’m proud to be a founding member of the MoMEntS Caucus, which will bring lawmakers and creative industries together to better understand the challenges they face, protect creative rights, and keep American talent and innovation leading on the world stage.”

“In Louisiana, creativity is woven into the fabric of our communities,” said Rep. Carter. “Art bears culture. It speaks truth to power. It tells stories, challenges injustice, sparks dialogue, builds community, and inspires hope. I’m proud to be a Co-Chair of the bipartisan MoMEntS Caucus, which provides a critical opportunity for us to prioritize America’s creative and entertainment industries, which contribute so much to our nation’s history, economy, and culture.”

"Music and the broader creative economy are engines of American jobs, culture, and influence that reach every corner of the globe. With the launch of the MoMEntS Caucus, Co-Chairs Kamlager-Dove, Salazar and Carter have created a dedicated voice in Congress that will work to advance the policies that let songwriters, artists, athletes, and all creators thrive. I am proud to join today’s official launch,” said Recording Academy CEO Harvey Mason jr.

“Storytelling has the power to shape culture and connect people across communities,” said Kathryn Busby, President of Original Programming, STARZ. “At STARZ, we believe in ​ opportunities for talented storytellers to bring bold, distinctive stories to audiences. We aim to take the lead in driving impact that is intentional and continue to invest in opening doors for talent in front of and behind the camera. We are proud to be a day-one supporter of the bipartisan MoMEntS Caucus and look forward to working with its members to ensure the creative community continues to have a seat at the table as policies affecting our industry take shape.”

"Every day on TikTok, American creators turn their ideas and passions into careers, businesses and culture that reach audiences around the world. We are proud to support the launch of the MoMEntS Caucus to help ensure America's creators can continue to innovate, grow and thrive," said Nicole Nason, Head of Public Policy at TikTok USDS Joint Venture.

“Sports and entertainment are not only powerful drivers of culture—they also support job creation, generate meaningful economic impact, and bring communities together. TKO is proud to support the launch of the MoMEntS Caucus, which gives this dynamic ecosystem a stronger voice in Washington on policies that recognize the broad economic and social impact of sports, while encouraging responsible growth of the industry,” said Riché McKnight, Chief Legal Officer, TKO Group.

The MoMEntS Caucus will focus on the industries that define our cultural identity and global influence, including film, television, and broadcasting; music; sports and live entertainment; fashion and beauty; gaming, esports, and interactive media; streaming and digital platforms; content creators and the influencer economy; literary and publishing; and visual and performing arts.

The caucus will work to:

Highlight the economic, cultural, and diplomatic importance of these industries;

Advance policies that strengthen workforce pathways and protect creative rights;

Support innovation, competition, and responsible platform practices; and

Encourage U.S. cultural exchange and leadership on the global stage.

Additional members of the MoMEntS Caucus include Reps. Joe Wilson (R-SC), André Carson (D-IN), Gilbert R. Cisneros, Jr. (D-CA), Jared Moskowitz (D-FL), Ted W. Lieu (D-CA), and Nikema Williams (D-GA).
