U.S. Representative Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) and nine of her House Democratic colleagues are seeking answers from the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) following the unauthorized reorganization of its staff and research projects. This reorganization has put two research projects on cyclospora—the bacterium that caused the largest foodborne illness outbreak in United States history, with most of the cases occurring in Michigan–on hold. In a letter to the USDA Secretary, the lawmakers are calling on the USDA to reinvest in this research.

“Research projects like those focused on cyclospora play an important role in helping researchers, investigators, and public health officials understand the nature of an outbreak and build a strategy to prevent the next potential outbreak. Researchers who worked on the cancelled cyclospora projects have reported that they are unable to continue any research beyond preserving samples they received from previous outbreaks, and that they are having to turn down requests for assistance from other federal agencies investigating the outbreak,” said the lawmakers.

In addition to Congresswoman Dingell, the letter was signed by U.S. Representatives Marc Veasey (D-TX-33), Andrea Salinas (D-OR-06), Haley Stevens (D-MI-11), Rashida Tlaib (D-MI-12), Jasmine Crockett (D-TX-30), Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL-08), Don Beyer (D-VA-08), Nanette Barragán (D-CA-44), and Yvette Clark (D-NY-09).

A copy of the letter can be found HERE and text is below:This letter is regarding reports that two of three cyclospora-related research projects conducted by the United States Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Agricultural Research Service (ARS) have been shelved on the heels of an unprecedented outbreak of cyclosporiasis — the gastrointestinal illness associated with the cyclospora parasite — across 48 states and Washington D.C. The third research project, though not halted, is moving from the Beltsville Agricultural Research Center (BARC) in Maryland to Iowa as part of USDA’s reorganization plan. Given that scientists working on this project are not expected to relocate, it is likely this research will not be conducted. While Americans are increasingly worried about the safety of our food supply and the ability of federal agencies to respond to outbreaks of foodborne illness like cyclosporiasis, it is especially concerning that USDA would rollback critical food safety research.

This summer’s outbreak of cyclosporiasis is the largest recorded outbreak of foodborne illness in United States history, with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reporting over 18,000 confirmed cases, over 14,000 of which were in Michigan. There are nearly 12,000 additional non-laboratory confirmed cases, and potentially thousands more from people who did not seek medical care or testing. Research projects like those focused on cyclospora play an important role in helping researchers, investigators, and public health officials understand the nature of an outbreak and build a strategy to prevent the next potential outbreak. Researchers who worked on the cancelled cyclospora projects have reported that they are unable to continue any research beyond preserving samples they received from previous outbreaks, and that they are having to turn down requests for assistance from other federal agencies investigating the outbreak. This will likely have a similar effect on private institutions who wish to carry out cyclospora research, since they also rely on samples from ARS. Despite these reported disruptions, USDA has claimed that these labs will be uninterrupted, and that the ARS is “working with research leaders to ensure an orderly transition of programs.”

USDA has directed the blame to Congress, who voted to defund the ARS projects as part of a 2026 Continuing Resolution, enacted on November 12, 2025 However, the Department began planning for a significant workforce reduction and agency restructuring as early as April 2025, according to a document submitted to the Office of Management and Budget and the Office of Personnel Management. Notably, the November 2025 Continuing Resolution included language prohibiting the use of USDA funds for the Department’s reorganization plan without congressional approval, which they appear to be circumventing by proceeding with their plan to reduce the workforce and relocate staff and subcomponent agencies. This includes a 43 percent staffing cut for the ARS, which oversees scientific research like the three cyclospora projects at issue.

The Trump Administration has claimed that research facilities like BARC are too expensive, without regard for the potential cost of stopping this research altogether. According to CDC, there have been 922 cyclosporiasis hospitalizations. While we do not yet know the total cost to the health system of this outbreak, USDA’s Cost Estimates of Foodborne Illness data estimate that, in 2023, the cost of foodborne illness in the United States was $74.7 billion. These costs — compounded by drastic cuts to Medicaid, expired ACA tax credits, and dismantled public health programs — make it clear that we must invest in research to prevent foodborne illness outbreaks.

As we continue to grapple with additional cases of foodborne illnesses in our food supply, the American people should be able to have confidence that the Trump Administration is working to investigate those cases and prevent future outbreaks. Therefore, we respectfully request that you respond to the questions below within two weeks of receipt of this letter.

For what reason did the Department choose not to seek congressional authorization for their reorganization plan? Do you plan to seek such authorization at any point or do you plan to proceed in direct violation of the law?

How many staff at ARS have been let go, left for another position or project, or retired?

a. What specific research was impacted by these departures?

How does USDA plan to ensure an “orderly transition of programs” throughout their reorganization process, despite their own acknowledgement that their relocation plans will result in significant staff attrition?

In terms of staff who have been ordered to relocate, how many are expected to vacate their positions instead of relocating?

What plans are in place to fill any vacancies that occur as a result of these staff departures?

What is the USDA’s plan for the relocation of research materials that are a part of the ongoing cyclospora research project at BARC? Specifically:

a. How does USDA plan to transport samples from BARC to the new location in Iowa?

b. How will USDA account for the potential impact of environmental factors on the integrity of the research conducted in the new lab location?

c. When can ARS researchers who are relocating to the new location expect their research equipment to reach them?

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter and for providing a detailed response to these questions. At a time when Americans are counting on the federal government to protect the safety of their food supply, it is critical that USDA maintain the scientific capacity necessary to investigate outbreaks, support public health officials, and prevent future illnesses.

The resolution commemorates the 30th anniversary of the Missouri-Panama State Partnership Program

Additionally, the legislation celebrates the enduring partnership between the State of Missouri and the Republic of Panama

The Missouri-Panama State Partnership Program was established in 1996 through the National Guard Bureau’s State Partnership Program

Congressman Bell: “For thirty years, Missouri and Panama have stood together as partners and as friends”

Washington, D.C. — Today, Congressman Wesley Bell (D-MO-01) led four bipartisan members of Missouri’s Congressional delegation in introducing a resolution commemorating 30 years of partnership between Missouri and Panama.

"For thirty years, Missouri and Panama have stood together as partners and as friends," said Congressman Bell. "What began in 1996 as a National Guard partnership has grown into something far greater – three decades of shared training, disaster response, and cooperation that have made both Missouri and Panama safer and stronger. This partnership is proof that one of America's greatest strengths lies in our alliances and the relationships we build with nations who share our values. I'm proud to lead this resolution honoring those who have sustained this friendship, and I look forward to deepening these ties for the next thirty years and beyond."

“For 30 years, the Missouri National Guard and Panama’s Public Forces have built a partnership grounded in trust, shared values and a commitment to strengthening our communities and our countries. What began as a military partnership has grown into a lasting relationship that reaches across education, trade, culture, and diplomacy. This anniversary is an opportunity to recognize the men and women who have helped build this partnership and to reaffirm our commitment to the strong ties between Missouri and Panama for years to come,” said Congressman Mark Alford (R-MO-04).

Since coming to Congress, Congressman Bell has made it a priority to maintain and strengthen the relationship between Missouri and Panama. During the FY26 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), he worked to support language to strengthen cybersecurity cooperation between Panama and Missouri. Recently, Congressman Bell met with Panama's Ambassador to the U.S., José Miguel Alemán Healy.

The National Guard's State Partnership Program (SPP) links U.S. states with partner nations around the world to build enduring military and civilian relationships, strengthen security cooperation, and advance shared interests. Established in 1996, the Missouri-Panama partnership is one of the program's longest-running, spanning three decades of joint training, disaster-response coordination, and exchanges that have strengthened both Missouri and Panama.

Over the past 30 years, the Missouri National Guard and Panamanian forces have worked side by side on everything from emergency preparedness to humanitarian assistance, forging bonds that extend well beyond the military and into a broader friendship between the people of Missouri and the Republic of Panama.

In addition to Congressman Bell, the bipartisan resolution was also co-led by members of Missouri’s Congressional Delegation, including Representatives Emanuel Cleaver II (D-MO-05), Ann Wagner (R-MO-02), Mark Alford (R-MO-04), and Sam Graves (R-MO-06).
title: Congressman Bell Leads Members of Missouri Delegation in Bipartisan Resolution Honoring Partnership with Panama

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Lou Correa (CA-46) today introduced a bipartisan resolution honoring the late John Seymour, former U.S. Senator, California State Senator, and Mayor of Anaheim, who died April 18, 2026, at 88.

"John Seymour spent his life serving California – as a Marine, a mayor, and a senator," said Correa. "His legacy of principled leadership still inspires us today."

A Marine veteran and UCLA graduate, Seymour built a career in Orange County real estate before entering public service – serving on the Anaheim City Council, as Mayor, in the state Senate, and finally in the U.S. Senate, where he was known as a pragmatic, bipartisan voice. PATERSON, NJ – Congressmember Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09), the Vice Ranking Member of the House Subcommittee on Aviation, today called on United Airlines to reconsider its plan to eliminate a popular direct route between Newark Liberty International Airport and Lima, Peru, long relied on by New Jersey’s large Peruvian-American community.

“I write to express my concern about United Airlines’ recent decision to eliminate nonstop service between Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) and Jorge Chávez International Airport (LIM) in Lima, Peru. Ending this longstanding route would have a serious impact on New Jersey communities that rely on direct service to Peru, while potentially leaving travelers with fewer choices and higher costs,” Congresswoman Pou writes United CEO Scott Kirby.

United announced earlier this month that it will end nonstop service between Newark and Lima on March 27, 2027, ending a route that has operated since 1996, first under Continental Airlines and later United following its merger. United plans to double its Houston-Lima service to two daily flights when the Newark route ends.

“Given the impact this decision would have for New Jersey’s Peruvian community and for travelers across the Tristate area, I am asking United Airlines to pause its plan to eliminate the Newark–Lima route and consider alternatives that could preserve direct service, including operating the route on a reduced schedule,” Pou concludes in her call to United’s CEO.

According to Census data, New Jersey has roughly 95,000 people of Peruvian origin living in the state. New Jersey’s Ninth District is home to one of the largest Peruvian communities in the United States. At the heart of this community is Paterson’s “Little Lima,” which is full of Peruvian bakeries, salons, restaurants, and other small businesses.

Congresswoman Pou is the lead sponsor of the PERU Act (H.R. 5335) which seeks to strengthen ties between the U.S. and Peru by adding Peru to the list of countries eligible to obtain E1 and E2 visas, so long as the Peruvian government treats United States nationals similarly.

The text of Congresswoman Pou’s letter is below.

Dear Mr. Kirby:

I write to express my concern about United Airlines’ recent decision to eliminate nonstop service between Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) and Jorge Chávez International Airport (LIM) in Lima, Peru. Ending this longstanding route would have a serious impact on New Jersey communities that rely on direct service to Peru, while potentially leaving travelers with fewer choices and higher costs.

New Jersey has deep-rooted ties with Peru, with roughly 95,000 people of Peruvian origin living in the state, the third largest Peruvian population in the country. New Jersey’s Ninth Congressional District, and Paterson in particular, is home to one of the largest Peruvian communities in the United States. At the heart of this community is Paterson’s “Little Lima,” which is full of Peruvian bakeries, salons, restaurants, and other businesses. These ties led Paterson to establish “sister city” partnerships with Machu Picchu and the Municipality of Lurigancho-Chosica in 2024 and 2025, respectively. For decades, our local community members have also worked to strengthen ties between Peru and the United States and rallied to support Peru in times of crisis, including the devastating 2007 earthquake.

For over 30 years, United Airlines and its predecessor Continental Airlines have maintained direct service between Newark and Lima. This route is far more than a convenience. It connects New Jersey families with loved ones in Peru and supports business, tourism, and trade between our two countries. Eliminating it would force many travelers to take connecting flights or travel to other airports, adding time and expense to trips that are already prohibitively expensive.

I recognize that rising fuel prices have created new challenges for the airline industry this year. United Airlines must make business decisions that reflect fast-changing market conditions. However, United has also reported increased revenues and strong passenger demand while announcing plans to expand its network. Given the company’s strong business performance over the last two quarters, United Airlines should provide greater clarity about when a long-established route serving a major New Jersey community is being eliminated. This is particularly true given that United has told investors that it expects to recover 100% of higher fuel cost by the fourth quarter.

The decision to eliminate the non-stop Newark-Lima route comes as United Airlines is announcing new routes to destinations in Luxemburg, Slovenia, France, and elsewhere. This growth is exciting for travelers, but new service should not come at the expense of a route that has served New Jersey’s Peruvian community for decades, particularly when the Newark-Lima route has continued to see strong demand and frequently full flights. United Airlines should be able to expand its network without leaving behind communities that have relied on established routes for decades.

Given the impact this decision would have for New Jersey’s Peruvian community and for travelers across the Tristate area, I am asking United Airlines to pause its plan to eliminate the Newark–Lima route and consider alternatives that could preserve direct service, including operating the route on a reduced schedule.

I appreciate your prompt attention to this matter and would welcome the opportunity to meet with you, along with representatives of our large Peruvian community, to discuss this decision and explore ways to preserve direct service between Newark and Lima. I hope we can work together toward a solution that keeps this important connection in place.

Sincerely,

Congresista Pou hace un llamado a United para mantener los vuelos entre Newark y Lima

La congresista hace un impulso para pausar la cancelación de una ruta con 30 años de servicio que atiende a la numerosa comunidad peruana de Nueva Jersey

PATERSON, NJ – La congresista Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09), vicepresidenta de mayor rango de la Subcomisión de Aviación de la Cámara de Representantes, pidió hoy a United Airlines que reconsideren la decisión de eliminar la popular ruta directa entre el Aeropuerto de Newark y Lima, Perú, de la cual la numerosa comunidad peruana de Nueva Jersey ha dependido durante décadas.

“Le escribo para expresar mi preocupación por la reciente decisión de United Airlines de eliminar el servicio sin escalas entre el Aeropuerto Internacional Newark Liberty (EWR) y el Aeropuerto Internacional Jorge Chávez (LIM) en Lima, Perú. El fin de esta histórica ruta tendría un grave impacto en las comunidades de Nueva Jersey que dependen del servicio directo a Perú, y podría dejar a los viajeros con menos opciones y costos más altos”, escribió la congresista Pou al director ejecutivo de United, Scott Kirby.

United anunció a principios de este mes que pondrá fin al servicio sin escalas entre Newark y Lima el 27 de marzo de 2027, terminando así una ruta que ha operado desde 1996, primero a través de Continental Airlines y posteriormente de United. United planea duplicar su servicio entre Houston y Lima a dos vuelos diarios cuando finalice la ruta desde Newark.

“Dado el impacto que esta decisión tendría en la comunidad peruana de Nueva Jersey y en los viajeros de toda el área triestatal, estoy pidiendo a United Airlines que suspenda su plan de eliminar la ruta Newark-Lima y considere alternativas que permitan preservar el servicio directo, incluida la posibilidad de operar la ruta con una frecuencia reducida”, concluyó Pou en su llamado al director ejecutivo de United.

De acuerdo con el Censo, Nueva Jersey cuenta con aproximadamente 95,000 residentes de origen peruano. El Noveno Distrito Congresional de Nueva Jersey alberga una de las comunidades peruanas más grandes de Estados Unidos. En el corazón de esta comunidad se encuentra Little Lima en Paterson, donde abundan panaderías, salones de belleza, restaurantes y otros pequeños negocios peruanos.

La congresista Pou es la principal patrocinadora de la Ley PERU (H.R. 5335), que busca fortalecer los lazos entre Estados Unidos y Perú al agregar a Perú a la lista de países cuyos ciudadanos pueden solicitar visas E-1 y E-2, siempre que el gobierno peruano otorgue un trato similar a los ciudadanos estadounidenses.

El texto de la carta de la congresista Pou se encuentra a continuación.

Estimado Sr. Kirby:

Le escribo para expresar mi preocupación por la reciente decisión de United Airlines de eliminar el servicio sin escalas entre el Aeropuerto Internacional Newark Liberty (EWR) y el Aeropuerto Internacional Jorge Chávez (LIM) en Lima, Perú. El fin de esta histórica ruta tendría un grave impacto en las comunidades de Nueva Jersey que dependen del servicio directo a Perú, y podría dejar a los viajeros con menos opciones y costos más altos.

Nueva Jersey tiene profundos lazos con Perú, con aproximadamente 95,000 residentes de origen peruano, la tercera población peruana más grande del país. El Noveno Distrito Congresional de Nueva Jersey, y Paterson en particular, alberga una de las comunidades peruanas más grandes de Estados Unidos. En el corazón de esta comunidad se encuentra Little Lima en Paterson, donde abundan panaderías, salones de belleza, restaurantes y otros negocios peruanos. Estos vínculos llevaron a Paterson a establecer relaciones de “ciudades hermanas” con Machu Picchu y la Municipalidad de Lurigancho-Chosica en 2024 y 2025, respectivamente. Durante décadas, miembros de nuestra comunidad local también han trabajado para fortalecer los lazos entre Perú y Estados Unidos y se han movilizado para apoyar a Perú en momentos de crisis, incluido el devastador terremoto de 2007.

Durante más de 30 años, United Airlines y su predecesora, Continental Airlines, han mantenido un servicio directo entre Newark y Lima. Esta ruta es mucho más que una comodidad. Conecta a familias de Nueva Jersey con sus seres queridos en Perú y apoya los negocios, el turismo y el comercio entre nuestros dos países. Eliminarla obligaría a muchos viajeros a tomar vuelos con conexiones o trasladarse a otros aeropuertos, agregando tiempo y gastos a viajes que ya tienen costos prohibitivos.

Reconozco que el aumento de los precios del combustible ha creado nuevos desafíos para la industria aérea este año. United Airlines debe tomar decisiones comerciales que reflejen las condiciones rápidamente cambiantes del mercado. Sin embargo, United también ha reportado un aumento en sus ingresos y una fuerte demanda de pasajeros mientras anuncia planes para ampliar su red. Dado el sólido desempeño comercial de la compañía durante los últimos dos trimestres, United Airlines debería ofrecer mayor claridad cuando decide eliminar una ruta de larga trayectoria que presta servicio a una importante comunidad de Nueva Jersey. Esto es particularmente cierto dado que United ha dicho a sus inversionistas que espera recuperar el 100 por ciento del aumento en los costos del combustible para el cuarto trimestre.

La decisión de eliminar la ruta sin escalas Newark-Lima se produce mientras United Airlines anuncia nuevas rutas a destinos en Luxemburgo, Eslovenia, Francia y otros lugares. Este crecimiento es una buena noticia para los viajeros, pero los nuevos servicios no deberían implementarse a costa de una ruta que ha servido durante décadas a la comunidad peruana de Nueva Jersey, especialmente cuando la ruta Newark-Lima continúa registrando una fuerte demanda y vuelos que con frecuencia están llenos. United Airlines debería poder ampliar su red sin dejar atrás a comunidades que han dependido de rutas establecidas durante décadas.

Dado el impacto que esta decisión tendría en la comunidad peruana de Nueva Jersey y en los viajeros de toda el área triestatal, estoy pidiendo a United Airlines que suspenda su plan de eliminar la ruta Newark-Lima y considere alternativas que permitan preservar el servicio directo, incluida la posibilidad de operar la ruta con una frecuencia reducida.

Agradezco su pronta atención a este asunto y agradecería la oportunidad de reunirme con usted, junto con representantes de nuestra numerosa comunidad peruana, para hablar sobre esta decisión y explorar maneras de preservar el servicio directo entre Newark y Lima. Espero que podamos trabajar juntos para encontrar una solución que mantenga esta importante conexión.

Atentamente,

Nellie Pou

Miembro del Congreso

title: Congresswoman Pou Calls on United to Save Nonstop Newark→Lima Flights

Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appeared on ABC’s This Week with George Stephanopoulos, where he made clear that while Republicans have abandoned the American people, House Democrats will continue to fight hard for an affordable America.

GEORGE STEPHANOPOULOS: We’re joined now by the House Democratic Leader, Hakeem Jeffries. Mr. Leader, thank you for coming in this morning. We want to talk about the convention in a second, but let’s start with AI and these remarkable warnings we’re getting this week. I know you met with President Obama and talked about this issue earlier this week. What will Democrats—what do Democrats think needs to be done right now?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we certainly need to begin to act urgently to address the challenges that exist and unfortunately Republicans have abandoned their responsibility. So, under Speaker Mike Johnson, he killed a bipartisan task force this Congress that was prepared to do the serious work necessary to try to erect the guardrails to protect the health, the safety, the well-being of the American people. So what we did as Democrats was to begin last December a Commission on Artificial Intelligence and the Innovation Economy so we could evaluate the steps that needed to be done and then present an aggressive framework, which we’re in the process of doing so that Congress can act on behalf of the American people.

GEORGE STEPHANOPOULOS: But do we even have time for that? You’ve got some of your colleagues, like Representative Ro Khanna and other Democrats, saying Congress should come back in right now, take urgent action right now. Don’t go back for the midterm elections until they’ve done something.

LEADER JEFFRIES: I agree with my colleagues that we actually need to act urgently, and unfortunately, House Republicans have effectively canceled the last two weeks of the legislative session scheduled for this month, which is something that they’ve repeatedly done. We should take decisive action now so that we can slow down, as the CEOs have recently acknowledged, slow down the pace of development in order to protect the American people and ensure that AI is proceeding safely.

GEORGE STEPHANOPOULOS: What is decisive action? Senator Bernie Sanders, as I said, has called for a ban on artificial superintelligence. Your colleague, Ted Lieu of California, says there needs to be a kill switch inside the companies. Are you for those?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’ll have that conversation this week upon our return. We’re going to meet as a Caucus on Tuesday morning, and a high priority will be action on artificial intelligence.

GEORGE STEPHANOPOULOS: Okay, let’s turn to the midterm convention—the President’s $5,000 promise. If Democrats take control next year, is that dead on arrival?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, listen, it wasn’t a serious proposal that was presented by Donald Trump. He’s broken every promise that he’s presented. Donald Trump promised to actually lower costs on day one. Costs haven’t gone down. They’ve gone up. Donald Trump promised not to start endless wars in the Middle East, but to stop them and then turned around and did the exact opposite in Iran. Donald Trump even promised to love and cherish Medicaid and then enacted the largest cut to Medicaid in American history. As Democrats, we’re going to focus on aggressively driving down the high cost of living and fighting for an affordable America because the cost of living in this country is way too high. Republicans have made the situation worse. Democrats are going to act aggressively.

GEORGE STEPHANOPOULOS: Democrats aren’t much more popular than Republicans right now. And the President and his allies at the convention this week tried to argue that you’re the party of communism. Let’s take a look.

RECORDING OF DONALD TRUMP: Remember during the last State of the Union, I said, our country will never be a socialist country. I was right. It’s going to be a communist country, if they win. You know what they did? They dropped socialism. They went right for the big one. And all I’m asking in this election is that you stand with me together. We will defeat communism in America once and for all.

GEORGE STEPHANOPOULOS: Worried that attack might cut?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Not at all. One thing that Donald Trump did say at the midterm convention that was interesting is to pretend as if he’s on the ballot. Mr. President, we don’t have to pretend. You are actually on the ballot. Your failed economy is on the ballot. The cost of living crisis is on the ballot. The fact that you’ve gotten us involved in a reckless and costly war of choice in the Middle East that has skyrocketed gas prices—that’s on the ballot. Ripping healthcare away from millions of Americans is on the ballot. The Trump Tariffs, which have increased costs on everyday Americans by thousands of dollars per year, are on the ballot. Donald Trump is absolutely on the ballot in November, and the American people are going to send a message loudly and clearly on Election Day that even Donald Trump cannot ignore.

GEORGE STEPHANOPOULOS: The internet activist Hasan Piker was also front and center at this convention in Dallas this week, particularly his comment that America deserved 9/11. How should Democrats handle him?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, I’ve been very clear in terms of my denunciation of him and the aggressive, in some cases antisemitic remarks that he’s issued, as have other Democratic candidates all across the country. Now what’s interesting is, in terms of who’s going to be on the ballot, George, in November, we’ve got extraordinary candidates. We’ve got combat veterans like Cait Conley and Rebecca Bennett, we’ve got doctors, we’ve got nurses, we have engineers, we have farmers, we have union leaders, we’ve got firefighters, we’ve got police officers, we have a hostage negotiator, we have a Tejano music superstar in the Rio Grande Valley and even a smokejumper in Montana. These are extraordinary candidates. Their names will appear on the ballot. They’ve got incredible patriotic life experiences and their commitment to public service is going to speak for itself.

GEORGE STEPHANOPOULOS: You’ve taken some heat from progressives in the party, including from many who align with the Democratic Socialists. Are you confident that you’ll actually be Speaker if the Democrats win?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’re focused right now on taking back control of the House of Representatives. That is the only mission that’s important, so we can lower the high cost of living, lower the cost of gas, lower the cost of groceries, lower the cost of housing, certainly fight to make healthcare affordable for every single American and combat the unprecedented corruption that’s been unleashed on the American people and beginning on day one, hold the crooks accountable. We’ve made clear, George, that if someone has been screwing over the American people, shortchanging the American people or stealing from the American people, they’re going to be held accountable under a Democratic majority.

GEORGE STEPHANOPOULOS: You said hold the crooks accountable. Does that mean that the House is going to be pursuing impeachment proceedings on day one?

LEADER JEFFRIES: No, we haven’t ruled anything in and we haven’t ruled anything out in terms of impeachment. As it relates to accountability, what we’re going to do, led by Jamie Raskin and House Committee Democrats on the Judiciary Committee as well as House Democrats on the Oversight Committee, led by Robert Garcia—both of them are doing a tremendous job—we’ve got to follow the facts, apply the law, be guided by the Constitution and then let the chips fall where they may, in the best interest of the American people so that the House, once again, can function like a separate and co-equal branch of government and a check and balance on an out-of-control executive branch.

GEORGE STEPHANOPOULOS: On that theme, a lot of Democrats had raised questions about the activities—the private business activities of Jared Kushner. Was it a mistake for you to meet with him?

LEADER JEFFRIES: No, listen, I’m of the view that if we’re going to be committed to actually solving problems on behalf of the American people, including, by the way, passing the housing affordability bill in this Congress that became law as a result of bipartisan work led by Maxine Waters in the House and Elizabeth Warren in the Senate, there are going to be times that you have to speak with people on the other side of the aisle, even individuals who you strongly disagree with on the overwhelming majority of issues.

GEORGE STEPHANOPOULOS: And if the number one issue is the cost of living right now, what do Democrats do on day one about that?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, listen, there’s a variety of different things that we’re going to have to do. We have to end the Trump Tariffs, because we know the Trump Tariffs have increased costs on everyday Americans by thousands of dollars per year. We’ve got to stop this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed gas prices to the highest levels, for instance, on Labor Day ever seen in the United States of America. We’ve certainly got to fix our broken healthcare system and do the type of things like restoring the Affordable Care Act tax credits, which have increased costs on everyday Americans by thousands of dollars per year, in some cases up to a thousand dollars per month in ways that are unaffordable for people who can no longer be able to go see a doctor when they need one. These are some of the things that I think we can begin to do, but it’s going to have to be a bold, aggressive legislative effort that we sustain, not just for the first 100 days, but for the first year and the entirety of the Congress.

GEORGE STEPHANOPOULOS: It’s almost certainly going to have to take some cooperation from President Trump. He went on Fox News this week and said he thinks he can make deals with you. Do you see areas where cooperation is possible?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, I think, look—we’ve said from the very beginning of this Congress, if the other side of the aisle is willing to find the common ground necessary to decisively address the fact that everyday Americans are drowning in this Republican economy, working hard, playing by the rules, can’t thrive and can barely survive, then we’re committed to actually trying to find that common ground, as we just recently did with the housing affordability bill that is now law.

GEORGE STEPHANOPOULOS: Leader Jeffries, thanks for your time this morning.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Thanks, George.

Full interview can be watched here.

The Haaretz article below, titled “Netanyahu Led Israel 'Blindly to Disaster,' Eisenkot Says After Haaretz Exposé on UAE Warning Before Oct. 7,” speaks for itself.

A readable PDF version of this article is available by clicking the link here or reading the story below.

Netanyahu Led Israel 'Blindly to Disaster,' Eisenkot

Says After Haaretz Exposé on UAE Warning Before Oct. 7

(Haaretz, September 8, 2026)

By: Noa Shpigel and Jonathan Lis

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu led Israel blindly to disaster and is unfit to serve, leading opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot said Tuesday, as opposition leaders responded to a Haaretz expose revealing that Netanyahu received an explicit warning from UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed that Hamas was planning a major operation against Israel.

"Those around Netanyahu are echoing disgraceful conspiracy theories and allegations of betrayal, while clinging to the most absurd statement a leader can make: 'No one woke me up,'" Eisenkot said.

Earlier Tuesday, Haaretz reported that bin Zayed, known as MBZ, personally warned Netanyahu that, in his assessment, Hamas' leader in Gaza, Yahya Sinwar, was preparing for war. The call took place in late September 2023, about a week and a half before the attack, and lasted 45 minutes.

"Who failed to wake whom?" Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, wrote on X, referring to a key finding in the report that Netanyahu did not inform Israel's security establishment of MBZ's personal warning.

Bin Zayed assessed that Sinwar was preparing for a major event, urging Netanyahu to prepare for the threat, an adviser to the president told Haaretz.

Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, leader of the Together party, said Netanyahu bore direct responsibility for the October 7, 2023 attacks. In an interview with Kan public radio, Bennett said Netanyahu "was deep in the conception."

Asked if he knew of the existence of MBZ's call to the prime minister, Bennett told Kan he was aware Netanyahu had received warnings from bin Zayed as well as Egypt's intelligence chief, but chose to ignore them.

Netanyahu was doing everything in his power to avoid the establishment of a state commission of inquiry that would "uncover the truth," Bennett said in a statement, referring to the report as truthful.

"Netanyahu was so captive to his own conception that even clear warnings from regional leaders did not move him from his seat," he added.

Democrats Party Chairman Yair Golan and party lawmaker Gilad Kariv also responded to the report, describing the findings as "criminal."

"He knew. He was warned," Golan wrote in a post on X, referring to Netanyahu. "The stories of 'I wasn't woken up' are over."

Golan accused Netanyahu of neglecting his responsibilities as prime minister through "deliberate and criminal abandonment," calling him "unfit and illegitimate" and urging that he be imprisoned for "his crimes against the State of Israel."

In a statement, Kariv described the revelations as a "crime against Israeli society and against every citizen of the country."

Kariv also said Netanyahu bears responsibility for the October 7, 2023, attacks "not only by virtue of being prime minister, but because he received warnings and alerts from multiple parties and sources and did nothing."

Kariv called for the establishment of a state commission of inquiry that would "open all the Pandora's boxes that led to the terrible massacre."
title: ICYMI: The Haaretz article below, titled “Netanyahu Led Israel 'Blindly to Disaster,' Eisenkot Says After Haaretz Exposé on UAE Warning Before Oct. 7."

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Yesterday, the bipartisan Doug LaMalfa Federal Disaster Tax Relief Certainty Act became law, delivering long-awaited tax relief for survivors of the January 2025 Los Angeles County fires.

The law ensures that qualifying wildfire relief payments, including settlements received by Eaton Fire survivors, can be excluded from federal taxable income regardless of when those payments are received.

Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28), a member of the House Ways and Means Committee, has fought for federal tax relief for Eaton Fire survivors since the aftermath of the fire. Earlier this year, she introduced H.R. 6842, the Disaster Survivors Tax Relief and Recovery Act, comprehensive legislation to address this and several additional financial barriers facing families rebuilding after major disasters.

Rep. Chu released the following statement:

“This marks a major victory for Eaton Fire survivors and a testament to what Congress can accomplish when Democrats and Republicans come together to put disaster survivors first. From the beginning, I have fought to make sure families who lost their homes, their savings, and so much more in the Eaton Fire would not then be punished with a massive federal tax bill on the very compensation they need to rebuild. After months of work in Congress, we finally got this relief across the finish line.

With this bipartisan legislation now law, Eaton Fire survivors can receive qualifying wildfire relief payments without worrying that the federal government will take a portion of that recovery money in taxes simply because their settlements arrived after an arbitrary deadline. Survivors have already lost far too much. They deserve to keep the full value of the compensation they receive to rebuild their homes and their lives.

I am incredibly proud to have fought alongside colleagues on both sides of the aisle to deliver this relief. Earlier this year, I introduced my Disaster Survivors Tax Relief and Recovery Act because I believe our tax code should help families recover from disasters, not make recovery harder. Today, a critical piece of the relief I have been fighting for is finally law.

But making wildfire settlements tax-free is only one piece of the enormous financial challenge survivors face. My legislation would go further, including by allowing disaster survivors to withdraw up to $100,000 from their retirement accounts without the usual early-withdrawal penalty; protecting access to the Earned Income Tax Credit and refundable Child Tax Credit for eligible families whose incomes fell after a disaster; expanding incentives for charitable disaster relief; providing additional Low-Income Housing Tax Credits to spur housing construction in disaster-affected communities; and providing additional tax relief for disaster losses.

These protections are desperately needed. Two out of three Eaton Fire survivors have still not returned home. Nearly half have exhausted their savings or taken on debt, and the typical homeowner still faces an estimated $500,000 rebuilding gap.

That is why the next major step must be President Trump fully funding Governor Newsom's disaster supplemental request, with no strings attached, to deliver the federal disaster funding our communities have been waiting far too long to receive. Without that investment, recovery efforts will stall, costs will continue to grow, and families will remain unable to come home.

While we celebrate this hard-fought bipartisan victory for disaster survivors, the fight continues. I will keep pushing to enact the remaining provisions of my Disaster Survivors Tax Relief and Recovery Act and to secure the federal disaster funding necessary to make our communities whole.”
title: Rep. Chu Celebrates Major Bipartisan Disaster Tax Relief Victory for Eaton Fire Survivors

PHOENIX — Arizona Industries for the Blind (AIB) presented U.S. Rep. Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) with the AbilityOne Congressional Champion Award on September 10, 2026,

The award was presented during a visit to AIB’s Phoenix facility, where Rep. Ansari met with AIB team members and learned how their work supports federal customers and demonstrates the capabilities of people who are blind.

“Congressional champions play an important role in protecting employment opportunities and ensuring the AbilityOne Program remains a dependable resource for federal customers,” said David Steinmetz, Community and Public Relations Manager for Arizona Industries for the Blind. “We appreciate Congresswoman Ansari taking the time to meet our team members, learn about their experiences and recognize the value they bring to Arizona and the nation.”

“I am honored to receive the AbilityOne Congressional Champion Award from Arizona Industries for the Blind,” said Rep. Yassamin Ansari. “AIB team members demonstrate every day that people who are blind bring valuable skills, talent and dedication to our workforce. I remain committed to supporting policies that expand employment opportunities and ensure that every person has the opportunity to achieve greater independence through meaningful work.”

The AbilityOne Congressional Champion Award recognizes members of Congress who demonstrate a commitment to the AbilityOne Program and the employment of people who are blind or have significant disabilities.

Through the AbilityOne Program, AIB team members provide essential products and services to federal and military customers. AIB’s operations include warehousing and distribution, packaging, kitting, document imaging and Base Supply Center services.

The award recognizes Rep. Ansari’s commitment to improving the lives of Americans who are blind or have significant disabilities and her support of the AbilityOne Program. David Steinmetz, AIB Public Policy Manager, stands behind them.

New Haven, CT – Today, U.S. Representatives Rosa DeLauro (CT-03) issued the following statement in remembrance marking 25 since the September 11, 2001, terror attacks.

“Twenty-five years ago, today, the United States of America experienced one of its darkest days in history.

On September 11, 2001, 2,977 people lost their lives, and countless others ­— families, first responders, and survivors — have carried the pain of that day ever since. Hundreds of thousands of others’ health were affected because of that day. Today, we remember those we lost, honor the courage of those who responded, and stand with the families and loved ones who continue to preserve their memory.

“We remember September 11th as a day that left a mark on us all. Twenty-five years have passed, but many of us remember the exact moment we learned of the attacks on the Twin Towers in New York City, the Pentagon in Washington, DC, and Flight 93. I think about the amount of despair I felt that day. I, along with other Members of Congress, evacuated our offices and gathered on the steps of our nations Capitol. In a moment of immense grief and uncertainty we stood together as one and sang ‘God Bless America.’ In that moment, the division that seemed important gave way and we discovered a shared sense of grief and hope. They sought to break our American spirit, but they only unified our resolve.

“On this solemn anniversary, let us remember the unity that followed the attacks. We as Americans stood together — not as Democrats or Republicans, but as neighbors, friends, and fellow Americans. Much has changed since September 11, 2001, but we have refused to forget. May we always remember that even on the darkest days our nation can find strength in one another, and that unity and hope is the force that will carry us further than division.
title: DeLauro Statement Marking the 25th Anniversary of the Attacks on September 11, 2001

Monterey, CA – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) joined Reps. Nikki Budzinski (IL-13), Chris Pappas (NH-01), and Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), along with nearly 100 other members of Congress, in demanding that Postmaster General David Steiner halt implementation of a new U.S. Postal Service (USPS) rule carrying out President Trump’s executive order restricting mail ballot delivery. The lawmakers warned that the rule could throw the nation’s election system into uncertainty and chaos just weeks before states begin sending mail-in ballots to millions of Americans. The rule would require USPS employees to cross-reference mail ballots against voter information supplied by states, effectively asking postal workers to act as election judges.

“The evidence is clear: Voting by mail is safe, effective, and helps to ensure everyone is able to execute their constitutional right to vote,” wrote the lawmakers. “USPS has played an essential role in elections for generations – and it is our fear that this final rule risks harming the democratic process and severely damaging USPS’s relationship with the millions of Americans who rely on USPS to deliver ballots every election cycle.”

The lawmakers pointed to USPS’s longstanding record of successfully delivering election mail and the extremely low incidence of mail-voting fraud. During the 2024 election cycle, USPS delivered 99.22 million ballots, including ballots for servicemembers overseas, and delivered 99.88% of election mail within seven days. A 2025 Brookings Institution study cited in the letter found an average of just four cases of voter fraud for every 10 million mail-in votes cast.

The letter also raises serious questions about USPS’s compliance with court orders governing the Administration’s mail-ballot policy. An anonymous whistleblower alleged that USPS resumed development of its Federal Ballot Mail Portal around July 29 while an injunction remained in effect and that work continued even after an August 27 temporary restraining order barred further preparatory steps. The lawmakers wrote that those allegations are difficult to square with USPS’s representation that it would take no action to implement the rule while the injunctions remained in place.

“This rule is a solution in search of a problem,” continued the lawmakers. “For these reasons, we respectfully ask that you halt the implementation of this final rule.”

Rep. Panetta and his colleagues demanded answers from Postmaster General Steiner, including whether USPS conducted a financial analysis of the rule, whether development of the Federal Ballot Mail Portal continued while court orders were in effect, whether USPS coordinated with the White House in developing the rule, how many postal employees would participate in ballot verification, and how USPS plans to handle ballots in states that have already printed envelopes that do not comply with the new requirements.

The full text of the letter is available here and below:

Postmaster General Steiner:

We write to express our grave concerns with the United States Postal Service’s (USPS) Final Rule entitled “Ballot Mail For Federal Elections” issued on August 21, 2026. If implemented, this rule would throw our nation’s entire election system into a state of uncertainty and chaos just weeks before states begin sending mail-in ballots to millions of voters. The implementation of this rule would also further undermine public trust in the USPS’s ability to deliver election mail to the tens of millions of Americans who utilize the Postal Service to cast their ballot every election cycle.

As you know, during the 2024 election cycle USPS delivered 99.22 million ballots for Americans from every corner of the country as well as our servicemen and women serving our nation overseas. USPS delivered 99.88% of election mail within seven days of being sent, and 97.73% within three days, with the average time to deliver ballots from voters to election officials being 1 day. USPS was similarly effective in delivering mail-in ballots during the 2022 midterm and 2020 general election and has been relied on to deliver absentee ballots since the Civil War.

Voter fraud through vote-by-mail is incredibly rare. In 2025, the nonpartisan Brookings Institution found that there are on average four cases of voter fraud for every 10 million mail-in votes, comprising about 0.000043% of total mail-in votes cast. Contrary to claims by President Trump and his allies that mail-in voting encourages fraud, Brookings found that universal vote-by-mail states had the lowest percentage of election mail fraud.

The evidence is clear: voting by mail is safe, effective, and helps to ensure everyone is able to execute their constitutional right to vote. USPS has played an essential role in elections for generations – and it is our fear that this final rule risks harming the democratic process and severely damaging USPS’s relationship with the millions of Americans who rely on USPS to deliver ballots every election cycle.

This administration’s actions appear to be a misguided effort to correct a problem that does not exist. As mentioned above, every neutral and nonpartisan study on vote-by-mail shows that there has never been systemic fraud associated with voting by mail. However, the primary comments in support of the rule discussed “voter fraud as a significant problem and lauded the proposed rule for helping to restore voters’ confidence in election integrity.” We believe that it is telling that the primary supporters of the rule are arguing in its favor almost exclusively on the grounds that it would help eliminate an exceedingly rare problem.

Furthermore, these concerns are compounded by questions about USPS's candor with Congress and the courts. At the June 24, 2026 Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee hearing, you reiterated that USPS would comply with any court orders governing mail-in voting. Yet an anonymous whistleblower disclosure submitted to Senator Blumenthal describes a different pattern: after USPS halted work on the Federal Ballot Mail Portal following the June 25, 2026 injunction, the whistleblower alleges USPS ordered development to resume around July 29, 2026 — while that injunction remained in effect — and that work continued even after the August 27, 2026 Temporary Restraining Order again barred USPS from taking further preparatory steps. This is difficult to square with USPS's own representation in the Final Rule that it would take no action to implement the rule while the injunctions remained in place.

Although we believe that this rule is unconstitutional and illegal, we also have grave concerns with how this rule would be implemented given the extremely short time frame before election mail is sent by states and voters. Under this rule, USPS would be asking its employees – many of whom are already overworked and understaffed – to essentially act as election judges by and cross-referencing mail-in ballots with lists provided by states. It is irresponsible to impose these additional and undefined responsibilities that would be outside the normal expectations of a USPS employee.

Given the Postal Service’s current financial crisis – which you are asking for support from Congress to solve – and subpar on-time delivery rates, it does not make sense to dedicate limited USPS resources to implement this rule, especially when USPS’s existing election mail procedures have proved to be extremely effective. This rule is a solution in search of a problem. For these reasons, we respectfully ask that you halt the implementation of this final rule.

We also ask that you respond to the following questions no later than Thursday September 10, 2026:

1. Has the USPS commissioned or completed a comprehensive financial analysis on the implementation costs of this rule? If so, please provide it to Congress.

2. Did USPS continue development of the Federal Ballot Mail Portal or related IT systems at any time while a court order enjoining implementation of Section 3 of Executive Order 14399 was in effect? If so, please provide the specific dates on which that work occurred and the legal rationale for continuing it while the injunction remained in place.

3. How could USPS represent—both publicly and in the Final Rule itself—that it would take no steps to implement the rule while the relevant injunctions remained in effect, when development work apparently continued during that same period?

4. Prior to issuing this rule, did anyone at USPS coordinate with or seek input from the White House about the contents of the rule? If so, in what form was input requested and please identify all White House political appointees and officials who were consulted?

5. Prior to issuing this rule, did anyone at USPS coordinate with or seek input from local and state election officials about the contents of the rule, specifically surrounding implementation?

6. How many USPS employees are expected to participate in the ballot verification process, and how will USPS fund additional training for employees without disrupting existing mail operations?

7. Given that multiple states begin mailing absentee ballots in a matter of days, under this rule, how does the Postal Service intend to deliver ballots in states that have already printed envelopes for the 2026 general election that do not comply with the envelope design standards required under the final rule?

Thank you for your time and consideration. We look forward to receiving your response.

Sincerely,

###
title: Rep. Panetta Joins Nearly 100 Lawmakers in Demanding USPS Halt Mail Ballot Rule

NEW YORK, NY — Today, U.S. Representative Seth Magaziner, Ranking Member of the Counterterrorism and Intelligence Subcommittee on the House Homeland Security Committee, joined elected officials, dignitaries, and family members of victims at the remembrance ceremony event at Ground Zero in New York City to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the September 11th attacks.

Magaziner took part in the September 11th Annual Commemoration Ceremony on the Memorial plaza, where family members read the names of the nearly 3,000 people killed in the attacks. The ceremony included seven moments of silence marking when each of the World Trade Center towers was struck and when each fell, the attack on the Pentagon, the crash of Flight 93 near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, and the lives lost in the years since to 9/11-related illness and injury.

“Twenty-five years later, we owe it to the victims, survivors and first responders who ran toward danger to make sure that our nation never forgets,” said Magaziner. “As we stand with the families of those who lost loved ones, we must commit to caring for the first responders who developed lasting illnesses because of their service and to work across party lines to prevent another attack like this from ever happening again.”

The visit began Thursday, when Members toured the National September 11 Memorial & Museum, laid flowers at the Memorial, and previewed the Museum's new 25th Anniversary Exhibition ahead of its public opening.

Magaziner was joined by several of his colleagues on the Homeland Security Committee including the Committee Chair, Rep. Andrew Garbarino (R-NY-02),, Rep. Jodey Arrington (R-TX-19), Rep. Clay Fuller (R-GA-14), Rep. Dan Goldman (D-NY-10), Rep. David Joyce (R-OH-14), Rep. Tim Kennedy (D-NY-26), Rep. Nick LaLota (R-NY-01), Rep. Analilia Mejia (D-NJ-11), Rep. Matt Van Epps (R-TN-07), and Rep. James Walkinshaw (D-VA-11).
title: Magaziner Attends Ceremony Marking 25th Anniversary of September 11th Attacks in New York City

Washington – Rep. Mike Thompson (CA-04) announced that the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) is providing $4 million in emergency funding to address the growing threat posed by the invasive glassy-winged sharpshooter (GWSS) in California. This summer, Rep. Thompson, U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA) and Adam Schiff (D-CA), along with Rep. David Valadao (CA-22) and ten colleagues teamed up to urge the U.S. Department of Agriculture to provide emergency funding to address the growing threat posed by the invasive glassy-winged sharpshooter in California.

The funding announcement follows congressional letters and a call between Rep. Thompson and USDA Undersecretary Hoskins about the importance of federal assistance to stop the spread of glassy-winged sharpshooters for California agriculture producers. USDA has been working in close collaboration with Secretary Karen Ross of the California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA) and county agricultural commissioners as they lead the response and conduct trace-forward activities.

“Glad that USDA is providing $4 million in funding to fight the glassy-winged sharpshooter,” said Thompson. “I have been working to ensure our Agriculture community receives the support it needs to address this issue, and while this is a great step in the right direction, there is still more work to be done to protect our community.”

This funding will allow the CDFA to expand trace-forward investigations, increase inspections, destroy infested materials, and strengthen trapping and visual surveys at high-risk locations associated with recent GWSS-infested plant shipments. The Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) works with the CDFA and county agricultural commissioners through a long-standing cooperative program to manage and contain GWSS in California.

APHIS receives an annual appropriation to support the CDFA and county partners in preventing the further spread of Pierce’s disease. In fiscal year 2026, APHIS has allocated more than $15 million to the CDFA for GWSS activities.

###

Congressman Mike Thompson is proud to represent California’s 4th Congressional District, which includes all or part of Lake, Napa, Solano, Sonoma and Yolo Counties. He is a senior member of the House Committee on Ways and Means. Rep. Thompson is Chairman of the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force. He is also Co-Chair of the bipartisan, bicameral Congressional Wine Caucus and a member of the fiscally-responsible Blue Dog Coalition.
title: THOMPSON SECURES $4 MILLION FROM USDA FOR GLASSY-WINGED SHARPSHOOTER RESPONSE ACTIVITIES

As the United States marks 25 years since September 11, U.S. Representative Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) penned an essay recounting her experience on that day and how Americans united the weeks that followed.

"We had been attacked, and we pulled together. For a brief time, the things that divided us seemed smaller than the things that united us. We talked to each other. We listened. We comforted strangers. We checked on neighbors. We reached across differences of faith, race and background. We spent time trying to understand one another rather than turning away,” Congresswoman Dingell wrote. “The Jewish community worked hard to support the Muslim community. Communities reached across lines of faith and ethnicity. People who might never have spoken to one another before stood together. Bridges were built.”

Congresswoman Dingell continued: “Twenty-five years later, I look around our country and worry about how many of those bridges are gone or endangered. Antisemitism is real. Hatred and fear directed at Muslims are real. Racism is real. Political and religious hatred can turn quickly into threats, violence and tragedy. We should be worried ‒ not because America is weak, but because we know how quickly fear can divide us if we allow it to. America did not deserve 9/11. No country deserves terrorism, hatred or violence. And no American should be made to feel unsafe because of their faith, religion, race, ethnicity or heritage. As we mark the 25th anniversary of 9/11, we will remember the nearly 3,000 people who were killed, and the countless families whose lives were changed forever. We will remember the firefighters, police officers, first responders and ordinary citizens who showed extraordinary courage. But remembrance must be more than looking backward. We should also remember who we were in the days after.”

Congresswoman Dingell’s op-ed can be found HERE and text is below:

The day, Sept. 11, 2001, is seeded in my mind and soul forever.

I was on one of the few planes still flying that morning. We landed at National Airport around 8 a.m., before the first tower was hit. Then U.S.-Rep. David Camp was sitting next to me. Before we left Detroit, I turned to him and said, "I have the weirdest feeling. If you weren’t sitting next to me, I think I would get off this plane."

We had no idea what was about to happen. As we watched planes crash into the World Trade Center, the Pentagon was attacked, and reports came that another plane might be headed toward the Capitol. But none of us fully understood what we were witnessing.

My husband, John, was in the Capitol. When people were being told to leave, he refused. He said, “No one is going to chase me out of the symbol of our democracy. I fought in World War II, and I’m staying here.”

Friends working at the White House came to my General Motors Foundation office in downtown DC, terrified. Secret Service agents had told women in heels to take off their shoes and run. Everything we knew about safety and normal life seemed to disappear in a matter of hours. No one was able to fly home. A few days later, John and I drove back to Michigan with Ohio Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur. We were deeply worried about Dearborn, our hometown, and about the possibility of backlash and violence against our Muslim neighbors.

President George W. Bush addressed the nation at a Joint Session of Congress on Sept. 20, but we stayed in Dearborn because we believed that in a moment of fear, we had a responsibility to stand with our community and fight hatred wherever we saw it. Bill Ford and John Dingell hosted a candlelight vigil at the Henry Ford Museum. Thousands came. There was fear, and there was faith. There was grief, but there was also an extraordinary sense that we were going to stand together.

Then came the names. Friends who were lost. Sons and daughters of friends. One of John’s dearest friends. Firefighters and police officers who ran into burning buildings to save people and never came home. The grief was overwhelming.

But something else happened in those days that I will never forget: America came together.

It was one of the most horrific times in our nation’s history, and yet, in some ways, it was also one of the most special. We had been attacked, and we pulled together. For a brief time, the things that divided us seemed smaller than the things that united us. We talked to each other. We listened. We comforted strangers. We checked on neighbors. We reached across differences of faith, race and background. We spent time trying to understand one another rather than turning away. The Jewish community worked hard to support the Muslim community. Communities reached across lines of faith and ethnicity. People who might never have spoken to one another before stood together. Bridges were built.

Twenty-five years later, I look around our country and worry about how many of those bridges are gone or endangered. Antisemitism is real. Hatred and fear directed at Muslims are real. Racism is real. Political and religious hatred can turn quickly into threats, violence and tragedy. We should be worried ‒ not because America is weak, but because we know how quickly fear can divide us if we allow it to. America did not deserve 9/11. No country deserves terrorism, hatred or violence. And no American should be made to feel unsafe because of their faith, religion, race, ethnicity or heritage.

As we mark the 25th anniversary of 9/11, we will remember the nearly 3,000 people who were killed, and the countless families whose lives were changed forever. We will remember the firefighters, police officers, first responders and ordinary citizens who showed extraordinary courage. But remembrance must be more than looking backward. We should also remember who we were in the days after.

We were frightened, but we did not have to be consumed by fear. We were grieving, but we reached out to one another. We were attacked, but we did not have to turn our anger against innocent people in our own communities. We found strength in coming together. That is the lesson I hope we carry into the next 25 years.

We cannot change what happened on Sept. 11, 2001. We cannot bring back those we lost. But we can decide what their memory asks of us.
title: ICYMI: Dingell Marks 25th Anniversary of September 11

WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) released the following statement today commemorating the 25th anniversary of the terrorist attacks on September 11, 2001:

“September 11, 2001, was a day of tragedy and created a new sense of vulnerability. But it also was followed by a unity of purpose and conviction that the terrorists would not prevail.

“I will never forget standing on the steps of the U.S. Capitol that evening, rallying with colleagues, staff, and fellow citizens who had gathered to show our solidarity with those who had lost loved ones, who were still searching for the missing, and who were working to restore safety. Moved by that moment, we began to sing 'God Bless America,' and soon everyone was joining in. It was a powerful expression of our unity and resolve. It was, too, a reminder that we are, despite our differences and the often-heated rhetoric in our politics, one nation with a common purpose and a shared hope for peace, justice, and the triumph of good over evil.

“The magnitude of this tragedy created great unity. But as it fades from memory, the realization of that unity becomes more difficult to sustain. We must nevertheless strive to recapture it.

“Ground Zero, the west side of the Pentagon, and the hallowed field in Shanksville are now quiet places of peace. Today, bells will be rung, names will be read, and hymns will be sung. But nothing we do today can honor the dead and injured more than to carry on tomorrow, as we have now done for a quarter century, and continue the difficult task of building the America that terrorists tried in vain to dismantle. An America united. An America filled with optimism in devotion its purpose. An America of big hearts and open arms. An America guided by its highest ideals and committed to ensuring equal justice and opportunity for all.

“Let us rededicate ourselves to seeking that unity of purpose today. May the memory of those lost on September 11, 2001, inspire us to that work now and forever.”
title: Hoyer Statement on 25th Anniversary of 9/11

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Rep. Grace Meng (D-NY) released the following statement on the Trump Administration’s latest attempt to include a citizenship question on the 2030 Census form:

“The Constitution requires congressional representation to be based on the ‘whole number of persons in each State’—not only citizens or green-card holders. Every person living in our country must be counted, regardless of citizenship or immigration status.

The Trump administration’s proposal would erase millions of people from the census data used to distribute political representation. It would exclude not only undocumented immigrants, but also refugees, asylum seekers, visa holders, and other people who are lawfully present in the United States but do not have permanent-resident status. This is un-American, unconstitutional, and a direct attack on immigrant communities.

An inaccurate count risks a decade of consequences. Census data help determine representation in Congress, electoral districts, and the allocation of federal resources for health care, education, infrastructure, and other essential services.

When Donald Trump tried to include a citizenship question on the 2020 Decennial Census form during his first term, I fought back and I won. Earlier this year, I co-led a letter with the Congressional Hispanic Caucus (CHC) and other Congressional leaders opposing changes to the Census test, which includes the citizenship question.

I’ve never stopped fighting to prevent this and I’m prepared to continue as the Top Democrat on the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies. My message is clear: immigrants are part of our communities, and they will not be rendered invisible. The 2030 Census must remain an accurate count of the people—not a political weapon.”

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Yesterday, Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17) led his Pennsylvania colleagues Congresswoman Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05), and Congresswoman Summer Lee (PA-12) on a letter to the Acting Director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) exposing the lack of data transparency in current ICE records management and reporting. ICE is refusing to document in public records which local law enforcement agencies with a 287(g) agreement are involved in arrests, thereby hiding from public view how local law enforcement is involved in ICE’s mass deportation regime.

Specifically, the Congressmembers are pushing for training records, complaints, and oversight records about 287(g) programs in Pennsylvania to be made public. The 287(g) program sets up partnerships between ICE and state or local law enforcement agencies to authorize selected officers to carry out federal immigration enforcement or deportation. Reps. Deluzio, Dean, Scanlon, and Lee are demanding ICE require its agents to fully complete the 287(g)-designation field in its arrest records and identify the participating agencies involved in arrests. They also make specific demands that more data, details, and records be released to the public.

The Pennsylvania congressmembers write in the letter:

“According to published federal records between January 1 to August 6, 2026, of the 1,227 Pennsylvania 287(g) arrest records, only 12 of those records included the task force designation agency that was involved in arrest. ICE chose to withhold that information more than 1,000 times so far this year despite such information being a designated field included in arrest records. This discrepancy undermines transparency and leaves the public without a clear understanding of which agency or department was involved.

The members continue:

“The public has a right to clear and complete information about the nature of the enforcement activities taking place in our neighborhoods and the departments or agencies responsible for carrying them out. Programs between federal and local law enforcement agencies must meet the highest standards of transparency.”

The full text of the letter is available HERE.

Congressman Deluzio is actively fighting back against Trump’s mass deportation scheme. In May 2026, he and Congresswoman Summer Lee conducted an unannounced oversight visit to Moshannon Valley Processing Center in Clearfield County, PA, where they found that the overwhelming majority of people locked up inside the ICE facility were considered low-security level—meaning that they have not been accused of serious, violent crimes or engaged in similar conduct while detained.

During this visit, the two congressmembers were blocked from bringing congressional staff inside the facility. These staff were immigration policy experts and able to provide translation services, limiting the congressmembers’ ability to communicate with people inside Moshannon. After this, Congressman Deluzio introduced the Oversight Access Act, a new bill which would permit Members of Congress to bring one member of their staff inside Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facilities when conducting oversight, without prior notice.

Rep. Deluzio led and joined his Pennsylvania colleagues on recent letters to ICE and the GEO Group, the for-profit prison corporation that owns and operates the Pennsylvania Moshannon Valley Processing Center to demand answers on GEO’s failure to comply with federal standards of adequate staffing and medical care to detainees and to stop obstructing congressional oversight.

###
title: Deluzio Leads PA Colleagues in Demanding Stronger Data Transparency from ICE

AKRON, OH – U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) issued the following statement honoring the 2,977 Americans who lost their lives in the World Trade Center attacks, and the resilience of the first responders who answered the call to serve on September 11, 2001.

“September 11th forever changed us as a nation. On the 25th anniversary of this horrific attack, I am remembering those we lost, and reaffirming my commitment to our first responders – including firefighters, police officers, and paramedics – who stand as pillars of courage in our communities, embodying America’s enduring spirit,” said Rep. Sykes. “As we come together to remember the 2,977 Americans lost on this day, I am reflecting on the lasting impact their memories have left on our nation.

“Every generation carries forward its own remembrance. Some are old enough to remember exactly where they stood that morning. Others have only known a world shaped by what came after: the wars, the security measures, and the grief that rippled through families.

“Despite the pain of our collective loss on September 11, I am reminded of the unwavering bravery of both first responders and bystanders who ran toward the destruction to save countless lives that day. Their selfless actions remind us of the deep resilience and unity at the heart of our country.

“If September 11th is remembered for what was lost, September 12th is remembered for what was found. Americans woke up the next morning to a changed country, but also to a shared sense of purpose that cut across every line that divides us. Neighbors checked on neighbors. Strangers gave blood, donated supplies, and stood in line for hours to help however they could. I have often said that Ohio’s 13th District is the Birthplace of Champions precisely because of moments like these, when everyday people choose to show up for one another.

“Twenty five years later, our shared promise is the same as it was on September 12, 2001. We do not forget, and we keep building a country worthy of what was given for it. As your representative in Congress, I remain steadfast in my commitment to fostering the American spirit and to always fighting for those who put their lives on the line to protect their fellow Americans.”

Rep. Sykes joined the City of Canton for the 9/11 Memorial Stair Climb, to honor the first responders who lost their lives in the attacks on September 11, 2001. Participants climbed the equivalent of the 110 stories of the World Trade Center beginning at 8:46 a.m. to coincide with the time the North Tower was struck.
title: Rep. Sykes Honors First Responders on the 25th Anniversary of 9/11

(WASHINGTON) – Today, Rep. Bennie G. Thompson (D-MS), Ranking Member of the Committee on Homeland Security, released the following statement on the 25th Anniversary of the September 11th, 2001 Attacks.

“Twenty-five years later, the pain of September 11th has not faded. We remember the nearly 3,000 people who were taken from their families and the extraordinary courage shown by first responders and ordinary citizens alike. The best way to honor them is to make sure our country never suffers a tragedy like that again.

“After 9/11, we worked across party lines to strengthen our homeland security. Today, those protections are being weakened as threats continue to evolve. Cutting national security staff, undermining cybersecurity, threatening TSA privatization, and withholding counterterrorism funding create dangerous security gaps. We should be working together to close gaps, not senselessly creating new ones.

“We must be clear-eyed about the world we live in – and strive to uphold our American values as we seek to secure our people and our homeland. We owe it to the Americans who lost their lives on 9/11 to ensure our government is focused on the most pressing threats facing the Nation so that, together, we can help defend the homeland against them.”
