Rep. Torres Urges Banking Regulators to Lower Capital Requirements for Low-Income Housing Tax Credit Investments
Yesterday, Rep. Ritchie Torres (NY-15) sent a letter to Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle W. Bowman, FDIC Chairman Travis Hill, and Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan V. Gould, requesting that federal banking regulators reduce the risk weight assigned to Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) equity investments and associated loans from 100% to 20%.
LIHTC has financed more than four million affordable homes since 1987 and remains the nation’s leading tool for producing and preserving affordable housing. Banks account for roughly 80% of LIHTC equity investment, and the current 100% risk weight increases the capital banks must hold against these investments, constraining the financing available for affordable housing.
The letter notes that LIHTC has a near-zero historical loss record. The annual LIHTC recapture rate averaged just 0.08% from 2008 to 2021, and the cumulative foreclosure rate by net equity was just 0.19% from 2000 to 2024. The letter argues that Basel III gives regulators an opportunity to revisit the risk weighting and bring it in line with LIHTC’s actual performance.
The full letter reads (PDF here):
“I am writing to respectfully request that the federal banking regulators reduce the risk weight for Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) equity investments, as well as associated loans, from 100% to 20%.
“LIHTC is the nation’s leading tool for financing the production and preservation of affordable housing. Since 1987, it has financed more than four million affordable homes. With less capital friction, LIHTC could finance millions more.
“The United States faces its deepest housing affordability crisis since the Great Depression. Excessive capital requirements artificially constrain the amount of financing available for affordable housing at a time when the nation can least afford self-inflicted scarcity. Basel III presents banking regulators with an opportunity to reexamine the risk weighting that unnecessarily inhibits investment in LIHTC.
“The 100% risk weight historically assigned to LIHTC is disproportionate to its actual historical risk. Although structured as equity, LIHTC investments exhibit a risk profile far more stable than traditional real estate equity. LIHTC has demonstrated near-zero rates of both recapture and foreclosure. From 2008 to 2021, the annual LIHTC recapture rate averaged just 0.08%. From 2000 to 2024, the cumulative LIHTC foreclosure rate by net equity was just 0.19%. There is nothing in the historical risk profile of LIHTC that justifies anything approaching a 100% risk weight.
“The impact of capital requirements on affordable housing finance cannot be overstated. Banks account for approximately 80% of LIHTC equity investment. Lowering the risk weight for LIHTC to 20% would substantially reduce the capital burden on bank balance sheets, expand investment capacity, and unlock substantial new financing for affordable housing.
“I am not asking banking regulators to treat LIHTC preferentially. Quite the contrary. I am asking for fairness: a risk weight that reflects reality as borne out by history. The verdict of history could not be clearer: LIHTC has an unassailable safety record. The Basel III framework should rate it accordingly.”
title: Rep. Torres Urges Banking Regulators to Lower Capital Requirements for Low-Income Housing Tax Credit Investments

text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Jared Golden (ME-02) released the following statement on the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terror attacks:

“Twenty-five years ago today, our nation endured the deadliest foreign attack on American soil. Today, we hold in our hearts the thousands who lost their lives on September 11, 2001, their families and loved ones. Their memory will not be forgotten.

We also honor those who ran toward danger in the wake of the attacks, from the first responders who rushed without question to Lower Manhattan to the generation who answered the call to defend our nation. That day, Americans joined together, resolute in the face of those who brought terror to our shores.

As we remember those lost and those forever changed on 9/11, let’s also remember that a united America can never be outmatched and that no shadow of fear or terror can dim our spirit.”

###
title: Golden statement on the 25th anniversary of 9/11

Washington, D.C. – United States Representatives Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) and Glenn “GT” Thompson (PA-15), co-chairs of the bipartisan Congressional Service Organization Caucus, introduced a resolution to designate the week of September 6 through September 12 as Celebrate Community Week and recognize the efforts of local service organizations across the country.

The resolution specifically applauds Kiwanis International, Rotary International, Lions Clubs International, and Optimist International for encouraging and promoting community service and humanitarian assistance through their local chapters.

"Local service organizations bring people together to serve working families, strengthen communities, and make a meaningful difference in CA-19 and across the country,” said Rep. Panetta. “Our bipartisan resolution recognizing Celebrate Community Week honors the countless volunteers who roll up their sleeves, give their time and talents, and step up in service to others. Their commitment to civic engagement, civic responsibility, and community service reflects the very best of our country.”

“Volunteerism is fundamental to healthy communities and an important aspect of our country’s shared values,” said Rep. Thompson. “I am grateful for community service organizations; the work they do provides opportunities to support our neighbors in need.”

"Kiwanis International and its fellow service organizations are dedicated to supporting communities in the United States and around the world,” said Kiwanis International President Michael Mulhaul. “We are grateful for the opportunity to collaborate on the Celebrate Community initiative and create meaningful change.”

“Volunteering with service organizations like Rotary gives people the chance to make a bigger impact by working with others, while also growing personally,” said Rotary International President Yinka Babalola. “Celebrate Community Week is a wonderful opportunity to highlight the contributions service organizations make both locally and globally, and the friendships people build along the way as they work toward common goals.”

Full text of the resolution is available here.

###
title: Reps. Panetta and Thompson Introduce Bipartisan Resolution to Commemorate Celebrate Community Week

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (D-CA-45) introduced H.R. 10349, the bipartisan Emergency Responders Mental Health Training (EMT) Act, with Representatives John Rutherford (R-FL-5), Mike Lawler (R-NY-17), and Don Davis (D-NC-1), to expand and improve access to specialized mental health and substance abuse care for first responders. The bill would establish a federal fellowship program to train more behavioral health professionals who understand the unique demands of emergency response work, addressing the mental health crisis that has made it difficult for public safety departments to recruit and retain talent.

“As we mark the 25th anniversary of 9/11, supporting our first responders' mental health has never been more urgent. They're on the front lines every day protecting our communities — often at a cost to their own well-being. I've heard directly from law enforcement in my district that access to mental health care remains a real problem. That's why I'm proud to introduce the bipartisan EMT Act to deliver the specialized mental health care our first responders deserve,” said Representative Tran.

"As a former sheriff, I have seen firsthand the physical and emotional toll that comes with serving on the front lines of public safety," said Representative John H. Rutherford, "Our first responders dedicate their lives to protecting our communities, but too often, those struggling with addiction or substance use disorders suffer silently. I am proud to co-lead legislation with Representative Tran (CA-45) to expand and strengthen our behavioral health workforce, equipping them with the tools they need to serve the men and women who protect our communities."

“Our first responders carry experiences that stay with them long after the emergency is over. Too many struggle to find mental health professionals who understand the unique pressures of their work. We have a responsibility to ensure specialized care is available when they need it. Supporting the mental health of our first responders means supporting the people who protect and care for our families every day,” said Representative Don Davis.

“Our first responders put themselves on the line every day to protect and serve our communities. They face traumatic situations, dangerous conditions, and immense stress, and they deserve access to the specialized mental health support they need. This legislation would help strengthen that support by training mental health professionals to better serve our emergency responders. We have a responsibility to make sure those who are there for us in our most difficult moments have the resources they need," said Representative Mike Lawler.

The Emergency Responders Mental Health Training (EMT) Act would establish a post-graduate fellowship pilot program to increase the number and quality of mental health professionals trained to assist emergency responders. The fellowships would support post-baccalaureate training, including master’s and doctoral degrees, across fields such as psychiatry, nursing, social work, psychology, marriage and family therapy, mental health counseling, and addiction counseling. The bill authorizes $10 million per year for five years and requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to report to Congress on the program’s implementation and results.

The legislation is endorsed by the National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI), National Fraternal Order of Police, National Association of Police Organizations (NAPO), Peace Officers Association of California (PORAC), Federal Law Enforcement Officers Association (FLEOA), Council on Social Work Education (CSWE), National Association of Social Workers, Depression and Bipolar Support Alliance (DBSA), American Association for Marriage and Family Therapy (AAMFT), California Association of Marriage and Family Therapists (CAMFT), National Association of Pediatric Nurse Practitioners, National League for Nursing, American Ambulance Association, National Association of Emergency Medical Technicians (NAEMT), and Falck Ambulances Services Inc.

“Our law enforcement officers selflessly put their lives on the line every day to serve their communities. The mental, physical, and emotional toll of repeated exposure to traumatic and hazardous situations is an often unspoken but widely understood aspect of the job. First responders are subject to significantly above-average rates of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), depression, stress, burnout, and suicide in comparison to the public. Consequently, this significantly impacts their ability to carry out their duties and, on a wider scale, hinders recruitment and retention rates for the profession,” said Patrick Yoes, National President of the Fraternal Order of Police, “This bill presents viable means to ensure that officer wellbeing is safeguarded so that they in turn can properly protect and serve their communities.”

“The work that law enforcement officers do each day and the environments in which they are placed take a huge toll on the human mind, body, and soul. Many of our officers suffer from PTSD and acute stress disorders, but they are reluctant to seek help, especially through services offered by their agency. They worry about confidentiality or believe the mental health specialists provided will not understand what they are going through, what they have experienced,” stated Bill Johnson, Executive Director of the National Association of Police Organizations. “NAPO supports the EMT Act as it will help ensure that officers have access to culturally competent mental health and wellness services. We thank Representatives Tran, Rutherford, Davis, and Lawler for their leadership and support.”

“The American Ambulance Association greatly appreciates the recognition by Representatives Derek Tran, John Rutherford, Don Davis and Mike Lawler of the special mental health circumstances facing our first responders, and their introduction of the Emergency Responders Mental Health Training Act to help ensure there are enough behavioral health practitioners trained to support our paramedics, EMTs, police officers, firefighters and 9-1-1 dispatchers,” said Jamie Pafford-Gresham, President of the American Ambulance Association.

“Falck strongly supports efforts to strengthen mental health care for emergency responders. This legislation recognizes the unique stressors faced by the men and women on the front lines and helps ensure they have access to culturally competent professionals who understand their experiences and can support their mental health, well-being and resilience,” said Falck Ambulances Services Inc. Spokesperson Jeff Lucia, “Emergency responders dedicate their lives to protecting others, and they deserve access to specialized, trauma-informed mental health care that recognizes the unique experiences of their profession. We appreciate Congressman Tran’s leadership on this issue and his commitment to advancing practical solutions that improve care for the people who keep our communities safe.”

"Peace officers spend their careers looking out for everyone else, often at great personal cost — not only through the risks we face in the line of duty, but through the trauma we carry home. Every first responder deserves care from someone who truly understands what this work demands. This bill meets that need, and PORAC is honored to stand behind it," said Peace Officers Research Association of California President Brian R. Marvel.

“Social workers represent the largest group of mental and behavioral health providers in the United States. More providers and more resources are needed—now and in the future. CSWE supports legislative efforts like the EMT Act, which will deliver near-term critical support to first responders experiencing mental health challenges, as well as expand training and funding opportunities to train future providers,” said the Council on Social Work Education.

As a member of the Bipartisan Congressional Law Enforcement Caucus, Representative Tran has made supporting first responders and their mental health a priority in Congress. In December 2025, Tran helped to introduce the bipartisan CARE for First Responders Act to expand counseling and mental health services for first responders, and has cosponsored several bills to support officer safety and wellness, including:

H.R. 309, the bipartisan National Law Enforcement Officers Remembrance, Support, and Community Outreach Act, to improve officer safety and wellness programs;

H.R. 3304, the Providing Child Care for Police Officers Act, to support parents in law enforcement; and

H.R. 8750, the COPS Reauthorization Act, to provide funding for local law enforcement agencies to hire, retain, train, and equip more officers through the Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS) program.

Representative Tran also securedover $1 million for the HOPE Center in Fullerton to deploy licensed mental health professionals alongside law enforcement, ensuring the right responders reach residents experiencing mental health crises while providing more bandwidth for officers to focus on serious crime.

###
title: Representative Tran Introduces Bipartisan Legislation to Strengthen Mental Health Support for Emergency Responders

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Michigan Congresswoman Haley Stevens alongside Reps. Jim Baird (R-IN), Don Beyer (D-VA), and Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA) introduced the Bipartisan Data Science and Literacy Act, to expand access to data science education and make sure Michigan students have the skills needed to compete in an increasingly data-driven economy.

Data science draws on statistics, computer science, and mathematics to analyze and derive insights from data. Yet many students graduate from high school without these foundational skills, even as nearly one in four jobs requires data science skills.

“Data is powering the technologies and jobs that will define America’s economic future, and our students deserve the skills to lead that future,” said Rep. Haley Stevens. “Whether a student goes on to work on the factory floor, in a research lab, at a small business, or developing the next breakthrough technology, the ability to understand and use data will be increasingly important. This legislation is about making sure Michigan students are ready.”

“Data science education can be the catalyst that launches American scientific leadership into the stratosphere. Introducing children to STEM early gives them a foundation to continually build upon, preparing them to tackle increasingly advanced concepts as they reach higher education and enter the workforce. This is how we compound our scientific knowledge and foster the next generation of American innovation. Start early, build upon that knowledge, and grow our nation’s understanding of STEM,” said Rep. Jim Baird.

“Data is one of the most powerful tools shaping our society today. It helps businesses streamline supply chain operations, public health officials track and prevent disease, and Americans navigate nearly every aspect of modern life. Yet too many students lack access to the education they need to understand and use data effectively. Our bill would provide educators with the resources necessary to expand access to a quality data science education and prepare students for 21st century jobs,” said Rep. Don Beyer.

“Every generation has a responsibility to prepare the next for the world they will inherit. As data becomes foundational across nearly every field, our classrooms must keep pace. This legislation builds on the work we have led here in PA-1 to strengthen career and technical education, expand pathways into high-demand fields, and better connect learning with opportunity. The bipartisan Data Science and Literacy Act will carry that mission forward—equipping more students with the skills to succeed, strengthening our workforce, and ensuring America continues to lead,” said Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick.

The Data Science and Literacy Act establishes a grant program at the U.S. Department of Education to expand access to data science education nationwide. The program would support data science instruction from pre-K through community college, strengthen students’ data literacy, and provide professional development opportunities for educators. The legislation also improves federal data collection and establishes evaluation and reporting requirements to guide future investments.

Specifically, the Data Science and Literacy Act authorizes educational grants for the following purposes:

Curriculum Development: Developing, implementing, and expanding data science curricula and instructional materials.

Student Support: Improving student outcomes in data science education, including targeted support for students historically underrepresented in the field.

Professional Development: Providing evidence-based training and recruitment support for educators to effectively teach data science and related subjects.

Partnerships: Supporting collaboration with community colleges, institutions of higher education, and other relevant organizations to strengthen data science education pathways.

Text of the bill can be found here.

The legislation is backed by Data Science 4 Everyone (DS4E), Alliance for Data Science & AI (ADSA), Alliance for Learning Innovation (ALI), American Mathematical Association of Two-Year Colleges (AMATYC), American Statistical Association (AmStat), Association of Mathematics Teacher Educators (AMTE), Computer Science Teachers Association (CSTA), Digital Promise, INFORMS, Inter-university Consortium for Political and Social Research (ICPSR), National Council of Teachers of Mathematics (NCTM), and National Science Teaching Association (NSTA).

“The average school experience is becoming disconnected from the fast-changing world our students are graduating into,” said Zarek Drozda, Executive Director of Data Science 4 Everyone (DS4E). “The question ‘why am I learning this?’ needs to have a better answer. Engaging in data science activities allows students to connect their academic subjects to the real-world, and learn a toolkit for navigating (and questioning) AI at the same time.”

“ADSA works with more than 100 institutions of higher education, from R1 universities, community colleges, HBCUs, and Hispanic-serving institutions. One thing we hear consistently is that they want to be better partners to the K-12 schools in their regions,” said Dr. Micaela Parker, Founder and Executive Director of Alliance for Data Science and AI (ADSA). “The Data Science and Literacy Act creates that opportunity by putting flexible resources into district, community college, and university partnerships to update curricula for the modern age. This bill reflects how students actually use data: across their whole education, not in a single elective. ADSA is proud to support it.”

“Too often, promising education investments go unmeasured, leaving us guessing about what actually works. The Data Science and Literacy Act gets this right by building evaluation into the bill from the start by directing the Institute of Education Sciences (IES) to rigorously assess grant effectiveness and requiring grantees to continuously monitor their own progress. That commitment to evidence, not just access, is exactly what we want to see in federal education investments,” Sara Schapiro, Executive Director of Alliance for Learning Innovation (ALI). “At the Alliance for Learning Innovation (ALI), we believe every student deserves the tools to make sense of data and put it to work solving real problems. We're proud to endorse this bipartisan legislation and thank Representatives Stevens, Beyer, Kim, and Baird for their leadership in building a stronger STEM pipeline for the next generation."

“H.G. Wells once said ‘Statistical thinking will one day be as necessary for efficient citizenship as the ability to read and write.’ (c. 1903) That day is today. This bill is the right step forward,” said Eddie Tchertchian, President of the American Mathematical Association of Two-Year Colleges (AMATYC).

“The presence of AI in our everyday lives and work has made statistical thinking more critical than ever, so I applaud Representative Stevens and her cosponsors for reintroducing this bill, " said Jeri Mulrow, President of the American Statistical Association (AmStat). “Statistical thinking, a core component of data literacy, is essential for today's students to effectively use AI, critically assess its outputs, and succeed in today's job market.”

“In continuing AMTE efforts to bring diverse mathematics teacher education communities together, our organization continues to support educators, coaches, consultants, specialists, and university and community college faculty to share and disseminate research, teaching, and community partnerships in different educational contexts,” said Farshid Safi, President of Association of Mathematics Teacher Educators (AMTE). “AMTE, intentionally and toward a more comprehensive and inclusive lens, adopts an expansive view of the term mathematics education to include intersections with fields such as data science and statistics education, mathematical modeling, STEM education while partnering with those engaged in early childhood, PK-12, and post-secondary contexts.”

“Data shapes the technologies students use, the decisions they encounter, and the world they will help create. The 2026 CSTA PK–12 Computer Science Standards identify Data & Analysis as a core concept in foundational computer science education, calling on students to use data to solve problems, make discoveries, and express ideas while critically examining its quality, representation, privacy, and impact,” said Bryan Twarek, Head of Research and Innovation of the Computer Science Teachers Association (CSTA). “The Data Science and Literacy Act would invest in the curricula, professional development, and partnerships teachers need to prepare their students to become critical consumers, responsible creators, and informed participants in a world powered by computing.”

“Data literacy is a foundational tool for real-world agency. Preparing students for a changing economy requires updating what and how we teach, moving away from narrow metrics of success to build practical skills across disciplines,” said Jean-Claude Brizard, Chief Executive Officer of Digital Promise. “The Data Science and Literacy Act delivers flexible resources that allow school systems and postsecondary partners to strengthen teacher capacity and create powerful learning experiences for every student. Digital Promise strongly supports this legislation as a crucial investment in long-term economic mobility.”

“Ensuring that data literacy is a foundational aspect of education is a cornerstone of the United States’ long-term economic and national security. Data is everywhere and the ideas and demands to create more of it, and the evermore complex ways to deploy it, are growing more significant by the day,” said Jeff Cohen, Chief External Affairs Officer at INFORMS. “This bill is a key part of addressing the substantial shortfall of STEM-prepared students for the workforce of tomorrow. Operations research, analytics, and the science and technology of decision-making is predicated on the sound and ethical use of data. INFORMS strongly supports the bipartisan Data Science and Literacy Act of 2026 and looks forward to working to ensure its passage and effective implementation.”

“Our students are graduating into a world where the ability to understand, interpret, and use data is no longer optional; it is essential. Science and STEM education provide powerful opportunities for students to develop these skills as they use data to ask questions and make sense of the world around them,” said Brianna Reilly Oliveira, Director of Professional Learning for the National Science Teaching Association. “NSTA strongly supports the Data Science and Literacy Act and its investment in educators and students. By equipping educators with the confidence, tools and strategies to integrate data literacy into science and STEM instruction, we can better prepare all students to thrive in a data-rich world.”

###
title: Rep. Haley Stevens Champions Bipartisan Data Science and Literacy Act to Prepare Students for Data-Driven Economy

Glen Cove, NY—Congressman Suozzi (D-NY) today joined Nassau County Legislature Minority Leader DeRiggi-Whitton (D-Glen Cove), Sea Cliff Mayor Elena Villafane, and local residents in Sea Cliff to announce the expansion of the Sea Cliff sewer system. The $6.5 million expansion will utilize more than $1.1 million in funds Congressman Suozzi secured in the FY2026 Community Project Funding grants. Nassau County Legislature Minority Leader Delia DeRiggi-Whitton secured an additional $4 million in bond authorization over the next two years to support the expansion of the sanitary sewer system in Sea Cliff, and local resources will cover the balance.

“This is a major accomplishment by Legislator DeRiggi-Whitton to help sewer critical areas in Sea Cliff and protect our precious Hempstead Harbor,” Congressman Suozzi said. “The continued success of Sea Cliff’s sewer expansion initiative is an outstanding illustration of what can be accomplished when all levels of government work collaboratively to solve problems for the communities we serve. I am excited to see how the $1 million in federal funding that I secured from the federal government has become a catalyst for millions more in County-level support spearheaded by Legislator DeRiggi-Whitton in partnership with Village leaders. This is transformational.”

The funds will be applied toward sewering a total of 2,860 linear feet on these streets:

• Prospect Avenue between Carpenter Avenue & Albin Street (900 linear feet, 20 service connections)

• Winding Way between 7th Avenue and Prospect Avenue (860 linear feet, 12 service connections)

• The Drive between Park Way and Carpenter Avenue (370 linear feet, five service connections)

• Park Way between 7th Avenue and Prospect Avenue (730 feet, eight service connections)

The forthcoming project will build upon previous work, completed during the summer of 2021, which sewered portions of Prospect, Maple, 12th, Sea Cliff, Summit, Central, 8th, and 7th Avenues, as well as all of Fairview Place. The expansion will also play a key role in the continued effort to clean up the Long Island Sound. By converting septic systems to sewer systems, this project will reduce nitrogen pollution into the Sound, helping impove the water quality of one of our nation’s great treasures.

Congressman Suozzi has long been a champion for protecting Long Island's environment, advocating for clean water, open space preservation, and investments that improve the health of the Long Island Sound, including delivering a 1000% increase in funding to improve the Long Island Sound since he came to Congress in 2017. His leadership has earned recognition from the New York League of Conservation Voters, which this year named him a Clean Water Champion for his decades-long commitment to safeguarding Long Island's water quality and securing federal support for critical environmental projects.

“Since Sea Cliff Village officials received their first funding for sewer expansion in 2014, Sea Cliff Avenue was our first area to focus on. Completing that was, in and of itself, a major accomplishment because it opened the doors for businesses to flourish and grow without having to consider the limitations of septic systems,” Minority Leader DeRiggi-Whitton said. “The fact remains that, of the 10 percent of Nassau County that is not sewered, about 90 percent falls within District 11, and that is why it was so important to pursue a vision that expands the initial project to connect additional streets to the gravity line that was completed five years ago. With critical support from Congressman Suozzi and this new County infrastructure funding, we are a major step closer to making those plans a reality.”

“This is exactly the kind of intergovernmental partnership that produces lasting results for our residents and our environment,” Sea Cliff Mayor Elena Villafane said. “Legislator Delia DeRiggi-Whitton’s success in securing $4 million in Nassau County capital funding, combined with Congressman Tom Suozzi’s $1 million commitment, brings us significantly closer to extending public sewers to areas of Sea Cliff that have relied on aging cesspools for generations. Protecting Hempstead Harbor is one of our highest priorities, and expanding sewer service is one of the most meaningful steps we can take toward that goal. On behalf of the Village, I thank Legislator DeRiggi-Whitton and Congressman Suozzi for investing in Sea Cliff’s future.”

###
title: Suozzi, Leader DeRiggi-Whitton, and Mayor Villafane Announce Expansion of Sea Cliff Sewer System

Rep. Torres Urges State Department to Press Honduras on Eviction and Prosecution of Garífuna Community
Today, Rep. Ritchie Torres (NY-15) sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging the State Department to press the Government of Honduras over the July 6, 2026 eviction of the Garífuna community of San Juan in Tela, Atlántida, and the criminal prosecution of five community members that followed.
On July 6, 2026, more than 200 Honduran National Police officers entered the San Juan community to clear land reportedly claimed by a hotel development. Officers deployed tear gas and live ammunition, and five members of the Black Fraternal Organization of Honduras (OFRANEH) were arrested. The five were released within hours but remain charged with aggravated usurpation of land within what they identify as their ancestral territory whose collective property rights the Inter-American Court of Human Rights affirmed in a binding 2023 judgment.
The letter notes that the operation appears to contravene the Honduran government’s own directive exempting Indigenous and Tribal lands from eviction enforcement, and raises concerns that two recently enacted Honduran laws, one broadening the legal definition of terrorist association and another shielding registered agro-industrial, tourism, and energy lands from legal claims, are being used together to convert land rights disputes into criminal prosecutions against community leaders.
Rep. Torres’s letter states that the matter is of direct concern to his constituents, as New York’s 15th Congressional District is home to one of the largest Garífuna diaspora communities in the United States, many of whom maintain family ties to San Juan, Triunfo de la Cruz, and neighboring communities.
The letter asks the State Department to urge Honduras to ensure the criminal proceedings against the five community members respect due process, to raise the apparent conflict between the eviction and Honduras’s own protections for Indigenous and Tribal land with Honduran authorities, to encourage full implementation of Inter-American Court judgments on Garífuna land rights, to confirm whether any Honduran security unit involved in the operation has received U.S. assistance or training, and to brief his office on the security situation facing Garífuna land defenders and on Embassy engagement to date. The letter requests a response within 30 days.
The full letter reads (PDF here):
“I write to express grave concern regarding the July 6, 2026 eviction of the Garífuna community of San Juan in Tela, Atlántida, Honduras, and the criminal prosecution of five community members that followed. I urge the Department to press the Government of Honduras to ensure that these proceedings are resolved consistent with due process and Honduras’s international obligations, to guarantee the safety of the affected families, and to comply with the binding judgments of the Inter-American Court of Human Rights concerning Garífuna ancestral territory.
“On July 6, 2026, a contingent of more than 200 Honduran National Police officers entered the San Juan community to carry out an eviction. According to press reports and human rights organizations, officers deployed tear gas and live ammunition, and five people were arrested. Police cited recently enacted legislation protecting agro-industrial and tourism land, and the property is reportedly claimed by a local hotel development. The five community members, all members of the Black Fraternal Organization of Honduras (OFRANEH), were released within hours but remain charged with aggravated usurpation of land within what they identify as their ancestral territory, the subject of the Inter-American Court’s 2023 judgment in the community’s favor.
“The five are Deinor Osmany Mejía Arzu, Irbin René López Cortes, Carlos Enrique Fernández Guzmán, Onil Rigoberto Hernández Zelaya, and Sara Abigail Acosta. On July 14, 2026, the trial court in Tela declined jurisdiction and transferred the case to the Juzgado de Letras con Competencia Territorial Nacional en Materia de Criminalidad Organizada in San Pedro Sula, reasoning that the San Juan community constituted an organized criminal structure. According to Honduran press reports, that court has since declared the proceedings null and void and returned the case to Tela, where, as of mid-August, no judge had been assigned to hear it. Two features of this case warrant the Department’s immediate attention.
“First, the operation appears to contravene the Honduran government’s own directive. Circular DGPN-(S/D)-No. 009-2026, reportedly issued by the National Police Directorate, instructs officers to act against illegal occupations but expressly exempts Indigenous and Tribal lands as defined under ILO Convention 169. San Juan is a Garífuna community whose collective property rights the Inter-American Court affirmed in 2023, and Decree 107-2026 itself provides in Article 1 that its provisions do not apply in recognized Indigenous and Tribal territories absent free, prior, and informed consultation under ILO Convention 169. I am not aware of any indication that such consultation took place before the eviction.
“Second, the eviction and prosecutions raise serious questions about Honduras’s compliance with rulings of the Inter-American Court of Human Rights. In its judgment of August 29, 2023, in Comunidad Garífuna de San Juan y sus miembros vs. Honduras, the Court found Honduras responsible for violating the community’s right to collective property and ordered specific reparations. Honduras has not fully implemented multiple Court judgments in favor of Garífuna communities, and in March 2026 the Court announced a fourth such judgment, in the case of Cayos Cochinos. These are binding obligations, not aspirational commitments.
“I am further concerned that these prosecutions form part of a broader pattern. Decree 84-2026, in force since May 22, 2026, amended Article 587 of the Honduran Penal Code to broaden the definition of terrorist association to include organizations that engage in territorial control or social dominance over communities through violence, intimidation, or coercion, even where the organization has a lawful purpose. Decree 107-2026, the Law for the Strengthening and Protection of the Agro-industrial Sector, Energy Projects, Tourism, Livestock, and Small Agricultural Producers, signed June 10, 2026 and published June 26, 2026, declares registered lands designated for those sectors immune from agrarian reform and other legal claims. The latter law also directs the Public Ministry and National Police to act immediately, including through evictions, against occupations of protected lands, and Honduran peasant organizations have denounced it as legalizing land dispossession. Applied together, these measures risk converting land rights disputes into criminal matters and placing community leaders at direct physical risk.
“This is a matter of direct concern to my constituents. New York’s 15th Congressional District is home to one of the largest Garífuna diaspora communities in the United States, many of whom maintain family ties to San Juan, Triunfo de la Cruz, and neighboring communities.
“I respectfully request that the Department:
1. Urge the Government of Honduras to ensure that the criminal proceedings against the five San Juan community members named above respect due process and Honduras’s international obligations, and to review whether usurpation charges are appropriate against residents of a community whose collective land rights the Inter-American Court has affirmed.
2. Raise directly with Honduran authorities the apparent inconsistency between the July 6 operation and both Circular DGPN-(S/D)-No. 009-2026 and Article 1 of Decree 107-2026, and seek assurances that no further evictions of Indigenous and Tribal territories will proceed without the consultation those provisions require.
3. Encourage the Government of Honduras to fully implement the Inter-American Court judgments concerning Garífuna land rights, including San Juan, Triunfo de la Cruz, Punta Piedra, and Cayos Cochinos.
4. Confirm whether any Honduran security unit involved in the July 6 operation has received United States assistance, training, or equipment, and describe what vetting has been conducted consistent with applicable law.
5. Provide a briefing to my office on the security situation facing Garífuna land defenders and on Embassy engagement to date.
“I appreciate your attention to this urgent matter and request a response within 30 days.”
title: Rep. Torres Urges State Department to Press Honduras on Eviction and Prosecution of Garífuna Community

Today, Representative Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12) attended a ribbon cutting celebrating the grand reopening of the renovated Reading Senior Center in Trenton, New Jersey and gave the following remarks:

When the senior center closed years ago, it was a tremendous loss to the Trenton senior community. The road to bring it back was a long one – and not without bumps along the way. But Mayor Reed, the City Council, and Mercer County were committed to serving the community and to getting this center back up and running… and better than it was before.

The city secured $600,000 in federal American Rescue Plan money, which I was proud to vote for, and it was signed by President Biden. In addition, the county secured matching Community Development Block Grants that I fought to protect from cuts in the Appropriations Committee.

The Reading Senior Center is a shining example of what can be accomplished when city, county, and federal officials work together, with one vision, to deliver for the seniors who have given so much to our city.

People have asked me, “What has been the most rewarding part of your time in Congress?” It’s days like this, when we can deliver results and give back to people who have put their hearts and souls into their communities.

The 11,000 square-foot facility will open its doors for the first time in over eight years, with its new operations and programs beginning Tuesday, September 15th. The Reading Senior Center will also become the new home of the City of Trenton Department of Health and Human Services’ Division of Community Relations and Social Services, beginning Wednesday, September 16, providing seniors with convenient access to City programs and assistance.
title: Rep. Watson Coleman Celebrates Grand Opening of Revitalized Reading Center for Trenton Community

Washington, DC - Today, Congressman Shri Thanedar (D-MI-13), along with Congressmen Wesley Bell (D-MO-01) and Mike Lawler (R-NY-17), introduced a bipartisan resolution recognizing September as “National Suicide Prevention Month” and September 10, 2026, as “World Suicide Prevention Day”. This resolution will bring awareness to the mental health battles that many face silently every day and decrease the stigma behind seeking treatment for mental illness.

“In 1996, I lost my first wife to her battle with mental illness,” said Congressman Shri Thanedar. The pain my young boys and I suffered was devastating and has stayed with me ever since. Her loss has inspired my work in Congress to ensure everyone has access to high-quality mental health care. By partnering in a bipartisan fashion with Representatives Bell and Lawler, we will bring awareness to this devastating issue and ensure that no more lives are lost to mental illness.”

"Suicide is an epidemic plaguing our youth that demands urgent attention, because behind every statistic is a family forever changed by a loss words can't capture," said Congressman Bell. "In Missouri and across the nation, too many people are suffering in silence, believing they have nowhere to turn. National Suicide Prevention Month is about changing that. We must meet this crisis head-on by investing in mental health care, breaking down the stigma that keeps people from asking for help, and making clear that reaching out is a sign of strength, not weakness. Mental health is health, and no one should have to face their darkest moments alone. If you're struggling, help is always within reach — call or text 988."

“Suicide is a devastating public health crisis, but it is not inevitable. We have a responsibility to ensure that people who are struggling know they are not alone and have access to the mental health care and support they need. During National Suicide Prevention Month and on World Suicide Prevention Day, we must recommit ourselves to breaking the stigma around mental health, expanding access to care, and doing everything we can to prevent the loss of another life,” said Congressman Mike Lawler (NY-17).

This resolution is supported by a broad range of mental health stakeholders, including the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention, saying “Suicide is the 10th leading cause of death in the United States, with nearly 49,000 Americans dying by suicide in 2024 and an estimated 2.2 million suicide attempts,” said Laurel Stine, J.D., M.A., Executive Vice President and Chief Policy and Advocacy Officer at the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention (AFSP). “AFSP commends Representatives Thanedar, Bell, and Lawler for introducing this bipartisan resolution recognizing September as National Suicide Prevention Month and September 10 as World Suicide Prevention Day. By raising awareness about suicide and the critical need to expand access to quality mental health, substance use, and suicide prevention services and care, we can help save lives and create a future where everyone has the support and resources they need to thrive.”

Another supporter, the National Alliance on Mental Illness, said the following about Thanedar’s resolution: “Every life lost to suicide is a tragedy, and every effort to prevent suicide must begin with ensuring people have access to the mental health care and support they need," said Hannah Wesolowski, Chief Advocacy Officer at the National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI). “National Suicide Prevention Month and World Suicide Prevention Day are important opportunities to raise awareness, spread hope, and spark meaningful action. NAMI thanks Rep. Thanedar for recognizing suicide prevention as a national priority.”

Congressman Shri Thanedar proudly represents Michigan's 13th Congressional District, which includes Detroit, Downriver, and the Grosse Pointes. As a champion for working families, Shri is committed to advancing economic opportunities, education, healthcare access, and entrepreneurship for underserved communities. Drawing from his journey from poverty to success, he works tirelessly to uplift Metro Detroit, ensuring every resident has the resources and support they need to thrive.

###
title: Congressman Shri Thanedar Leads Bipartisan Resolution Designating September as National Suicide Prevention Month

Lawmakers: “We write with urgent concern about the life-threatening conditions facing Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, a Palestinian pediatrician being badly mistreated in Israeli custody.”

Netanyahu’s government has filed no formal charges against Dr. Abu Safiya, nor has he received a trial.

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03), and Congressman Raul Ruiz, M.D. (CA-25), led 69 of their colleagues in calling on U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to engage his counterparts in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government to secure the release of imprisoned Palestinian pediatrician Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya. The lawmakers emphasized the lack of due process afforded to Dr. Abu Safiya, who has yet to receive formal charges, and highlighted his worsening physical condition.

“We write with urgent concern about the life-threatening conditions facing Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, a Palestinian pediatrician being badly mistreated in Israeli custody,” the lawmakers wrote. “As recently as last month, Dr. Abu Safiya’s lawyer warned that his physical condition had deteriorated to the point of near-death.”

Dr. Abu Safiya is the longtime director of Kamal Adwan hospital in Gaza City. During the war in Gaza, he played a critical role in providing wounded civilians with vital medical care. Among his most notable contributions was the construction of a malnutrition unit that treated hundreds of children.

On December 27, 2024, Dr. Abu Safiya was arrested while on duty at his hospital and remains in Israeli custody. No formal charges were ever presented against him, and to this day, he has yet to receive a trial.

“For over 18 months, Dr. Abu Safiya has languished in Israeli jails, including an underground facility previously shut down due to the poor conditions its detainees faced,” the lawmakers continued. “According to his lawyer, authorities have repeatedly denied him adequate access to medical care, food and toiletries, causing him to lose significant weight.”

On July 2, 2026, Dr. Abu Safiya’s lawyer visited him in jail and found that the severity of his injuries had rendered him nearly unrecognizable. His body bore fresh bruises, and he struggled to remain conscious. The lawmakers urged Secretary Rubio to do everything in the Trump Administration’s power to free Dr. Abu Safiya before he dies in custody.

The letter is cosigned in the House by 66 Members.

The letter is cosigned in the Senate by 3 Senators.
title: Dexter, Ruiz Condemn Lack of Due Process for Imprisoned Palestinian Pediatrician Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya and Demand His Release by Netanyahu’s Government

Yesterday, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries spoke to reporters following a roundtable in Denver with Assistant Democratic Leader Joe Neguse (CO-02), local elected officials and members of the Greater Metro Denver Ministerial Alliance about how House Democrats are united in the fight to make life better for everyday Americans and reverse the toxic policies of Donald Trump and extreme MAGA Republicans. Below are excerpts of his remarks during the gaggle and the roundtable.

LEADER JEFFRIES ON THE ROUNDTABLE: We had a wonderful, thoughtful, powerful conversation with the Denver Ministerial Alliance as well as elected officials and community leaders. We discussed a host of issues, including a lot of the challenges that relate to the extremism that’s been unleashed on the people of Colorado and this nation by the Trump administration, including the cuts to Medicaid and SNAP, the attacks on healthcare, the out-of-control ICE activity and the assault on voting rights. I look forward to continuing to stay in close touch with the leadership here in Denver, in the greater Denver area and beyond. San Diego, CA — Today, Representative Scott Peters (CA-50) released the following statement after San Diego Unified School District (SDUSD) and San Diego City College both informed the Congressman's office of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrest activity outside their schools within the past week:

"I am deeply troubled by reports that students and parents were detained without warning while trying to attend classes or bring kids to school. Schools are supposed to be a safe place for young people to learn. Yet this Administration exploits the places we trust most—schools, childcare facilities, hospitals, courthouses, and places of worship. President Trump has turned these places into hunting grounds.

“ICE isn’t going after the 'worst of the worst,' as President Trump promised. We saw this at Buona Forchetta, when ICE agents threw the owner against a wall, handcuffed employees, and used flash-bang grenades on bystanders. These people weren't drug lords or violent criminals; they were workers trying to make a living.

“Parents and children should not have to worry about ICE agents waiting outside a classroom or a doctor's office. That's why I led introduction of the Protecting Sensitive Locations Act, which would bar immigration enforcement within 1,000 feet of schools, hospitals, and churches except in true emergencies. I will also continue working with SDUSD and City College to make sure San Diegans have the resources they need to stay informed and protected.

"Until ICE operates responsibly and reasonably to target dangerous criminals instead of hardworking families, I will push for real reforms from ICE and hold them accountable for the fear they have inflicted on my constituents and communities across the country. I urge all state and local elected officials to express their support for the Protecting Sensitive Locations Act and my Stop Excessive Force in Immigration Act so we can deliver commonsense reforms that keep our communities safe."

Background:

Last year, Rep. Peters led the Stop Excessive Force in Immigration Act, a bill to make our communities safer by establishing a stronger standard for Federal immigration agents' use of force. The bill would also restrict use of crowd munitions like tear gas and create greater transparency in enforcement by requiring the use of body cameras and strictly limiting the use of masks. Rep. Peters has pushed Congress to pass these common sense reforms, but they have been blocked by the Republican majority.

New York, NY - U.S. Representative Dan Goldman (NY-10) presented the Kings County District Attorney’s Office with a $354,000 Community Project funding award. The award will be used to bolster the Outreach and Assistance Response (SOAR) program. The program is designed to conduct immediate outreach to violent crime victims and their families.

Rep. Goldman requested and secured funding for the project, which was included in a package of bills to fund the federal government. Goldman secured $13,756,000 for 15 community projects in NY-10 in the FY 2026 appropriations process.

Rep. Goldman presented the award to Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez.

“Violent crime often leaves lasting trauma for victims and their families, who benefit greatly from immediate assistance,” said Congressman Dan Goldman. “I am proud to have secured $354,000 to fund the Kings County District Attorney’s Office’s program that does just that – from financial help to mental health assistance.. Thank you to District Attorney Gonzalez for his leadership on this issue to provide Brooklyn families with the respect and care they deserve."

Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez said, “While Brooklyn is experiencing a public safety renaissance with historic lows in homicides and shootings, there are still too many families dealing with the trauma of a shooting, an assault or the loss of a loved one. And even when there has not yet been an arrest or a criminal case, victims and families may need immediate support. The new SOAR program will offer just that and fill gaps that traditional compensation programs cannot always cover, allowing our counselors to assist and stand with every victim of serious violence and their families. I am grateful for Congressman Dan Goldman who secured the grant that will allow us to launch this important initiative.”

Kings County District Attorney’s SOAR (Support Outreach and Assistance Response) conducts outreach and provides support to victims of violent assaults and homicides regardless of whether anyone has been arrested for the crime. Typically the victim’s services staff in a DA’s office only comes into contact with a victim once an arrest has been made and a case generated. The SOAR team responds to violent crimes even when there is no case in the DA’s office. The response team provides assistance with victim compensation, counseling, and relevant case related information. The SOAR team also engages in community outreach to inform the public of KCDA’s services and commitment to public safety.

Immediately following a violent incident or homicide, usually within the first 24 to 48 hours, SOAR counselors work with the NYC Police Department to obtain contact information of survivors or surviving family members. In cases where other agencies or organizations, such as the offices of elected officials or community-based organizations, have already had contact with the victim or family, SOAR counselors work with those agencies to ensure a warm handoff from those organizations to our experts in trauma, crime victim’s rights, and criminal justice.

The funds will assist with building the SOAR team by covering the salary for a program coordinator and four new staff members dedicated to the program.

###
title: Congressman Dan Goldman Presents $354,000 Grant Award to Kings County District Attorney’s Office

Washington, DC – Today, Rep. Frank J. Mrvan sent a letter to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) requesting an investigation into the power outages following the derecho that struck Northwest Indiana on August 11, 2026.

The text of the letter is below and a pdf is available here.

“I write to request that the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), in coordination with the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC), conduct a comprehensive federal review of the widespread and prolonged power outages that followed the severe weather event, a derecho, that struck Northwest Indiana on August 11, 2026.

“The derecho brought extraordinary straight-line winds across Northern Indiana, with peak wind gusts reaching approximately 100 to 110 miles per hour across portions of Lake and Porter Counties. The storm caused unprecedented damage and resulted in nearly 375,000 customer outages within Northern Indiana Public Service Company’s (NIPSCO) service territory. Tens of thousands of Northwest Indiana residents remained without electricity for nearly two weeks. This was the largest outage event in NIPSCO’s history and far exceeded the average duration of electricity interruptions associated with major events. The Cities of Gary, Lake Station, and Portage, as well as the Town of Munster, were among the hardest hit communities and the last areas to receive full restoration.

“The consequences of these prolonged outages were significant. Families lost food, homes experienced flooding and subsequent mold growth, businesses lost inventory and revenue, and residents lost access to essential medical equipment and prescription medications. For many constituents, the lack of electricity also meant the loss of reliable access to phones, computers, internet service, and other means of communicating with family members, reporting outages, and applying for emergency assistance.

“Most concerning, vulnerable residents were left without reliable access to medical care and other essential services. For nearly two weeks, too many Northwest Indiana families were literally left in the dark.

“On August 25, 2026, a federal Major Disaster Declaration was approved for Indiana, providing critical assistance as communities begin the long process of recovery. However, federal assistance must address not only the damage caused by this storm, but also what can be learned from the unprecedented duration of the resulting power outages.

“The Indiana Office of Utility Consumer Counselor has petitioned the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission (IURC) to investigate NIPSCO’s storm restoration practices, and I strongly support that state-level investigation. At the same time, given the scale of this event, I believe a federal review is warranted.

“I respectfully request a joint FERC-NERC investigation to assess what contributed to the prolonged outages and determine whether NIPSCO’s preparation, system performance, and restoration efforts were consistent with applicable reliability requirements and best practices. I also request that the findings include recommendations to improve electric-grid reliability and storm resilience.

“Specifically, I ask that the investigation examine whether NIPSCO and its parent company, NiSource, complied with FERC-approved federal reliability standards and whether any deficiencies in reliability planning, system resilience, or emergency response warrant additional federal action. The review should evaluate the following factors:

Storm preparedness: The short- and long-term preparations NIPSCO undertook before the August 11 derecho, including emergency response planning, staffing, equipment, mutual-aid arrangements, and pre-positioning of resources.

Grid resilience and system design: The performance and resilience of NIPSCO’s distribution and transmission infrastructure in the face of extreme straight-line winds and increasingly severe weather events.

Vegetation management and maintenance: The adequacy and effectiveness of routine maintenance and vegetation-management practices, particularly considering the significant investments NIPSCO has reported making in these areas.

Restoration performance: The causes of the prolonged restoration timeline, including why certain communities remained without power substantially longer than others and whether restoration priorities, resource allocation, communications, and repair practices were appropriate.

Regional comparison: NIPSCO’s restoration performance compared with other electric utilities in Indiana and the surrounding region that experienced outages from the same weather event.

Infrastructure investments: Whether the substantial investments NIPSCO has made in recent years toward infrastructure replacement, grid modernization, reliability, and vegetation management have produced the adequate levels of resilience.

“This last point deserves particular scrutiny. NIPSCO has emphasized that recent rate increases are necessary to support infrastructure upgrades and improve grid reliability. Since 2016, customers have contributed approximately $2.3 billion toward infrastructure replacement, and $81 million towards vegetation management between 2023 and 2025. Given the magnitude of these investments, Northwest Indiana residents deserve to know why they experienced outages of this magnitude and duration, and whether additional investments, preparation, maintenance, or changes in reliability standards could have reduced the impact on families and businesses.

“I appreciate your consideration of this request and your commitment to ensuring the reliability and resilience of our nation’s electric grid. I also request that FERC coordinate, as appropriate, with the IURC, NIPSCO, state emergency-management officials, and other relevant stakeholders to implement the lessons learned from this event. I stand ready to work together to advance transparency and accountability, strengthen our electric infrastructure, and ensure that Northwest Indiana families and businesses can depend on safe, reliable, and affordable power.”

###
title: Mrvan Requests Federal Investigation into NWI Power Outages

MEDIA ADVISORY: Select Committee and Congressional Executive Commission on China Ranking Members to Hold Joint Shadow Hearing on Human Rights in China Ahead of Xi’s Visit to Washington
WASHINGTON – Ranking Member Ro Khanna of the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) and Ranking Member Jim McGovern of the Congressional-Executive Commission on China will jointly hold a shadow hearing titled The Void in China Policy: Why Human Rights Must Be on Trump’s Agenda with Xi at the White House. The hearing will be held on Tuesday, September 15 at 3:30 P.M. in HVC-215.
The Chinese government’s human rights abuses have traditionally attracted bipartisan concern in Congress—resulting in the passage of recent legislation such as the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act, which was signed into law by President Biden in December 2021, as well as the creation of bipartisan panels like the Select Committee and the Congressional-Executive Commission on China.
Unfortunately, the Trump Administration’s disregard for human rights in China and assault on organizations advocating for human rights has jeopardized bipartisan support for U.S. human rights policy. President Trump has praised Xi Jinping’s abysmal human rights record and carried virtually no human rights agenda to Beijing during his visit in May—other than a request to free two wrongfully imprisoned individuals, only one of whom was released. The Administration has also slashed funding and eliminated grants for China human rights organizations, reduced human rights staffing at the State Department, and sought to eliminate entities that empower human rights defenders in China, such as the National Endowment for Democracy and Radio Free Asia.
Hearing witnesses will discuss the state of human rights in China and provide an assessment of and recommendations for U.S. human rights policy.
The following witnesses will provide testimony:
- Tahir Imin, Founder and Director, Uyghur Post
- Palden Gyal, President, International Tibet Media Organization
- Yaqiu Wang, Fellow at the Penn Project on the Future of U.S.-China Relations at the University of Pennsylvania
- Jonathan Stivers, U.S. Director, Committee for Freedom in Hong Kong; Commissioner, U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission
When: Tuesday, September 15 at 3:30 P.M.
Where: U.S. Capitol Visitor Center, HVC-215
A livestream of the hearing will be available here.
Members of the media planning to attend should RSVP to Julia.Snodgrass@mail.house.gov and Matt.Bonaccorsi@mail.house.gov

ATLANTA, G.A. — Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) announced that Atlanta Public Schools has received $700,000 in congressionally directed spending to support future community schoolyard projects in Atlanta.

Congresswoman Williams joined Atlanta Public Schools and Trust for Public Land leaders to celebrate the new federal investment, which will help transform school grounds into vibrant outdoor spaces that support student learning and recreation while expanding neighborhood access to green space beyond the school day.

Congresswoman Nikema Williams said:

“As a proud APS mama, I know how much it means for our children to have places where they can learn, play, explore and just be kids. These projects aren’t just playgrounds and outdoor spaces. They support outdoor education, build climate resilience, connect us to nature and improve park equity — because all children deserve a safe and accessible place to play, no matter their ZIP code or bank account.”

The Schoolyards Program is a national initiative of Trust for Public Land designed to expand community access to schoolyards during non-school hours and increase the percentage of people who live within a 10-minute walk of a park. In Atlanta, the program is implemented in partnership with APS, other non-profit organizations, and city agencies, with additional support from the philanthropic community.

George Dusenbury, Georgia State Director of Trust for Public Lands said:

“Community schoolyards are one of the smartest ways we can expand access to green space in Atlanta neighborhoods. This federal investment will help Atlanta Public Schools create places that support students during the school day and serve families and neighbors after hours, ensuring more Atlantans have safe, high-quality places to play, learn and gather.”

In Atlanta, 18 percent of residents still do not live within a 10-minute walk of a park. Over the past six years, TPL has worked with 14 Atlanta schools to redesign schoolyards so they can serve as parks during non-school hours. The first campus selected for this phase is Crawford W. Long Middle School in the Glenrose Heights neighborhood of South Atlanta. Additional details on sites and timelines will be announced as planning moves forward.

Dr. Bryan Johnson, APS Superintendent said:

“At Atlanta Public Schools, we know schools are more than buildings; they are spaces where lifelong memories are made. This project allows us to welcome all of our neighbors to create memories, friendships, and strong bonds right here on our schoolyards. By transforming these spaces into vibrant, welcoming places for play, learning, and connection, we are strengthening the relationship between our schools and the communities they serve. We are proud to partner with the Trust for Public Land to create schoolyards that are truly for everyone.”

PROVIDENCE, RI – In an effort to investigate and expose the Trump Administration’s blatant and unwarranted politicization of federal disaster aid, Rhode Island’s Congressional delegation sent a letter to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) demanding answers and the preservation of records and documentation related to Rhode Island’s request for a major disaster declaration for the historic February 2026 blizzard.

Despite the fact that damage from the blizzard far surpassed FEMA’s threshold for federal assistance, the Trump Administration unfairly denied the state’s request and brazenly rejected appeals from Rhode Island and other ‘Blue states’ that requested a Major Disaster Declaration.

Between February 22-23, 2026, Rhode Island was struck by a record-breaking blizzard that dumped 37.9 inches of snow in a 24-hour period and the state experienced wind gusts of 74 miles per hour. The winter storm hit Rhode Island with the intensity of a Category 2 hurricane, caused severe power outages for tens of thousands of Rhode Islanders, and tragically resulted in two fatalities and hundreds of emergency room visits. The storm created immense challenges for local businesses, which faced prolonged closures due to storm-related damage and disruptions to transportation, utilities, and public services.

In the aftermath of the blizzard, Rhode Island officials worked directly with FEMA to document over $19 million in direct storm damages eligible for federal reimbursement.

Pointing out that the Trump Administration still has yet to provide Rhode Island with a written, detailed explanation for why the state’s request was denied despite exceeding FEMA’s thresholds for assistance, U.S. Senators Jack Reed and Sheldon Whitehouse and U.S. Representatives Seth Magaziner and Gabe Amo wrote to the executive branch:

“The facts could not be clearer. This storm was not typical winter weather; indeed, the National Weather Service confirmed snowfall totals that exceeded the historical 1-day snowfall records in all five Rhode Island counties. Downplaying this devastating blizzard as just “winter weather” is an insult to those whose lives and businesses were upended by the historic blizzard.”

The lawmakers note a cache of documents has already been obtained by Politico -- Trump overrode his own agencies to deny 4 Democratic disaster requests – that exposes partisan retribution. Politico notes: “President Donald Trump overruled his own agencies when he denied disaster aid for four Democratic-led states this month.

“Emails between state and federal officials obtained by POLITICO along with more than 150 pages of documents submitted to FEMA by three states — New Jersey, Massachusetts and Rhode Island — provide new details about Trump’s low rate of approving disaster aid for his political adversaries.”

Full text of the letter follows:

Dear Secretary Mullin and Administrator Hamilton:

We write to request that you immediately preserve and provide all Department of Homeland Security documentation related to Rhode Island’s request for a major disaster declaration under the Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act for its February 2026 blizzard.

Between February 22-23, 2026, Rhode Island was struck by a record-breaking blizzard that produced up to 37.9 inches of snow – its highest one-day snowfall on record – and up to 74-mile-per-hour winds. The storm hit the state with the intensity of a Category 2 hurricane, caused severe power outages, and tragically resulted in two fatalities and hundreds of emergency room visits. The State of Rhode Island worked with expert officials from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to develop a joint Preliminary Damage Assessment, which was submitted on April 7, 2026 with the state’s request and found over $19 million in validated damages – more than nine times the threshold required for disaster assistance.

To date, FEMA has not provided Rhode Island officials with a written, detailed explanation for why the state’s request was denied despite exceeding FEMA’s thresholds for assistance. However, on September 3, 2026, Administrator Hamilton, referencing the Administration’s denials for assistance to Rhode Island, New York, New Jersey, and Massachusetts, posted on X: “Winter weather is not new to the Northeast. Federal disaster aid is not a backstop for routine state & local budgeting.”

The facts could not be clearer. This storm was not typical winter weather; indeed, the National Weather Service confirmed snowfall totals that exceeded the historical 1-day snowfall records in all five Rhode Island counties. Downplaying this devastating blizzard as just “winter weather” is an insult to those whose lives and businesses were upended by the historic blizzard.

Given the lack of a detailed, written explanation and Administrator Hamilton’s flippant claim that the blizzard’s impact was a failure of state and local budgeting, we request that you immediately preserve and provide all communications and records, including those with other agencies, the President, and others at the White House, relating to FEMA’s evaluation of Rhode Island’s disaster request. If you fail to preserve and provide this information, it is only reasonable to assume that claim is entirely without merit.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this important matter.

###
title: RI Delegation Opens Probe into Trump Politicizing Disaster Relief

WASHINGTON, DC — Last week, Representative Marie Gluesenkamp Perez attended a hearing held by the House Committee on Rules to advocate for changes to House rules for next Congress. She urged the committee to enact a number of reforms within the U.S. House of Representatives. Among these reforms were an effort to create cognitive standards for members of the House, to form a Select Committee to explore Electoral Reform options, allow for remote committee testimonies, and to expand the code of conduct to ban Members of Congress from sleeping with House staff.

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez testifies in front of the Rules Committee

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez opened her testimony asking committee members to consider the adoption of her BRIDGE to Congress Resolution to allow remote witness testimony at Congressional hearings. The Congresswoman noted that for too long everyday people and people who live far from the Capitol face significant burdens in coming to DC to speak in front of their representatives. This provision hopes to bring local issues into committee spotlights and reduce the influence of lobbyists and paid policy professionals.

“For a constituent in Southwest Washington, testifying in person can mean taking time off work, finding child or elder care, and paying for a plane ticket and hotel in Washington, D.C. Most working families I know simply can’t afford that,” said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez, “The result is a witness pool that lacks geographic, economic, and lived-experience diversity. Instead of hearing directly from a fisherman in Pacific County or a shop teacher in Skamania County, Congress gets a feedback-loop from people paid to discuss policy. That leads to bad policy and erodes public trust.”

The Congresswoman continued her testimony by urging the adoption of her resolution establishing a bipartisan Select Committee on Electoral Reform. Throughout her time in congress, Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez has pursued options for making Congress a more representative body to the average American. The Electoral Reform Select Committee Act was the first piece of legislation she introduced in the 119th Congress. If formed, the bipartisan Select Committee would investigate options such as multi-member districts with proportional representation, expanding the House, and independent redistricting commissions to improve the responsibility members of Congress have to their constituents.

“Regardless of party or ideology, more and more Americans feel that our democracy isn’t working for them. Americans feel unrepresented and are losing faith in a government that they view as unreflective of their communities and values.” Said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez, “As Members of Congress, we need to take a step back, reexamine how we got here, and work toward what we can do to fix it.”

Video of the Congresswoman’s remarks can be found here:

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez continued her testimony by reminding the committee that accountability and trust in Congress demands they take action on the instances of sexual misconduct that have plagued this Congress.

“This is about trust, accountability, and not giving powerful people a free pass to continue perpetuating a culture of sexual assault and misconduct. Americans deserve to know that their elected officials are held to high standards–and that their representatives are hellbent on making this institution work better for the American people,” Said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez, “As members, we are here to work – not date. The next rules package should include a code of conduct that prohibits Members of Congress from having sexual relationships with House staff, no matter where that staffer works—whether in another Member’s personal office, a committee, or a caucus.”

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez ended her testimony by once again raising her mental acuity standards provision to her colleagues in the House. She has made repeated efforts to urge the Office of Congressional Conduct to create a standard of conduct as it relates to members suffering from significant and irreversible cognitive decline. Recently she offered this provision in the Appropriations Committee as an amendment to the Legislative Branch Appropriations Act. The amendment failed overwhelmingly, with Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez casting the only yes vote on the entire committee.

“Americans elect Members of Congress to be their voice in Washington, and that responsibility comes with a clear standard of conduct. Clause 1 of Rule XXIII of the Rules of the House requires Members to ‘behave at all times in a manner that shall reflect creditably on the House.’” Said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez, “When a Member is no longer able to fulfill the responsibilities of the office because of a significant and irreversible cognitive impairment, and unelected staff are effectively running the office on that Member’s behalf, we have to establish a process to evaluate and address it.”
