CHICAGO — Today, Congressmembers Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Mike Quigley (IL-05), and Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), joined by a coalition of local elected officials including State Senator Celina Villanueva, State Representative Edgar Gonzalez Jr, Cook County Commissioner Alma Anaya, Alderperson Michael Rodriguez, Alderperson Jessie Fuentes, and immigration advocacy organizations, including Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights (ICIRR), Brighton Park Neighborhood Council (BPNC), Organized Communities Against Deportations (OCAD) and The Resurrection Project (TRP), held a press conference to mark one year of resistance to Operation Midway Blitz.

The coalition called for action on immigration reform, including by forcing a vote on the Dream and Promise Act, and demanded full accountability from local and federal authorities, including the Cook County State’s Attorney, for the brutality and terror inflicted by the federal government’s immigration enforcement actions on communities throughout the region.

“A year ago, the Trump administration tried to break us and take away our dignity by sending masked federal agents into our city through Operation Midway Blitz. They failed, and instead our community came together, stood up and challenged their abuse of power,” said Congressman Jesús “Chuy” García. “One year later, we are more united than ever. But the fight is not over. Masked federal agents continue to operate in our neighborhoods, and we will keep demanding that they leave and that those responsible for their crimes be held accountable. Most importantly, we will continue fighting for meaningful immigration reform so that no community has to endure the failures of our broken immigration system again.”

"We are commemorating the one-year anniversary of Midway Blitz, when the Department of Homeland Security began a campaign of terror in Chicago. Those of us who lived through its terror are clear: DHS REMAINS the biggest threat to our collective safety," said Congresswoman Delia Ramirez. "As we regain the majority next year, our grief, our anger, and our calls for justice must move us to action that honors all those stolen from us by DHS, by holding EVERY fascist who has permitted and profited from DHS’s violence accountable, by abolishing ICE, and by dismantling DHS."

"Donald Trump's Operation Midway Blitz had one goal and one goal only: to terrorize Chicago. ICE and CBP agents didn't go after the worst of the worst, they kidnapped people off the streets, tear gassed elementary schools, and killed a father of two," said Congressman Mike Quigley. "Unfortunately, the horror of Trump's immigration policies didn't end with Operation Midway Blitz. Just last month, I attended a deportation hearing where I saw children in court without their parents, facing a language barrier, and being asked to explain why they deserve to stay in this country. This cruelty must be stopped. I'm more committed than ever to working with my colleagues and advocates to protect our immigrant neighbors and stop Trump’s DHS in its tracks before they can do any more harm."

“One year after Operation Midway Blitz, we remember the harm caused by this authoritarian operation, but we also honor the faith leaders, community organizers, attorneys, educators, and ordinary Chicagoans who stepped up to protect their neighbors and defend the values that make our city strong,” said Congressman Jonathan Jackson. “I will continue to demand accountability for the abuses inflicted on immigrants and our communities. I stand with my Congressional colleagues in renewing our call for comprehensive immigration reform rooted in the fundamental belief that every person deserves dignity, equity, and due process.”

“This week marks the one-year anniversary of Operation Midway Blitz, and Chicago residents are still reeling from the horrors our communities have been forced to face, as masked officers continue to wreak havoc across our city by taking countless residents into custody and dismantling families left and right,” said State Senator Celina Villanueva. “Since the operation was launched last September, Latino communities, especially those I represent, have lived in constant fear – afraid of leaving their homes and sending their children to school. After a year of brutalizing protestors, patrolling city streets, raiding our neighborhoods and harming our residents, it is far beyond time to demand accountability and justice from this administration, not only for Latino Illinoisans but also for everyone who has been impacted by these senseless acts of hate.”

“Operation Midway Blitz did not break our community, it strengthened our resolve. For a year, our immigrant families, neighbors, and community organizations have stood together against fear and intimidation. We will continue to defend every family and protect the welcoming spirit that defines our community,” said 22 Ward Alderperson Michael D. Rodriguez.

“Whether it be the apartment raids in South Shore, the shooting of Marimar Martinez in Brighton Park, or the murder of Silverio Villegas González, it’s been proven that ICE does NOT keep us safe - they are designed to intimidate communities of color and deport as many people as possible…Local leaders and politicians must stand with immigrants and enforce the laws and policies our communities fought for to make Illinois a welcoming place for all, said Lawrence Benitio, Executive Director, ICIRR.

“Operation Midway Blitz isn’t over - we’re still reeling from the impact of thousands of neighbors being stripped from our community. Families separated. Jobs lost. Communities destabilized. Yet, through it all, our community keeps showing up and fighting back. We refuse to let this terror be normalized,” said Any Huamami, Director of Organizing, Brighton Park Neighborhood Council.

“On this day, last year our communities were being terrorized by masked agents, kidnapped without explanation, and families have been forcibly broken by this federal administration’s immigration enforcement campaign. Last year showed us we were all at risk of being detained only based on what we look like. Unlawful arrests became the norm, but we are still here exposing those actions and reminding people that ICE is still in our communities. It is our duty to continue to be vigilant and protect each other,” said Antonio Gutierrez, Co-Founder and Strategic Coordinator, Organized Communities Against Deportations.

“Chicago's Northwest Side was one of the concentration points for Operation Midway Blitz. Local community members came together to fight back against this attack on our community as part of the statewide network of rapid responders anchored by ICIRR. Our work did not end when Midway Blitz concluded. We continue to see daily ICE abductions and assaults in our neighborhoods to this day. Community members will continue doing their part to keep us safe. It is now long overdue for police departments locally to do their job, and investigate the actions of these agents, so we can hold them to account. It's the least that our community members and neighbors who were tear gassed, pepper sprayed and faced assault and aggression from the federal government deserve,” said Pastor Juan Pablo Herrera, Board President, PLSNA.

“The fear that swept through our communities is real, but this year wasn’t defined by fear, but by the beauty and resilience of our community. The Trump administration set out to make an example of Chicago. Instead, we led by example—building a statewide coordinated response that has connected tens of thousands of community members to legal support, and a rapid response network that shows that immigrants across Illinois never stand alone, said Eréndira Rendón, Vice President of Immigrant Justice, The Resurrection Project.

WASHINGTON, DC — Como parte de su agenda para priorizar lo básico y atender la crisis de agua en Puerto Rico, el Comisionado Residente, Pablo José Hernández, solicitó al Senado que mantenga en la versión final de la legislación federal de infraestructura de agua varios proyectos y prioridades para Puerto Rico que ya fueron aprobados por la Cámara de Representantes.

Las prioridades ya están incluidas en la versión de la Ley de Desarrollo de Recursos Hídricos, conocida como el Water Resources Development Act (WRDA) de 2026 de la Cámara de Representantes, que avanzó en comité, y Hernández está trabajando para que se mantengan durante las negociaciones con el Senado y lleguen a la versión final.

“Mi agenda de priorizar lo básico se trata de conseguir resultados en los problemas que afectan a nuestra gente todos los días. Puerto Rico necesita mejor infraestructura de agua, comunidades más protegidas de las inundaciones y acción para nuestras costas. Ya estamos avanzando estas prioridades en la Cámara y ahora estoy trabajando para asegurar que lleguen a la meta,” expresó el Comisionado Residente.

Entre las medidas que el Comisionado Residente busca asegurar se encuentran hasta $75 millones para proyectos de infraestructura de agua y ambiental en Puerto Rico, $10 millones para agua y alcantarillado en Corozal y nuevos estudios de impacto para el proyecto de control de inundaciones del Río Puerto Nuevo en San Juan, de manera que se puedan atender las preocupaciones de las comunidades aledañas.

También está defendiendo nuevos estudios para proyectos de control de inundaciones, protección costera y daños por tormentas en Ceiba, Fajardo, Loíza, Naguabo, Humacao, Vega Baja y Yabucoa.

###

Rep. Hernández Pushes Water Projects for Puerto Rico

Resident Commissioner seeks to secure projects for Corozal, San Juan, and seven municipalities as part of his agenda to prioritize the basics

WASHINGTON, DC — As part of his agenda to prioritize the basics and address the water crisis in Puerto Rico, Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández asked the Senate to maintain, in the final version of federal water infrastructure legislation, several projects and priorities for Puerto Rico that have already been approved by the House of Representatives.

The priorities are already included in the House version of the Water Resources Development Act, known as the 2026 Water Resources Development Act (WRDA), which advanced in committee, and Hernández is working to ensure they remain during negotiations with the Senate and make it into the final version.

“My agenda to prioritize the basics is about delivering results on the problems that affect our people every day. Puerto Rico needs better water infrastructure, communities better protected from flooding, and action for our coasts. We are already advancing these priorities in the House, and now I am working to make sure they reach the finish line,” said the Resident Commissioner.

Among the measures the Resident Commissioner seeks to secure are up to $75 million for water and environmental infrastructure projects in Puerto Rico, $10 million for water and sewer infrastructure in Corozal, and new impact studies for the Río Puerto Nuevo flood control project in San Juan, so that the concerns of neighboring communities can be addressed.

He is also advocating for new studies for flood control, coastal protection, and storm damage projects in Ceiba, Fajardo, Loíza, Naguabo, Humacao, Vega Baja, and Yabucoa.
title: Comisionado Impulsa Proyectos de Agua para Puerto Rico.

Washington D.C. - New Dem Members hosted a roundtable with housing policy experts and industry representatives to solicit ideas on what Congress’s next steps should be to address the affordable housing crisis. New Dem Housing, Infrastructure, & Transportation Working Group Chair Norma Torres (CA-35), New Dem Vice Chair for Outreach Salud Carbajal (CA-24) and Housing Task Force Chair Emilia Sykes (OH-13) hosted the roundtable. They were joined by 14 additional New Dem Members and eight stakeholders for the discussion.

“Getting the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act into law was an important step forward, but the lasting impact of this law will depend on how effectively we put it into practice," said Rep. Norma Torres. "It's also critical that we look at what's next, which is why we put together this roundtable to hear from experts, stakeholders, and Coalition Members to kickstart work on further policy changes we need to make homes more affordable for our constituents."

“New Dems are leading the charge to address our nationwide housing crisis. In the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, roughly half of the provisions were sponsored by New Dems or priorities from our Housing Affordability Agenda. While this law represents significant progress, our work is far from complete,” said Rep. Salud Carbajal, New Dem Vice Chair for Outreach. This week’s roundtable gave us an opportunity to engage with housing stakeholders and map out the next steps needed to build on the momentum we’ve created.”

"As Chair of the Housing Task Force, I've seen firsthand how the affordable housing crisis touches every part of our country," saidRep. Emilia Sykes. "We achieved great wins in the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, including provisions from my HOMES Act to rein in corporate investors who are pricing working families out of their own neighborhoods. But there's more to do. This roundtable was about listening to the people building, financing, and studying housing every day, so we can turn their expertise into the next set of solutions Congress delivers."

This roundtable continues the discussion around affordable housing solutions following successful passage of the 21st Century Road to Housing Act earlier this year. This landmark housing package contained provisions from 22 New Dem Member-led bills and two New Dem proposals and delivered on many of the key objectives laid out in the New Democrat Coalition’s Housing Affordability Agenda.

New Dem Members’ work to address the affordable housing crisis has become a cornerstone of our efforts this Congress. This roundtable expanded these efforts and was an opportunity for Members and guests to discuss what Congress needs to do next to build more homes quickly, expand access to affordable housing, make it easier for families to finance their homes, and more.

Roundtable guests included:

Lake Coulson, Senior Vice President for Government Affairs and Chief Lobbyist, National Association of Home Builders

Nicole Upano, Assistant Vice President, Housing Policy and Regulatory Affairs, National Apartment Association

Mike Kingsella, Chief Executive Officer, Up for Growth

Dr. Lesli Gooch, CEO, Manufactured Housing Institute

Libby O’Neill, Senior Policy Analyst, National Low Income Housing Coalition

Tina Lee, Manager of Housing Policy, Economic Innovation Group

David Garcia, Deputy Director of Policy, Terner Center at U.C. Berkeley

Elayne Weiss, Senior Policy Advisor, National Association of Realtors

CHICAGO — Hoy, los miembros del Congreso Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Mike Quigley (IL-05) y Jonathan Jackson (IL-01) —acompañados por una coalición de funcionarios electos locales, entre ellos la senadora estatal Celina Villanueva, el representante estatal Edgar Gonzalez Jr., la comisionada del condado de Cook Alma Anaya y los concejales Michael Rodriguez y Jessie Fuentes, así como organizaciones defensoras de los inmigrantes como Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights (ICIRR), Brighton Park Neighborhood Council (BPNC), Organized Communities Against Deportations (OCAD) y The Resurrection Project (TRP) — ofrecieron una conferencia de prensa para marcar un año de resistencia frente a la Operación Midway Blitz.

La coalición instó a tomar medidas en materia de reforma migratoria, incluyendo la exigencia de una votación sobre la Ley Sueño y Promesa (Dream and Promise Act), y reclamó plena rendición de cuentas por parte de las autoridades locales y federales —incluida la Fiscal Estatal del condado de Cook— ante la brutalidad y el terror que las acciones de control migratorio del gobierno federal han infligido a las comunidades de toda la región.

“Hace un año, la administración Trump intentó quebrantarnos y arrebatarnos la dignidad enviando a agentes federales enmascarados a nuestra ciudad mediante la Operación Midway Blitz. Fracasaron; en su lugar, nuestra comunidad se unió, alzó la voz y desafió su abuso de poder”, declaró el Congresista Jesús “Chuy” García. “Un año después, estamos más unidos que nunca. Pero la lucha no ha terminado. Los agentes federales enmascarados siguen operando en nuestros vecindarios, y continuaremos exigiendo que se marchen y que los responsables de sus crímenes rindan cuentas. Y lo que es más importante: seguiremos luchando por una reforma migratoria significativa para que ninguna comunidad tenga que volver a sufrir las consecuencias de nuestro sistema migratorio fallido”.

“Conmemoramos el primer aniversario de Midway Blitz, cuando el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) inició una campaña de terror en Chicago. Quienes vivimos ese terror lo tenemos claro: el DHS SIGUE SIENDO la mayor amenaza para nuestra seguridad colectiva”, afirmó la Congresista Delia Ramirez. “Al recuperar la mayoría en el Congreso el próximo año, nuestro dolor, nuestra indignación y nuestras exigencias de justicia deben impulsarnos a una acción que honre a todos aquellos que el DHS nos arrebató; debemos hacer rendir cuentas a CADA fascista que haya permitido la violencia del DHS y se haya beneficiado de ella, así como abolir el ICE y desmantelar el DHS”.

"La 'Operación Midway Blitz' de Donald Trump tenía un único objetivo: aterrorizar a Chicago. Los agentes del ICE y la CBP no fueron tras los peores delincuentes; secuestraron a personas en plena calle, lanzaron gases lacrimógenos contra escuelas primarias y mataron a un padre de dos hijos", declaró el Congresista Mike Quigley. "Lamentablemente, el horror de las políticas migratorias de Trump no terminó con la Operación Midway Blitz. Apenas el mes pasado, asistí a una audiencia de deportación donde vi a niños ante la corte sin sus padres, enfrentándose a una barrera idiomática y teniendo que explicar por qué merecen quedarse en este país. Hay que poner fin a esta crueldad. Estoy más comprometido que nunca a trabajar con mis colegas y con los defensores de derechos para proteger a nuestros vecinos inmigrantes y poner un alto al Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) de Trump antes de que causen más daño".

"Un año después de la Operación Midway Blitz, recordamos el daño causado por esta operación autoritaria, pero también honramos a los líderes religiosos, organizadores comunitarios, abogados, educadores y ciudadanos de Chicago que dieron un paso al frente para proteger a sus vecinos y defender los valores que fortalecen a nuestra ciudad", afirmó el Congresista Jonathan Jackson. "Seguiré exigiendo que se rindan cuentas por los abusos cometidos contra los inmigrantes y nuestras comunidades. Me uno a mis colegas del Congreso para reiterar nuestra exigencia de una reforma migratoria integral, basada en la convicción fundamental de que toda persona merece dignidad, equidad y el debido proceso".

“Esta semana se cumple el primer aniversario de la Operación Midway Blitz, y los residentes de Chicago aún se encuentran conmocionados por los horrores que nuestras comunidades se han visto obligadas a enfrentar, mientras agentes enmascarados continúan sembrando el caos en toda la ciudad, deteniendo a innumerables residentes y desmantelando familias sin miramientos”, declaró la Senadora Estatal Celina Villanueva. “Desde que se lanzó la operación el pasado mes de septiembre, las comunidades latinas —especialmente aquellas a las que yo represento— han vivido con miedo constante: temor a salir de sus hogares y a enviar a sus hijos a la escuela. Tras un año de agresiones brutales contra manifestantes, patrullajes en las calles, redadas en nuestros vecindarios y daños a nuestros residentes, ya es hora de exigir rendición de cuentas y justicia a esta administración, no solo para los latinos de Illinois, sino también para todos aquellos afectados por estos actos de odio sin sentido”.

“La Operación Midway Blitz no quebrantó a nuestra comunidad; fortaleció nuestra determinación. Durante un año, nuestras familias inmigrantes, vecinos y organizaciones comunitarias se han mantenido unidos frente al miedo y la intimidación. Seguiremos defendiendo a cada familia y protegiendo el espíritu acogedor que define a nuestra comunidad”, afirmó el Concejal del Distrito 22, Michael D. Rodriguez.

“Ya sean las redadas en apartamentos de South Shore, el tiroteo contra Marimar Martínez en Brighton Park o el asesinato de Silverio Villegas González, ha quedado demostrado que ICE NO nos protege; su función es intimidar a las comunidades de color y deportar a tantas personas como sea posible. Los líderes locales y los políticos deben apoyar a los inmigrantes y hacer cumplir las leyes y políticas por las que nuestras comunidades lucharon para convertir a Illinois en un lugar que dé la bienvenida a todos”, afirmó Lawrence Benitio, director ejecutivo del ICIRR.

“La Operación Midway Blitz no ha terminado; todavía sufrimos las consecuencias de ver cómo miles de vecinos fueron arrancados de nuestra comunidad. Familias separadas. Empleos perdidos. Comunidades desestabilizadas. Sin embargo, a pesar de todo, nuestra comunidad sigue dando la cara y luchando. Nos negamos a permitir que se normalice este terror”, declaró Any Huamami, directora de organización del Brighton Park Neighborhood Council.

“Hace un año, por estas fechas, nuestras comunidades sufrían el terror provocado por agentes enmascarados; hubo personas secuestradas sin explicación y familias separadas a la fuerza debido a la campaña de control migratorio de esta administración federal. El año pasado nos demostró que todos corríamos el riesgo de ser detenidos simplemente por nuestra apariencia. Las detenciones ilegales se convirtieron en la norma, pero seguimos aquí denunciando esas acciones y recordando a la gente que ICE continúa operando en nuestras comunidades. Es nuestro deber mantenernos alerta y protegernos mutuamente”, afirmó Antonio Gutiérrez, cofundador y coordinador estratégico de Organized Communities Against Deportations.

“El noroeste de Chicago fue uno de los puntos clave de la Operación Midway Blitz. Los miembros de la comunidad local se unieron para resistir este ataque, formando parte de la red estatal de respuesta rápida coordinada por ICIRR. Nuestra labor no terminó cuando concluyó la Operación Midway Blitz; a la fecha, seguimos presenciando secuestros y agresiones por parte del ICE en nuestros vecindarios. Los miembros de la comunidad seguirán haciendo su parte para mantenernos a salvo. Ya es hora de que los departamentos de policía locales cumplan con su deber e investiguen las acciones de estos agentes para que podamos exigirles responsabilidades. Es lo mínimo que merecen los miembros de nuestra comunidad y los vecinos que sufrieron ataques con gases lacrimógenos y gas pimienta, además de agresiones y violencia por parte del gobierno federal”, declaró el pastor Juan Pablo Herrera, presidente de la junta directiva de PLSNA.

“El miedo que recorrió nuestras comunidades es real, pero este año no estuvo definido por el miedo, sino por la belleza y la resiliencia de nuestra comunidad. La administración Trump se propuso dar un ejemplo con Chicago. En cambio, nosotros dimos el ejemplo: construimos una respuesta coordinada a nivel estatal que ha conectado a decenas de miles de miembros de la comunidad con asistencia legal, así como una red de respuesta rápida que demuestra que los inmigrantes de todo Illinois nunca están solos”, afirmó Eréndira Rendón, vicepresidenta de Justicia para Inmigrantes de The Resurrection Project.

GRANITE CITY, IL — Yesterday, Congresswoman Nikki Budzinski (IL-13) met with leadership at Gateway Regional Medical Center to address serious concerns surrounding patient-safety and the hospital’s ongoing financial crisis. In an exclusive interview with KMOV David Amelotti, Budzinski shared what was discussed in the closed-door meeting and emphasized what must be done to ensure the community continues to have access to quality care and hospital staff have the resources they need.

Watch the full interview HERE.

In August, reporting from KMOV raised serious concerns around billing and staffing issues at Gateway that were impacting patient care. Budzinski immediately sprang into action, reaching out to the state and ultimately sending a four-page letter to American Healthcare Systems CEO and Gateway Regional Medical Center CEO, Michael Sarian and Joe Ottolino, demanding clear answers on Gateway’s finances, employee benefits, and staffing stability.

In response to the letter, hospital leadership agreed to meet with the Congresswoman in person. Budzinski visited the hospital to hear directly about the challenges facing the facility, and discuss a path forward to address concerns about patient care and the hospital’s financial stability. Going forward, Budzinski is pushing Gateway to make serious and meaningful improvements to adequately serve patients in the community and remain in a position to provide the quality care patients deserve and continue receiving critical Medicare and Medicaid funding.
title: VIDEO: Budzinski Meets with Gateway Memorial Hospital CEO, Demands Reform to Improve Operations

“Exercising your right to worship should not require you to exhibit particular courage as you enter your synagogue, church, mosque, temple, mandir, or gurdwara,” said Congressman Suozzi. “I will always stand up for people’s right to protest peacefully, but attendees of religious services should not be harassed, threatened, intimidated, or targeted for practicing their faith. I am proud to lead this bipartisan and bicameral Right to Worship Act that both protects free speech and the freedom to worship.”

“The breadth of support for the Right to Worship Act is very gratifying. So many groups recognize the horrifying reality that the threat to the freedom to not unique to any one faith or congregation. Every religious community feels it, which is why this bill will protect everybody,” Suozzi continued. “I’m proud to stand with such a broad coalition of faith leaders united behind this essential legislation to safeguard the right to worship for every religious community on Long Island, in Queens, and across America.”

Congressman Suozzi’s Right to Worship Act follows his earlier introduction of the SACRED Act in April 2026. Suozzi worked with colleagues in both parties and chambers to build bipartisan, bicamerical support for his buffer zone legislation, introducing the Right to Worship Act in the House with Congressman Brad Knott (R-NC) last month alongside a companion measure in the Senate by Senators Cruz (R-TX) and Slotkin (D-MI). Suozzi also expanded the coalition of organizations supporting the legislation, securing the endorsement of more than 20 national groups across faiths for the Right to Worship Act.

Suozzi was introduced today by Alan Mindel, Chair of the Board of Directors for the Holocaust Memorial and Tolerance Center.

“We at HMTC at our core believe in the religious freedom of all citizens and recall the words of Goerge Washington that “The Government of the United States… gives to bigotry no sanction, to persecution no assistance,” said Alan Mindel. “This bill grants necessary protections to houses of worship so as to protect the constitutional rights of freedom of religion granted to all Americans. In the current climate where people have been obstructed from entering their house of worship, this new law will allow each American, regardless of faith, to freely enter their church, synagogues, or mosque for their constitutionally protected right to pray, without obstruction or harassment. We applaud Congressman Suozzi and all the sponsors of this important piece of legislation.”

In addition to Mr. Mindel, Suozzi was joined by ADL (Anti-Defamation League) New York/New Jersey Deputy Regional Director Brandi Katz Rubin, American Jewish Committee Long Island Director Eric Post, UNITED SIKHS community advocate Inderjeet Singh, BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha representative Girish Patel, and Bishop Lionel Harvey. Additional organizational and congregational leaders, including rabbis and synagogue presidents, attended as well to show their support for the legislation.

The Right to Worship Act would establish a 100-foot, protest-free buffer zone around houses of worship during religious services, making it unlawful to knowingly disrupt or impede people from attending. The bill prohibits conduct that knowingly “hinders,” “deters,” “threatens,” or “intimidates” worshippers trying to enter religious services and would impose civil fines for violations. It authorizes individuals, the U.S. Attorney General, and state attorneys general to sue violators. Peaceful expression protected by the First Amendment is excluded from the bill’s prohibited activities.

The legislation is endorsed by a broad coalition of groups representing a variety of faith communities, including:

Anti-Defamation League (ADL)

Agudath Israel of America

American Muslim & Multifaith Women's Empowerment Council (AMMWEC)

American Jewish Committee (AJC)

Hadassah

Hindu American Foundation

Islamic Society of North America (ISNA)

Jewish Federations of North America (JFNA)

North American Division of Seventh-day Adventist Church

National Association of Evangelicals (NAE)

StandWithUs

UJA-Federation of New York

Union for Reform Judaism

Union of Orthodox Jewish Congregations of America (Orthodox Union)

UNITED SIKHS

title: Suozzi Highlights Broad Local Support for Bipartisan, Bicameral Buffer Zone Bill

WASHINGTON – U.S. Representatives Robin Kelly (IL-02), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), and Emily Randall (WA-06) led 49 Members of Congress in sending a letter to Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz calling for an immediate end to the sharing of Medicaid enrollee data with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

Despite a federal preliminary injunction limiting data transfers, CMS continues to share private data belonging to millions of enrollees—including U.S. citizens and lawful residents—beyond court-approved limits. Reports also reveal ICE improperly mishandled the data across internal channels and shared it with third-party analytics contractors like Palantir Technologies.

"The role of HHS should be to protect the health of all those living in this country and provide essential human services, not to be a watchdog for DHS or act as immigration enforcement," the Members stated in the letter.

Read the Full Letter Here

title: 53 Members of Congress Demand HHS and CMS Halt Medicaid Data Sharing with ICE

JERSEY CITY, NJ – El miércoles, los Representantes Rob Menendez (NJ-08), el Presidente del Caucus Hispano del Congreso, Adriano Espaillat (NY-13) y Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) realizaron una visita de supervisión en Delaney Hall, operado por GEO Group, tras las repetidas denuncias sobre las condiciones dentro del centro de detención, incluyendo reportes de comida en mal estado, aire acondicionado inadecuado o no funcional y graves preocupaciones sobre el acceso a atención médica oportuna y adecuada.

Tras la visita, los miembros emitieron la siguiente declaración conjunta:

"El ICE y GEO Group tienen una responsabilidad con las personas que mantienen bajo custodia federal. Lo que escuchamos y observamos hoy deja en claro que quienes se encuentran en Delaney Hall continúan siendo peligrosamente desatendidos.

Nos reunimos con personas que detallaron la demora o negación de atención médica cuando las personas están enfermas o con dolor, la entrega de alimentos en mal estado e inseguros, y un aire acondicionado inadecuado que obliga a las personas a soportar condiciones peligrosas. Esto es un fracaso de atención y supervisión financiado con fondos federales.

Seguiremos exigiendo respuestas claras sobre lo que está ocurriendo dentro de esta instalación, incluyendo las muertes de personas detenidas en Delaney, qué está haciendo el DHS para abordar estas condiciones y por qué las personas bajo custodia federal se han visto obligadas a soportarlas en primer lugar."

Los miembros continuarán revisando la información recopilada durante la visita de hoy y llevarán a cabo una supervisión adicional según sea necesario, incluyendo la búsqueda de respuestas de los funcionarios federales y los operadores de la instalación con respecto a las condiciones reportadas en Delaney Hall.
title: Los Reps. Menendez, Espaillat y Mejia realizan visita de supervisión en Delaney Hall tras reportes de condiciones negligentes

Today, U.S. Representative Sharice Davids announced that she secured $8.3 million for the Kansas State Department of Education through the U.S. Department of Education’s Teacher and School Leader Incentive Program (TSL). The program strengthens teacher and school leader recruitment, retention, professional development, and leadership opportunities across the country.

“I went to Kansas public schools and became a first-generation college student, so I know firsthand how much a good teacher and a strong education can change a student’s trajectory,” said Davids. “This new investment will help Kansas continue to build the kind of schools where students can thrive by supporting the teachers and school leaders who show up for our kids every day.”

The TSL program helps schools recruit and keep quality teachers and school leaders. The funding can help schools provide teachers with additional training and coaching, create opportunities for experienced teachers to take on leadership roles, and offer incentives for educators who take on more responsibility. The program also helps schools attract and keep strong educators in low-income and rural communities where they are needed most.

A U.S. Department of Education evaluation of the program’s predecessor found that performance-based incentives led to student achievement gains equivalent to roughly three to four additional weeks of learning. The TSL program has since funded 160 projects serving more than 2,000 schools in 36 states and Washington, D.C.

Last year, Davids spoke out against the Trump Administration’s plan to dismantle the U.S. Department of Education, warning that eliminating the department could put critical education funding and services at risk for students, teachers, and families. She has continued pushing for federal investments that support Kansas classrooms, including securing funding for early education, STEM programs, and apprenticeships.

This award includes $2,903,167 in base funding and $5,483,666 in additional frontloaded funding, bringing the total FY 2026 award to more than $8.3 million. The FY 2026 TSL program is expected to provide approximately $60 million nationwide through competitive grants to eligible state agencies, school districts, and other organizations.
title: Davids Secures Major Federal Award to Recruit, Support Kansas Teachers

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Don Davis (NC-01) is proud to announce that the 2026 Congressional App Challenge is now open for middle and high school students in North Carolina’s First Congressional District.

The Congressional App Challenge is a nationwide competition designed to encourage middle and high school students to explore coding and computer science by developing their own original apps. The challenge promotes the importance of STEM (science, technology, engineering, and math) education and supports the next generation of tech innovators.

“The Congressional App Challenge proudly highlights the remarkable creativity and innovation of North Carolina’s First Congressional District,” said Congressman Don Davis. “Students across eastern North Carolina are gaining the skills and experience needed to lead in an increasingly technology-driven economy. (Houston, Texas) — On Thursday, September 10, 2026, Congressman Al Green will join Brandon Mack, President of the Houston LGBTQ+ Political Caucus, Avery Belyeu, Chief Executive Officer of The Montrose Center, and Daron Perez, Transwellness Coordinator of The Montrose Center to host a press conference addressing concerns regarding the maltreatment of transgender immigrants in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention facilities. The press conference follows Congressman Green’s September 4, 2026, communiqué to U.S. Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, in which he raised concerns about the denial of specialized medical care and the removal of protections for transgender immigrant detainees. A copy of the communiqué is accessible by clicking here.

"ICE detention cannot become a place where transgender people are punished for their identity. When the government takes someone into custody, it assumes responsibility for that person's safety, health, and dignity. We support and stand in solidarity and agreement with Congressman Al Green's demand for answers and accountability. We urge DHS to take immediate and verifiable action,” Brandon Mack, President, Houston LGBTQ+ Political Caucus.

“Transgender individuals who find themselves in the care of our government during immigration proceedings deserve dignity, safety, and basic health care. That means they are not mistreated, are housed in safe accommodations, and are able to access all of their medications. We are grateful to Congressman Green for seeking clarification on how these guarantees are being met,” Avery Belyeu, Chief Executive Officer, The Montrose Center.

Congressman Al Green stated, “Transgender persons deserve to live without fear that their identity will be used as a reason to deny them care, especially health care, safety, or humane treatment while in ICE custody. While many communities have suffered under harmful immigration policies, we must not overlook the particular vulnerabilities faced by transgender immigrants in detention. Government custody must never become a license to discriminate. We must demand humane treatment and necessary medical care, and we must protect transgender lives.”
title: Congressman Al Green, the Houston LGBTQ+ Political Caucus, and the Montrose Center will Address the Maltreatment of Transgender Immigrants in ICE Detention Facilities

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Representative Mark Takano (CA-39), a senior member of the House Education and the Workforce Committee, and Senator Bernie Sanders (I-VT) reintroduced the Thirty-Two Hour Workweek Act.

The bill, first introduced by Rep. Takano in 2021, amends the Fair Labor Standards Act to reduce the standard workweek from 40 hours to 32 hours for nonexempt employees. Covered employees would be eligible to receive overtime compensation for any hours worked beyond 32 hours in a standard workweek.

It’s time for labor law to catch up to the modern-day nature of work. Since 1979, American workers’ productivity has risen 93.2% while wages have risen only 33.7%. Though Americans are more productive than ever, their pay remains relatively stagnant and federal labor protections have not seen meaningful change for over 85 years.

The Thirty-Two Hour Workweek Act ensures that all American workers reap the benefits of their increased productivity by having more of their time back or receiving more time and a half pay.

“The 40-hour workweek was established in law nearly 90 years ago,” said Congressman Mark Takano. “Since then, cell phones, the internet, and now AI have increased worker productivity, but the profits have been largely concentrated at the top by billionaires and corporations. Work has fundamentally changed. It’s time that labor standards caught up. I’m proud to continue partnering with Senator Sanders in reintroducing this bill to make sure that the gains from historically high productivity are felt by all American workers.”

“At a time when artificial intelligence and robotics will radically transform our economy, it is imperative that the financial gains from this new technology benefit working families, not just a handful of billionaires and corporate CEOs. One important way to do that is through a 32-hour workweek with no loss in pay or benefits,” Senator Bernie Sanders said. “A 32-hour workweek is not a radical idea. What’s radical is that, despite an explosion in technology and productivity over the last fifty years, millions of workers are working longer hours for lower wages while nearly $80 trillion in wealth has been redistributed from the bottom 90 percent to the top 1 percent. That has got to change. It’s time to reduce the stress level in our country and allow workers and their families to enjoy a better quality of life. It’s time to pass this bill.”

The Thirty-Two Hour Workweek Act has been endorsed by: Association of Flight Attendants-CWA (AFA-CWA), The American Federation of Labor and Congress of Industrial Organizations (AFL-CIO), The International Federation of Professional and Technical Engineers (IFPTE), National Employment Law Project (NELP), National Nurses United (NNU), Radio and Machine Workers of America (UE), Service Employees International Union (SEIU), United Auto Workers (UAW), United Food and Commercial Workers (UFCW) and WorkFour.

Full text of the bill can be found here.

###
title: Rep. Takano, Sen. Sanders Reintroduce 32 Hour Workweek Act

Washington, D.C. — Today, Speaker Emerita Pelosi joined Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24), along with Senate Environment and Public Works Committee Top Democrat Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) and U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA) and Adam Schiff (D-CA), and 13 of their colleagues in filing an amicus brief in California v. Wright, pending in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California, to challenge the Trump Administration’s use of the Defense Production Act (DPA) to facilitate the restart of the Sable Offshore oil pipeline system along the California Central Coast.

The brief argues that the Administration has failed to identify a legitimate national defense need for Sable’s crude oil and that the DPA order does not satisfy the statutory requirements for invoking this extraordinary authority. Sable produces crude oil—not finished fuels used by the military—and the order does not establish a connection between Sable’s production and an unmet military fuel requirement.

“The Trump Administration’s abuse of the Defense Production Act to revive the Sable pipeline is an unlawful corporate giveaway masquerading as a national security measure,” said Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi. “California communities know the devastating consequences of offshore oil spills. Congress created the Defense Production Act to protect our national security—not to reward political allies, endanger our coastline and override vital environmental safeguards.”

An excerpt from the brief is below.

“This case is not about national defense. It is about a heavily leveraged, crude oil company asking the President to transform the Defense Production Act (DPA) from a statute designed to ‘assure the availability of domestic energy supplies for national defense needs,’ 50 U.S.C. § 4502(a)(5), into a corporate rescue operation for political allies; a rescue that advances the Administration’s political preference for fossil-fuel development at the expense of all other concerns. The Department of Energy’s (‘DOE’) March 13, 2026 order (the ‘Wright Order’) comes nowhere close to identifying a need for Sable crude oil or pipelines in the Order’s generalized invocation of California’s military presence and increased reliance on foreign crude. DOE never explains why those general circumstances create a national-defense need for Sable’s crude, much less how restarting its beleaguered pipelines would meet one.

“Merely invoking “national defense” or an “emergency” does not insulate executive action from the statutory prerequisites that Congress imposed in the DPA on the exercise of delegated authority. Enforcing these requirements, i.e., that the Secretary establish the statutory predicates for invoking the DPA, does not amount to second-guessing genuine executive judgments about national defense. Instead, enforcement honors the conditions precedent Congress imposed to prevent abuse of the DPA. DOE’s failure to satisfy these statutory prerequisites invalidates the Wright Order.”
title: Pelosi Joins Democratic Colleagues in Challenging Trump Administration’s Involvement in the Sable Offshore Pipeline Restart

GEORGETOWN, Del. — Today, U.S. Senators Chris Coons and Lisa Blunt Rochester and U.S. Representative Sarah McBride (all D-Del.) traveled across Sussex County to celebrate more than $5 million in federal investments to expand access to affordable healthcare through La Red Health Center in Georgetown and Seaford and Beebe Healthcare’s Long Neck Health Center in Millsboro.

The events were part of the delegation’s “Delaware Delivers: Federal Investment at Work” tour highlighting how federal dollars are being put to work to expand access to affordable care and meet the needs of Delaware communities. Photos from the events can be found here.

“Anyone who lives downstate will tell you there simply aren’t enough doctors in Sussex,” said Senator Chris Coons. “It makes it harder for people to get the care they need, leaving communities here sicker, ER wait times longer, and health care more expensive for everybody. That’s why we’ve taken action in Washington to get millions of dollars to add more doctors and clinics to Sussex County – because you deserve care no matter where you live.”

“Every Delawarean should have access to quality affordable health care, regardless of their zip code or background,” said Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester. “We will continue to work to close health care gaps and lower rising health care costs, so no Delawarean has to choose between putting food on their table and getting the care they deserve.”

“Sussex County is experiencing significant growth, so it’s imperative that our healthcare system keeps pace,” said Rep. Sarah McBride. “The federal investments we’re highlighting today will help us do just that — by expanding critical services, from primary care to substance use disorder treatment, for residents across Sussex County. I’m proud to have worked alongside Senators Coons and Blunt Rochester to bring these resources home and invest in the health of our neighbors. Every Delawarean deserves access to quality, affordable healthcare, no matter their ZIP code or circumstances. Because when more people can get the care they need, when they need it, we lower healthcare costs for everyone.”

The congressional delegation first toured the La Red Health Center in Georgetown to celebrate the more than $3.7 million in federal funding to strengthen its facilities and services across Sussex County. The investments include $2 million for facility enhancements at La Red’s Georgetown campus, including maximizing administrative space, improving energy efficiency, making structural repairs, and enhancing safety; $720,000 for infrastructure improvements at its Seaford location, including replacing the HVAC system and repaving the parking lot to improve accessibility; and $1 million to strengthen La Red’s Rural Re-Entry Program, which connects formerly incarcerated people with healthcare, treatment, housing, and workforce support.

“This funding is critical for La Red and our patients,” said Rachel Hersh, President & CEO of La Red Health Center. “Every year, 15,000 people in Sussex County count on us for their healthcare needs. This funding will allow us to make necessary improvements to our Georgetown and Seaford facilities that will extend the lives of those buildings. It will also allow us to enhance our care for our patients by adding staff to our rural re-entry program.”

The delegation then traveled to Beebe Healthcare’s Long Neck Health Center in Millsboro to celebrate $1.75 million in federal funding to relocate and expand Beebe’s Coordinated Care Center. The investment will help renovate the Long Neck facility to expand access to primary care, care coordination, and chronic disease management in a rapidly growing area of Sussex County.

Beebe launched the Coordinated Care Center in Lewes in August 2024 to help bridge the gap between hospital care and critical follow-up care for patients who do not have a primary care provider. Patients can leave the hospital with a follow-up appointment already scheduled, helping connect them with continued care and reduce the risk of readmission. The expanded Center will allow Beebe to serve more patients discharged from its emergency departments or inpatient care without a primary care provider.

"At Beebe Healthcare, we know that access to care is about more than having healthcare options available," said David A. Tam, MD, MBA, CPHE, FACHE, President & CEO, Beebe Healthcare. "The Coordinated Care Center helps bridge the gap between a hospital stay and long-term health, connecting patients to primary care, care coordination, chronic disease management, and other support services that help them stay well. By reducing avoidable hospital readmissions and helping patients access timely follow-up care, the center can help reduce unnecessary emergency department utilization while connecting patients to the right care at the right time. This investment will allow us to expand that proven model, bringing care closer to home while advancing our commitment to value-based care focused on prevention, wellness, and better health outcomes. We are grateful to Delaware's Congressional Delegation for their partnership in helping improve the health of our community."

Sussex County is growing rapidly, but access to healthcare has not kept pace. These federal investments will help La Red and Beebe expand capacity and services to meet growing demand and connect more Sussex County residents with quality care close to home.

The funding was secured through the federal appropriations process in the House and Senate.
title: PHOTO RELEASE: Coons, Blunt Rochester, McBride Celebrate Federal Investments to Expand Rural Healthcare Access in Sussex County

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) issued the following statement after Secretary of the Smithsonian Lonnie G. Bunch III announced his plans to retire:

“For the past seven years, Lonnie Bunch has led the Smithsonian with a deft hand and a passion for its mission. He has skillfully navigated challenges to the institution’s independence and academic integrity, and the Smithsonian has benefited from his strong leadership and unique cascade of talents.

“Earlier, as the founding Director and principal architect who collaborated with John Lewis and other major African-American leaders, including from the Congressional Black Caucus, Secretary Bunch created one of the premier institutions teaching and preserving African-American history and culture.

“I am extremely disappointed that a world-class institution is losing a world-class leader. The next leader of the Smithsonian must be someone like Secretary Bunch who will fight to preserve its independence. We must not allow political interference to shape how visitors experience the art, history, and science presented at Smithsonian facilities. They must be based on facts and on expert interpretation by respected scholars, not based on ideology.

“Sadly, Secretary Bunch is the latest casualty of this Administration’s war on intellectual honesty and the complex facts of our history. This President and his advisors have no shame or regard for the truth, ordering messages to be posted in front of the Smithsonian Museum of American History and other places promoting revisionist, partisan interpretations of our past.

“I look forward to engaging with the Board of Regents and with key Congressional colleagues to ensure that the process to select the fifteenth Secretary of the Smithsonian is fair, open, and unblemished by political interference.”
title: Hoyer Statement on the Retirement of Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie G. Bunch III

Southbridge, MA — Today, Congressman Richard E. Neal joined Southbridge Town Manager Jack Jovan and town officials to highlight the impact of federal investments made possible by the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA), the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA), and the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA). More than $1.5 billion has been invested across the First Congressional District.

In Southbridge, $18.2 million was invested in projects and initiatives, with funding streams including:

$11.5 million in ARPA funding, consisting of $5 million in Coronavirus Local Fiscal Recovery funding and $6.5 million in Elementary and Secondary School Emergency Funding

$6.7 million in funding from the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act and the Inflation Reduction Act

“I am delighted to join with Town Manager Jack Jovan, members of the Town Council, and local residents to highlight the Town’s superb work in putting these once-in-a-generation investments to good use. Based on what we saw here today, I am pleased to see another community in the First District that benefited from these landmark laws and put these funds to work for its residents,” said Congressman Neal. “Whether it’s investing in the Town’s infrastructure, supporting food assistance and workforce development programs, or providing a lifeline for small businesses, the Town seized the opportunity to both address immediate needs and make investments for the future. It’s important that we take the time to show the public how these federal dollars were put to use and allow the public to judge for themselves the impact of these investments. That’s what this tour is all about.”

As a result of the ARPA, the Town of Southbridge was able to pursue more than 60 different initiatives that invested in the Town’s infrastructure, public schools, and local services, and provided critical support to small businesses and nonprofit organizations. Among these initiatives are:

$150,000 for the United Way of South Central Massachusetts Southbridge Resident Community Assistance Program

$100,000 for the YMCA, including $50,000 for the YMCA “What’s for Dinner” food assistance program through the Southbridge Community Center, and $50,000 for the YMCA workplace development program for teens

$300,000 for small businesses in the downtown district

$250,000 for infrastructure improvements on West Street

$29,490 for lights at the softball field

$31,120 for playground equipment at Henry Street Playground

$194,219 for a new DPW loader

$27,925 for the Southbridge Senior Center catering services

$270,723 for a new DPW hotbox for road repairs and paving

$39,029 for a new generator at the Southbridge Community Center

$44,972 for design and building phases of a new broadband network at the Jacob Edwards Library

$50,000 for a feasibility study of the Quinebaug Valley Rail Trail. This project also received a $2.6 million grant from the U.S. Economic Development Administration, which was funded by the American Rescue Plan, ultimately supporting completion of the project.

“The Town of Southbridge was fortunate to receive ARPA funding, and we have worked to use those resources in a thoughtful and responsible manner. These funds allowed us to respond to immediate needs while also investing in infrastructure, public safety, economic development, municipal facilities, and projects that will benefit Southbridge well beyond the life of the ARPA program,” said Southbridge Town Manager Jack Jovan. “The Rail Trail is a particularly good example of the value of strategic investment. The ARPA-funded feasibility work helped position the Town to pursue significant outside funding and ultimately deliver a major community asset. The Town appreciates the work of the Town Council, department heads, municipal employees, community organizations, and residents who contributed to the successful implementation of these projects. The Town remains committed to responsible stewardship of public funds and to making investments that strengthen Southbridge’s infrastructure, services, economic vitality, and quality of life.”

In addition to the ARPA, MassDOT has received $6.7 million from the IIJA for intersection improvements at Central, Foster, Hook, and Hamilton Streets. This is in addition to a $7.8 million Rebuilding American Infrastructure with Sustainability and Equity (RAISE) grant that Southbridge was awarded in FY24 for the reconstruction of Hamilton Street. As a major cut-through in the Town, this street will greatly benefit from added lighting and crosswalks to increase safety, drainage, improved traffic flow, new sidewalks, and paving. The IIJA increased funding for the RAISE Grant Program in FY24, awarding $1.8 billion to projects across the country and enabling communities like Southbridge to finally secure the necessary funding after years of pursuing this investment.

###
title: Neal Makes Sixth Stop on “Landmark Laws, Local Investments” Tour with Visit to Southbridge

HILLSDALE, NJ — Yesterday, Monday, September 7, 2026, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) joined Congressman Mike Lawler (NY-17), Mayor Michael Sheinfield, the Hillsdale community, Rosemarie D’Alessandro, and the D’Alessandro family to unveil “Joan’s Joy Legacy Lane,” a new street sign honoring the memory of Joan D’Alessandro and her mother’s decades-long fight for stronger child protection laws.

“Joan’s joy is still here. It’s on this street sign. It’s in the law that bears her name. And it’s in every child who is a little safer because you refused to let her story end in silence,” said Congressman Gottheimer (NJ-5).

Joan D’Alessandro was a seven-year-old Girl Scout who was murdered on April 19, 1973, while delivering cookies to a neighbor’s house in Hillsdale. Her mother, Rosemarie D’Alessandro, turned her grief into advocacy, championing the passage of “Joan’s Law” in New Jersey in 1997 under Governor Christie Whitman, and its federal counterpart, signed by President Bill Clinton in 1998, ensuring that anyone who murders and sexually assaults a child under fourteen is never eligible for parole. The legislation has been updated in New Jersey to apply to any child under eighteen.

Gottheimer is a cosponsor of the Paula Bohovesky and Joan D’Alessandro Act, to raise the age for prohibition on parole to cover all minors eighteen and under who were murdered and sexually assaulted.

Below: Gottheimer Helps Unveil “Joan’s Joy Legacy Lane”

title: PHOTO RELEASE: Gottheimer Attends Unveiling of “Joan’s Joy Legacy Lane” in Honor of Joan D’Alessandro

Washington, D.C.—Today, House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure Ranking Member Rick Larsen (D-WA) and Subcommittee on Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Greg Stanton (D-AZ) released the following statement after the Washington Post reported that the Trump administration will use a conference room in the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) headquarters to host immigration hearings. 
“FEMA helps all Americans after disasters, but by repeatedly dragging FEMA into border security—from managing ICE detention facilities to now hosting deportation hearings—DHS is eroding Americans’ trust in FEMA,” Ranking Member Larsen said. "I oppose the use of FEMA HQ for Trump’s inhumane deportation agenda.”
“Hosting immigration hearings inside FEMA headquarters during peak hurricane season tells you everything about this administration's priorities,” Ranking Member Stanton said. “They're hollowing out the agency Americans count on in their worst moments and repurposing it for Trump's mass deportation agenda. It‘s a dangerous betrayal of FEMA's mission, and families in harm's way will pay the price.”
Background
The FEMA headquarters has no listed affiliation with the Department of Justice. And, according to immigration attorneys, people were notified about a change in their hearing location within days of the newly scheduled appointments—or were not notified at all. Reports indicate a deliberate attempt by the Trump administration to cause people to miss their immigration hearings and face deportation.

title: Ranking Members Larsen, Stanton Statements on Trump Administration’s Use of FEMA HQ for Immigration Hearings

Letter details how event tickets and merchandise orders flowed through vendors owned by Trump’s former campaign manager and tied to the RNC and MAGA PACs

Washington, D.C. – Today, House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.) and Committee on House Administration Ranking Member Joe Morelle (D-N.Y.) sent an urgent request to the Government Accountability Office to investigate whether Freedom 250, Trump’s shadow organization that hijacked America’s 250th birthday, used federal resources to build a voter contact list for President Trump and his allies ahead of the midterms.

“Based on our preliminary findings, President Trump and his allies are in a position to use information on American voters, harvested with taxpayer money and government resources, in an attempt to tip the scales in the upcoming midterm elections,” the lawmakers wrote. “This is a grave threat to Americans’ personal privacy and freedom from election interference, and we are asking the Government Accountability Office to investigate.”

Watch Ranking Member Huffman discuss the findings.

The letter builds on the Natural Resources Committee Democrats’ July 2 interim report, “From Vanity to Insanity,” which documented how Freedom 250 sidelined the congressionally chartered, nonpartisan America250 Commission and captured most of the $150 million Congress set aside for the semiquincentennial.

According to the letter, every American who requested a free ticket to a Freedom 250 event on the National Mall submitted their name, email, phone number, and ZIP code into Campaign Nucleus – a system owned by Brad Parscale, the architect behind President Trump’s 2016 digital operation and 2020 campaign. A second Parscale company, Dyspatchit, handles Freedom 250’s email and text messaging, which collects billing and mailing addresses. A third Trump campaign-affiliated company, Ace Specialties, runs the official Freedom 250 merchandise storefront and also collects billing and mailing addresses, as well as other contact information.

“A national contact list assembled at taxpayer expense, enriched with geolocation and behavioral data and scored for persuadability, is an asset of extraordinary value to a party heading into a midterm election,” the lawmakers wrote.

Freedom 250’s operations are entangled with Trump and the GOP’s political ambitions, according to the letter. Freedom 250 asked Americans registering for free July 4 tickets to consent to “alerts [and] donation requests,” then sent them links to a Trump-branded WinRed site soliciting donations of up to $5,000 for the Never Surrender PAC. Freedom 250 blamed a vendor mistake, yet registrants went on to receive emails carrying Freedom 250’s name and logo from an address on the Trump campaign’s own domain, and federal records show Never Surrender pays the same vendor that runs Freedom 250’s email program.

“In either scenario, it is clear that Freedom 250 and the Trump campaign are co-mingling their activities and using Freedom 250’s collected data to point registrants to a campaign PAC’s website,” the lawmakers wrote.

The letter warns that no federal privacy law protects this data because of Freedom 250’s intentional structure as a nonprofit subsidiary, and that its own privacy policy names no data protection manager, sets no retention limit, and permits vendors to “disclose, share, and use your information.” The board that controls Freedom 250 now includes multiple Trump campaign architects and a former president of the firm that handles voter data for the Republican National Committee.

The data privacy concerns stretch beyond elections. The Patriot Games application, processed through Parscale’s system, required teens aged 14 to 17 to post public introduction videos and hand over their personal social media handles. The competition itself lasted three days in August, yet parents were asked to sign over open-ended rights to their child’s name, image, and likeness with no expiration date and for use by Freedom 250 itself, meaning the data was never confined to the event. Minors who identified their age, school, and hometown on camera then became targets of hate, harassment, and obscene comments by online trolls who weaponized this data.

“Freedom 250’s solicitation of teens’ videos with little respect for their privacy adds evidence to their pattern of being cavalier with Americans’ data,” the lawmakers wrote.

Huffman and Morelle asked GAO to produce a full list of Freedom 250’s vendors and their political clients, determine how much federal money paid for data collection services, identify what safeguards, if any, stop the data from reaching political committees, assess potential violations of appropriations and campaign finance law, and recommend options for closing the privacy gaps that allow a federally funded nonprofit to run a nationwide data collection operation at the President’s behest.

Read the full letter here.

title: Huffman, Morelle Demand Gov Watchdog Investigate Whether Trump’s Freedom 250 Harvested Americans’ Data to Influence the Midterm Elections

WASHINGTON — On Friday, Representatives Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Ro Khanna (CA-17), and Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10), joined by 27 of their colleagues, in urging Secretary of State Marco Rubio to use every available resource to support ongoing search-and-rescue efforts following the catastrophic flash floods in Nepal and to ensure the safety and recovery of American citizens and others affected by the disaster.

As of September 4, the death toll from the flash floods had surpassed 1,300 people, and at least 4,000 people remained missing, including at least 75 U.S. citizens.

“We support the Department’s announcement of $500,000 in assistance through its global award with Catholic Relief Services to support emergency shelter, relief items, and water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) assistance, as well as the $3.6 million in humanitarian assistance announced on August 29,” the lawmakers write. “Nonetheless, given the unprecedented loss of life and countless missing persons, we urge the Department to do much more.”

The lawmakers requested that the State Department:

Provide daily updates to family members of those missing and Congress as rescue efforts continue.

Deploy a Disaster Assistance Response Team (DART) to flood-affected communities.

Coordinate with the interagency and private sector to utilize high-altitude assets and thermal/infrared drones to search for missing persons and share aerial imagery with partners.

Engage Nepali and PRC disaster authorities and international partners to ensure full coverage and access across search areas.

Ensure rapid delivery of disaster assistance and provide additional reconstruction support.
title: Krishnamoorthi, Khanna, Subramanyam Urge Secretary Rubio to Strengthen U.S. Response to Catastrophic Floods in Nepal

The Bellerose Long Island Rail Road (LIRR) station is currently the only remaining station in Nassau County with no elevator, escalator or ramp to the platform

Watch the Full Press Conference Remarks HERE.

BELLEROSE, NY — Today, Congresswoman Laura Gillen (NY-04) announced $250,000 in new federal Community Project Funding (CPF) she secured through the Fiscal Year 2026 appropriations process to help upgrade the Bellerose LIRR station to be fully accessible in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), including upcoming station renovations such as a new elevator, ramps and stairs. Rep. Gillen was joined by Bellerose Village Mayor Kenneth Moore and disability inclusion advocates Nadia Holubnyczyj-Ortiz and Sheila Moriarty at the Bellerose LIRR station to announce the federal investment.

“I’m proud to have secured this $250,000 in federal funding to help make the Bellerose Long Island Rail Road station fully ADA-accessible, including with a new elevator, ramps and stairs,” said Rep. Gillen. “This investment will create an inclusive and accessible station for Long Islanders with disabilities, seniors, parents with young children and anyone who relies on the LIRR. I will continue fighting to bring more of our tax dollars home to Long Island and deliver the improvements our communities deserve.”

“We are incredibly thankful to Congresswoman Laura Gillen for bringing $250,000 in federal funding back home to upgrade the Bellerose LIRR station,” said Bellerose Mayor Kenneth Moore. “Her ongoing partnership ensures our Village gets the federal support it deserves. Today marks a major step forward in making our station safe, inclusive, and accessible to every resident.”

“As a disabled resident of New York's Fourth Congressional District, I know that accessibility is not an abstract policy discussion,” said disability inclusion advocate Nadia Holubnyczyj-Ortiz. “It determines whether individuals with disabilities can get to work, access healthcare, participate in our communities, and live with the same independence and dignity as everyone else. That is why Congresswoman Laura Gillen's work to secure federal funding for accessibility improvements at the Bellerose LIRR station matters so deeply. The true measure of inclusion is not what we say. It is what we build—and whether the people we elect are willing to make it happen. I am grateful to Congresswoman Laura Gillen for doing exactly that.”

During the press conference, Rep. Gillen discussed the upgrades and how they will improve quality of life for Nassau County residents, particularly for people with disabilities, seniors and parents with young children who rely on the LIRR.

The Bellerose LIRR station dates back more than 100 years and is vital to residents and commuters traveling on the Hempstead Branch. Rep. Gillen worked with the Village of Bellerose, the MTA Long Island Rail Road and other leaders to secure this investment to make the Bellerose station fully ADA-accessible.

The funding for the Bellerose LIRR station is part of more than $13 million in Community Project Funding that Rep. Gillen secured for Nassau County to invest in community infrastructure, enhance public safety, support our local law enforcement and first responders and improve the quality of life for residents across Nassau County.

###
title: Rep. Gillen Announces $250,000 in New Federal Funding for Accessibility Upgrades at Bellerose LIRR Station

WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Representative Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10) introduced a National Data Center Plan. The Responsible Data Center Siting Act, the Data Center Fair Share Act, the Data Infrastructure Energy Measurement and Standards Act, and the Data Infrastructure Risk Reduction Act are four bills to guide data center development to ensure our communities are protected.

The package requires data centers to pay for their own energy, evaluate the cumulative impacts on communities, the environment, and our national security before building data centers, accurately measure water and energy usage, and protect Americans living near data infrastructure.

“Our region is home to the fourth largest concentration of data centers in the world, and many more are on the way. Because of this, our utility bills are up and transmission lines are cutting through our schools and backyards. People are concerned about the future of our community and angry about the impact this will have on noise, the environment, and their property. The approach to building data centers has been driven by short-term profit rather than long term planning.

But it doesn’t have to be this way. We need a national plan that puts communities first rather than the current ad hoc approach. That's why I am pushing this legislation forward: to give Virginians and the American people a voice,” said Congressman Suhas Subramanyam.

“Since its founding, in 2014, the Coalition to Protect Prince William County has been warning residents, elected leaders, and the SCC of the unprecedented power demands of the data center industry. Prince William County residents are already paying a high cost with our rising utility rates and energy infrastructure expansion threatening our homes, our schools, our parks, our private property. Congressman Subramanyam's National Data Center Plan is a needed step in the right direction to protect residents, our environment, and our grid from irresponsible development. Without action, the risk to our grid is no longer a question of IF we will suffer a catastrophic failure, but when.” said Elena Schlossberg, the Executive Director of the Coalition to Protect Prince William County.

Below is background on the four bills:

The Responsible Data Center Siting Act would direct the Secretary of Energy to establish best practices for siting data centers considering energy availability and impacts on utility bills, water use and electricity use, and the environment. It would also consider community impacts such as noise, national security, work force, and tax revenue to guide data center development in a way that protects constituents. The bill is co-sponsored by Reps. Mike Quigley (D-IL), Andre Carson (D-IN), Hillary Scholten (D-MI), Veronica Escobar (D-TX), Greg Stanton (D-AZ), and Mike Levin (D-CA).

The Data Center Fair Share Act requires data centers and other large energy users to pay the full cost of grid and generation upgrades needed to serve them. In Northern Virginia, residents are being stuck with rising utility bills to support the enormous energy demands of hundreds of data centers. Under this legislation, states would be required to adopt large-load tariffs ensuring data centers — not residents — pay for their own power. States that fail to adopt these tariffs will lose access to federal highway funds.

"This bill is a welcome and necessary step to create meaningful protections for consumers," said Karim D. Marshall, Director of Climate and Energy Policy at the Consumer Federation of America. "Families are suffering under astronomical energy prices and they need a backstop against the costs passed on to regular people. Something that is more than an empty promise. The Tech billionaires say that they will responsibly share our power and water. They say that they will be responsible without data and information. They say ‘trust us, we know better.’ The moment demands that consumers are protected from the abuses of the rich and powerful. Consumers shouldn't be forced to subsidize Big Tech through their power bills. The Data Center Fair Share Act creates real consequences for jurisdictions that are willing to sell out their people to please Big Tech."

The Data Infrastructure Energy Measurement and Standards Act directs the National Institutes of Standards and Technology (NIST) to develop technical standards for measuring data center energy and water use. This will ensure we know exactly how much water and energy data centers are using.

The Data Infrastructure Risk Reduction Act will require the development of a strategy to protect the communities living around data centers and data infrastructure from adversaries.

View the Responsible Data Center Siting Act here.

View the Data Infrastructure Energy Measurement and Standards Act here.

View the Data Infrastructure Risk Reduction Act here.

title: Rep. Subramanyam Introduces National Data Center Plan

PHILADELPHIA, PA – Today, Congressman Brendan F. Boyle (PA-02) held a press conference outside the Northeast Philadelphia Satellite Election Office, calling on Congress to urgently pass H.R. 8666, the Vote by Mail Protection Act, to stop President Trump’s efforts to restrict access to the ballot. Boyle also announced a new oversight letter to the United States Postal Service, demanding answers about new procedures that could interfere with the delivery of mail-in ballots and pressing USPS to fully comply with court orders protecting voters.

“We are now exactly eight weeks from what perhaps may be one of the most consequential congressional elections in our lifetime. There are many people throughout the nation who vote by mail, including President Donald Trump,” said Congressman Boyle. “Unfortunately, this White House continues its unprecedented assault on vote-by-mail. First, I am calling on Congress to pass a bill that I'm proud to co-sponsor, the Vote by Mail Protection Act. Second, I am sending an oversight letter today to the Postmaster General demanding answers about this new system and what it could mean for Philadelphia. These are basic questions, and voters — whether Democrat, Republican, or Independent — deserve these answers.”

In the 2024 general election, 200,000 Philadelphians voted by mail or absentee ballot. In his letter, Boyle demands answers about reports that USPS is rushing to make changes to the handling of mail-in ballots at the direction of the Trump administration. Boyle also calls on USPS to provide information about how these changes could impact Philadelphians who vote by mail, what safeguards are in place, and what communications USPS has had with the White House.

The full text of Boyle’s letter to Postmaster General David Steiner can be found here.

Boyle was joined at today’s event by Philadelphia City Commissioner Lisa Deeley and leaders from the American Postal Workers Union.

“We know this playbook,” said City Commissioner Deeley. “It's been the same playbook since 2016. The trick plays have gotten a little more elaborate, but the message is clear: to create confusion and to stop people from exercising their right to vote. I remind everybody, as the Congressman said, you have time, and most importantly, I remind you that it's preparation, not panic, that will win the day for democracy on November the 3rd.”

“The American Postal Workers Union represents over 200,000 postal workers, covering the clerks that you see at the window, the folks that process the mail, the maintenance employees that fix the machines, those that clean, and our drivers. Vote-by-mail works. There's no evidence whatsoever that there's been fraud in elections. And we take pride in doing it. We hope it continues. I appreciate Congressman Boyle, what he's doing for this, and we hope for the best,” said Vince Tarducci, Eastern Region Coordinator, American Postal Workers Union.

###
title: ICYMI: Boyle Demands Answers from USPS on Vote-By-Mail, Calls for Congress to Pass Vote by Mail Protection Act
