SACRAMENTO, CA – Today, on 988 Day, Congresswoman Doris Matsui (CA-07) brought together Sacramento behavioral health leaders and crisis response professionals at the future WellSpace Health Community Wellness Campus to highlight her newly introduced bipartisan legislation, the 988 Implementation Act, which underscores the need to strengthen crisis care for families in Sacramento and communities across the country.

“As we continue to fight the mental health crisis in America, we need to invest in what works. 988 works,” said Congresswoman Matsui. “WellSpace answers the phone when someone has nowhere else to turn. Leaders, providers, and advocates have built something here that delivers, and we need to ensure they have the resources they deserve. That’s my job. To take what’s working here. And make sure Washington pays attention. When I introduce legislation, I start with Sacramento.”

Congresswoman Matsui was joined by Dr. Jonathan Porteus, CEO of WellSpace Health, Dr. Le Ondra Clark Harvey, CEO of the California Behavioral Health Association, which represents behavioral health providers, including 988 call centers, across California, and Devyn Leslie, Lead Crisis Line Specialist at WellSpace Health to discuss what happens when a Sacramento resident reaches out for help during a mental health or substance use crisis and how Congress can help communities provide the care they need beyond the initial call.

WellSpace Health operates 988 for the Sacramento region and across Northern California, providing confidential crisis support by phone, text, and chat 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Its broader crisis system also connects residents with in-person behavioral health services and short-term crisis care.

“When someone is suicidal or experiencing another mental health crisis, help should be as easy to reach as possible and seamlessly integrated in a continuum of services,” said Dr. Jonathan Porteus. “Every connection is an opportunity to provide immediate support to ensure people know they don’t have to navigate a crisis alone. We’re thankful Congresswoman Matsui is prioritizing 988 funding now and for the future.”

“988 cannot simply be a number we ask people to call. It must be the front door to a functioning system of care,” said Dr. Le Ondra Clark Harvey. “When someone reaches out during what may be the most vulnerable moment of their life, what happens next is critical. Congresswoman Matsui’s 988 Implementation Act recognizes that we need the full continuum: someone to call, someone to come, and somewhere to go. CBHA’s diverse, community-based providers see every day why sustained investment in 988 call centers, mobile crisis response, workforce, and stabilization services is essential. We have made tremendous progress since the launch of 988, but launching the number was never the finish line. We must build a crisis system with the capacity to answer, respond, stabilize, and connect every person to the care they need.”

“Our role is to meet people in that moment with compassion and listen without judgement,” saidDevyn Leslie. “We are here to help them find a path forward, and sometimes what a person needs to hear most is that someone is there who is ready to help and listen. 988 makes this possible every hour, everyday.”

Today’s event was held at the future WellSpace Health Wellness Campus on Stockton Boulevard, where Matsui joined WellSpace and community leaders for the project’s groundbreaking earlier this year. The campus represents the kind of community-based approach the 988 Implementation Act seeks to expand, bringing behavioral health and other health services together so Sacramento residents can receive appropriate care closer to home.

Since the national 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline launched in 2022, it has received more than 26 million calls, texts, chats, and ASL videophone contacts from people seeking help. Congresswoman Matsui’s bipartisan legislation would build on that progress by giving states and communities additional resources to strengthen the services available when someone needs more than support over the phone.

The 988 Implementation Act is supported by more than 35 national organizations representing mental health advocates, health professionals, state and local officials, civil rights advocates, veterans, and others.

More information about the bill can be found HERE.

A summary of the legislation can be found HERE.

title: ON 988 DAY, MATSUI AND SACRAMENTO CRISIS CARE LEADERS CALL FOR PASSAGE OF BIPARTISAN 988 IMPLEMENTATION ACT

Last month, when DoD announced delays to critical PFAS cleanup efforts at Stewart Air National Guard Base, Ryan immediately raised the alarm and called on Secretary Hegseth to restore the initial timeline

Friday, after receiving no response from DoD and instead facing even further delays, Ryan rallied with community members and advocates against the “massive betrayal” to the Hudson Valley

Toxic chemical contamination at Stewart has poisoned the drinking water for Newburgh, one of the largest cities in NY-18; this phase of DoD’s remediation effort was meant to be completed this month, but is being delayed by 25 years to 2051

NEWBURGH, NY – Last week, Congressman Pat Ryan – a member of the House Armed Services Committee, Iraq War combat veteran, and the first West Point graduate to represent the Academy in Congress – rallied with local community members and advocates in Newburgh against the decades-long delay of PFAS remediation efforts in Orange County, following news this week that the timeline has been pushed back for a third time.

DoD’s remedial investigation and feasibility study, a key step toward determining a permanent cleanup plan, was expected to be completed in September 2026, but has now been delayed 25 years, to 2051.

Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are toxic “forever chemicals” impacting the health and safety of servicemembers at and around more than 500 U.S. military installations. The PFAS contamination at Stewart Air National Guard Base has tainted the drinking water in Newburgh, one of the Hudson Valley’s largest cities.

When delays were reported last month, Ryan immediately raised the alarm and wrote to Secretary Hegseth demanding that DoD restore all existing PFAS remediation efforts and timelines, provide a detailed written briefing within 30 days, and commit publicly and in writing that no further delays will be imposed without written justification citing specific, documented technical or legal necessity.

After receiving no response from DoD and instead facing even further delays, Ryan’s rally brought together community members, local advocates, and leaders to call for accountability, demand answers from DoD, and push for PFAS remediation.

“Every American – especially our kids – deserves to have clean drinking water. For years, we’ve been fighting hard to ensure clean, safe drinking water is available in every Hudson Valley community, including those around Stewart Air National Guard Base. This critical step was supposed to be completed today. Instead, inexplicably, Hegseth’s DoD has chosen to deprioritize the project and pushed back the timeline 25 years. It’s a massive betrayal, and we’re fighting back, ” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “We’re still facing a public health crisis in the Hudson Valley, and the federal government should be speeding up the clean-up, not slowing it down by decades. Our community is coming together with one voice and a clear message for Hegseth’s DoD: we deserve better, and we won’t stop fighting until every one of our neighbors has access to clean water. We are not giving up this fight.”

“It is unacceptable that the Department of Defense is delaying this cleanup for an unprecedented 20-plus years while the people of Newburgh and New Windsor have live with the consequences,” said Riverkeeper Senior Director of Advocacy, Policy, and Planning Dan Shapley. “Riverkeeper has spent the last decade fighting to protect this community while the full remediation process inches forward. What we can't afford now is to lose the momentum we've finally built. This year's interim projects are proof that meaningful progress is possible right now, not just on some far-off cleanup horizon. Our message to every decisionmaker up the chain is simple: Don’t stand in the way of progress.”

“Newburgh has been waiting years for the Stewart Air National Guard Base PFAS cleanup to conclude the Remedial Investigation phase,” said David H Toman, Hudson River Sloop Clearwater. “We cannot allow this cleanup process to be delayed unnecessarily, and we stand with Congressman Ryan and the Newburgh community in calling on the Department of Defense to complete the Remedial Investigation and Feasibility Study without further delay and keep the cleanup moving forward. Clean drinking water and the health of our community should not, and can not, wait decades for action; the time for action is now.”

“The Department of Defense’s decision to further delay the PFAS cleanup at Stewart Air National Guard Base by more than 2 decades is a direct betrayal of public health and destroys any trust this community had in the military's remediation process. Forcing families to wait decades while toxic "forever chemicals" run off the base is an unforgiveable environmental injustice and we deserve better. This delay condemns yet another generation to a poisoned environment and passes a heavy, exhausting burden for clean water down to my daughters—and quite possibly their future children—leaving them an inheritance of toxic exposure. Our community demands a timely restoration of our land and watershed,” said Jennifer Rawlison, Community Co-Chair of the SANG Restoration Advisory Board and Newburgh Clean Water Project Steering Committee Member.

“The science is clear: there is no known safe level of exposure to toxic PFAS chemicals,” said Rob Hayes, Senior Director of Clean Water with Environmental Advocates NY. “Newburgh residents have already waited far too long for the Department of Defense to remediate PFAS contamination in and around Stewart Air National Guard Base and Washington Lake. Delaying the start of cleanup efforts for more than 20 years is unconscionable when contamination of the surrounding environment is still ongoing, putting clean water and the health of the community at risk. We stand with our local partners and officials to demand that the Department of Defense abandon any attempts to delay PFAS cleanup and instead remediate this pollution as swiftly as possible.”

“This Administration promised to “make America healthy again”, but delaying cleanup of PFAS forever chemicals will only do the opposite,” said Mike Schade of Toxic-Free Future, a national environmental health research and advocacy organization, and a member of the Stewart Air National Guard Restoration Advisory Board (RAB). “We need faster, not slower cleanup of these toxic chemicals, to put Americans’ health first. Pushing this process out for decades is a slap in the face to the residents of Newburgh and New Windsor, who were exposed to PFAS chemicals for far too long. We need urgent action to protect the Hudson Valley from these toxic forever chemicals.”

“Newburgh doesn't drink its own water anymore. Firefighting foam from the air base contaminated our reservoir, so we now buy our water from New York City,” said Council Member Ronald Zorrilla. “New York State has been paying that bill for pollution we didn't create. If that ever stops, our residents face an 80- to 90-percent rate increase. But buying us water is not a cleanup. The Defense Department doesn't get to rent its way out of this until 2051.”

###
title: FOLLOWING SILENCE FROM DOD ON 25-YEAR DELAY TO PFAS CLEAN-UP IN ORANGE COUNTY, CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN AND HUDSON VALLEY COMMUNITY RALLY AGAINST “MASSIVE BETRAYAL”

SACRAMENTO, CA – Today, Congresswoman Doris Matsui (CA-07), a member of the Smithsonian Board of Regents, released the following statement after Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie Bunch announced that he would retire from his position after seven years leading the Smithsonian Institution.

“Lonnie Bunch has spent his life telling America’s full story, with honesty, with humanity, and a deep belief in the power of history to help us better understand one another. His leadership has made the Smithsonian stronger, more inclusive, and more open to the millions of people who look to this treasured institution to learn who we are as a nation.

“Lonnie and I have known each other and worked together for two decades, first when he was Director of the National Museum of African American History and Culture and now as Secretary. As the Board of Regents’ representative to the Museum’s Council, I worked alongside him through its development and construction, and saw up close the vision and persistence it took to build a place worthy of the stories it holds. Lonnie took the Museum from a bold idea to a national treasure, one that faces our painful history squarely and sends every visitor home with hope.

“He brought that same spirit to his time as Secretary. Lonnie has led the Smithsonian with grace and integrity through some extraordinarily difficult moments. He never lost sight of what the Institution is for: to preserve our history, pursue knowledge, and tell the American story in all of its complexity. Grounded in the truth of that history, he has pushed it to new heights.

“Lonnie has my deepest gratitude for his decades of service and for everything he has done to strengthen the Smithsonian for generations to come. Most people know him as one of the nation’s great historians and cultural leaders. I am proud to say he is my dear friend. I wish him and his family every happiness in this well-earned next chapter.”

# # #
title: MATSUI STATEMENT ON SMITHSONIAN SECRETARY LONNIE BUNCH’S ANNOUNCEMENT

text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Frederica S. Wilson (FL-24) released the following statement on the retirement of Lonnie G. Bunch III.

“Lonnie Bunch III did not simply preserve history. He made it, defended it, and refused to let anyone erase it.

“As the first Black Secretary of the Smithsonian and founding director of the National Museum of African American History and Culture, he transformed a dream carried across generations into a national treasure.

“For 38 years, Secretary Bunch fought to ensure that Black history was protected and told truthfully. When powerful forces sought to censor exhibits, distort the past, and diminish the Black experience, he stood firmly in their way.

“Attempts to censor our history cannot erase it, and attempts to silence the truth will only make us tell it louder.

“If there is a sword worth falling on, it is this: We will never stop telling the full American story."

Following federal failures, Congresswoman requests that California officials conduct additional inspections and enforce state health codes to ensure safety and well-being of individuals at Adelanto facility.

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representative Norma J. Torres (CA-35) called on California Attorney General Rob Bonta and California Health & Human Services Agency (CalHHS) Secretary Kim Johnson to expand state inspections and oversight of the Adelanto ICE Processing Center, building on congressional oversight efforts into reported health and safety violations at the facility.

“For months, I have been demanding answers about conditions at Adelanto, and the federal government has continued to fall short,” said Rep. Norma J. Torres. “Four people have died there since early 2025, yet reports of unsafe conditions continue even after a federal court ordered the facility to make changes. These are not just violations on paper. They put people’s health and lives at risk. When the federal government fails to protect people in its custody, California must step in and use every tool available under state law to protect human life and hold GEO Group accountable.”

Rep. Torres’s oversight of Adelanto predates the latest allegations regarding contaminated drinking water. Since January 2025, Congresswoman Torres and her office have conducted 20 oversight visits at the Adelanto facility, spoken with detained constituents, and sought investigations from federal and state officials into water quality, medical care, and safety conditions.

The latest request follows a July 16 preliminary injunction issued by U.S. District Judge Sunshine Suzanne Sykes in L.T. v. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, which found that facility operator The GEO Group, Inc. likely subjected detainees to unconstitutional and inhumane conditions, including mold, disease, unsafe food and water, and inadequate medical care. Recent video evidence has also reportedly shown worm-like organisms in the facility’s drinking water.

In her letter, Rep. Torres called on the California Department of Justice (CA DOJ )and CalHHS to coordinate with county health officials and use state authority under AB 103 and SB 1132 to inspect Adelanto and other immigration detention facilities across California.

She requested responses from state leadership regarding upcoming inspection schedules, coordination with county health officials, and any barriers state officials have encountered from GEO Group, DHS, or ICE during previous oversight efforts.
title: Rep. Torres Calls For Expanded State Oversight of Adelanto ICE Facility Following Court Injunction and Reports of Gross Violations

Pressley Has Fought to Protect Black History Against Trump’s Crusade to Whitewash Museums; Demanded Investigation Into Trump’s Attack on Smithsonian

Pressley Has Drawn Parallels Between Trump’s Attempt Remove Museum Exhibits to Nazi Germany Destroying Jewish Art

WASHINGTON – Today, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07) issued the following statement thanking outgoing Smithsonian Secretary Lonnie Bunch III and slamming the Trump Administration’s ongoing fascist assault on American museums. Secretary Bunch announced that he would step down from his role at the end of this year.

Congresswoman Pressley has led efforts in Congress to protect Black history against Trump’s crusade to whitewash American museums and has demanded an investigation into Trump’s attack on the Smithsonian. In a July committee hearing, the Congresswoman highlighted Trump’s attempts to erase, whitewash, and rewrite American history, through his attacks on Smithsonian museums and cultural institutions.

“Secretary Lonnie Bunch III spent his career making sure America tells the full truth about itself. I am deeply grateful for his extraordinary leadership, his stewardship of American history, and his unwavering defense of our stories during an unprecedented, anti-Black, and fascist assault from the highest levels of power.

“I was honored to meet with Secretary Bunch last year to discuss his work and how we can push back against the Trump Administration’s attacks on the Smithsonian’s independence and its mission to tell the full, complicated, and beautiful story of America. It is a shame that he is stepping down at a moment when Black America and Black history are under attack by an occupant of the Oval Office hell bent on erasing, whitewashing, and rewriting our shared history to push a false narrative about our country.

“While Secretary Bunch’s resignation is a loss for the Smithsonian and our country, his work must continue. I wish him the very best in his future endeavors, and I will not stop fighting to protect our museums, defend the truth, and preserve our history for generations to come.”

Rep. Pressley has been a leading voice in defending diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility, protecting Black history, and pushing back against Republicans’ efforts to deny intellectual freedom—whether by banning books or threatening museums.

Rep. Pressley has also led on securing critical funding for museums, arts, and humanities.

In 2022, she secured $207 million in federal funding for both the National Endowment for the Humanities and the National Endowment of the Arts, which has supported communities, schools, and small businesses throughout the Massachusetts 7th Congressional district. She also secured $2,505,000 for the National Underground Railroad Network to Freedom program in the National Parks Service Operations.

Rep. Pressley has advocated for support for museums across the country that are dedicated to archiving, researching, and preserving the African American experience, such as the National Museum of African American History and Culture. In FY26, she secured $6 million for the Museum Grants for African American History and Culture—including $500,000 for Boston’s Museum of African American History—which will provide such museums the resources they need to build on their work and continue to make history more accessible to the public.

In February 2026, Rep. Pressley led 52 of her colleagues in introducing a resolution to honor Black history museums and cultural institutions in their telling of our accurate, shared American history and protect these institutions from erasure, whitewashing, and funding cuts.

In August 2025, Rep. Pressley condemned Trump’s attempt to politicize, editorialize, and whitewash exhibits at Smithsonian museums—particularly museums and exhibits with diverse and factual presentations of American history.

In May 2025, Rep. Pressley, alongside Congressman Paul Tonko (NY-20), Co-Chair of the Congressional Museum Caucus, led 69 of their colleagues on a letter to the Inspector General of the Smithsonian Institution demanding an investigation on the impact of Donald Trump’s harmful Executive Order attacking Smithsonian museums – namely, the American Art Museum, the American Women’s History Museum, and the National Museum of African American History and Culture – attempting to erase histories of marginalized communities. A copy of the letter is available here.

In May 2025, Rep. Pressley convened a roundtable and press conference at the Museum of African American History in Boston to uplift the vital role of museums in preserving our shared history amid Donald Trump’s attack on cultural institutions and his attempts to erase the documented histories of marginalized communities.

In April 2025, Rep. Pressley delivered a floor speech slamming Trump’s attack on Smithsonian museums and affirming that Black history is American history.

U.S. Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02) joined a bipartisan coalition of 167 Members of Congress last Friday in urging the Trump administration to abandon its proposal to rescind the Roadless Rule, a longstanding and successful conservation guardrail protecting 44 million acres of iconic landscapes and National Forest System lands. The letter underscores the Rule’s broad, bipartisan support, as well as its critical role in safeguarding clean drinking water, wildlife habitats, carbon storage, and outdoor recreation economies across 37 states.

“Since its adoption in 2001, the Roadless Rule has served as a cornerstone of public lands conservation, now protecting approximately 44 million acres of National Forest System lands across 37 states. These areas provide clean drinking water, critical wildlife habitat, carbon storage, and world-class recreation opportunities,” wrote the Members. “The enduring support for the Roadless Rule is rooted in its clear and measurable benefits. Over the past 25 years, the rule has helped protect watersheds, biodiversity, and ecosystem integrity by limiting road construction and large-scale logging in undeveloped areas.”

In the letter, the lawmakers criticize their lack of meaningful public engagement, calling for the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) to extend the comment period, hold in-person public meetings, and conduct full Tribal consultation. The lawmakers also demanded the Trump administration halt its rescission effort and instead focus on successful implementation of this bedrock policy.

The full text of the letter can be read here and below.

Dear Secretary Rollins and Chief Schultz,

As Members of Congress representing a broad range of communities, stakeholders, and outdoor interests, we write in strong support of the U.S. Forest Service’s Roadless Area Conservation Rule (“Roadless Rule”) and in firm opposition to the Department of Agriculture’s proposal for rescission. We urge the Department to halt this effort and instead focus on effective implementation of this longstanding and successful policy.

Since its adoption in 2001, the Roadless Rule has served as a cornerstone of public lands conservation, now protecting approximately 44 million acres of National Forest System lands across 37 states. These areas provide clean drinking water, critical wildlife habitat, carbon storage, and world-class recreation opportunities. Iconic landscapes such as the Tongass National Forest in Alaska, the Gila National Forest in New Mexico, and the George Washington National Forest in Virginia exemplify the ecological, cultural, and economic importance of these lands.

The Roadless Rule was developed through one of the most robust public processes in federal rulemaking history. The Forest Service received 1.6 million public comments - approximately 95 percent in support - and held over 600 public meetings nationwide. In contrast, the current rescission effort has lacked meaningful public engagement. The Department provided just 21 days for public comment on the Notice of Intent in 2025 and has yet to hold any public meetings. Despite these limitations, more than 600,000 comments were submitted, with over 99 percent opposing rescission. This overwhelming and bipartisan public support underscores the continued popularity and importance of the Roadless Rule. Unsurprisingly, at just 30 days, the ongoing comment period for the Draft Environmental Impact Statement (DEIS) and proposed rule is equally insufficient, and we encourage the USFS to extend the comment period to 120 days for a fair and transparent process.

Given the extraordinary public interest in the Roadless Rule and the significant consequences that its repeal would have for communities across the country, the Forest Service should also conduct a robust series of in-person public meetings before finalizing any rescission. Additionally, Tribes are entitled to the opportunity to engage in robust consultation, as the repeal of the Rule will have dramatic consequences on their way of life. When the Roadless Rule was originally developed, the aforementioned 600 public meetings ensured that affected communities, Tribes, local governments, industry, recreation interests, and conservation organizations had the opportunity to engage directly with the agency. The proposal to repeal the Rule warrants the same level of public engagement. Public meetings should be held in regions where National Forest System roadless areas are most affected, providing local communities with a meaningful opportunity to ask questions, provide testimony, and ensure the administrative record reflects the perspectives of those who will experience the greatest impacts. A transparent, accessible, and geographically representative public engagement process is essential to maintaining public confidence in the rulemaking process and ensuring the agency fully considers the consequences of such a consequential policy change.

The enduring support for the Roadless Rule is rooted in its clear and measurable benefits. Over the past 25 years, the rule has helped protect watersheds, biodiversity, and ecosystem integrity by limiting road construction and large-scale logging in undeveloped areas. Forest Service data show that watersheds within roadless areas are far more likely to be in “properly functioning” condition compared to those outside of them, which are more often classified as “at risk” or “impaired.”

These healthy ecosystems support a wide array of wildlife. Roadless areas provide habitat for hundreds of species listed or proposed for protection under the Endangered Species Act, including grizzly bears, lynx, and other sensitive species, and disproportionately support species of conservation concern. In addition, these areas play a vital role in climate resilience and carbon storage. For example, the Tongass National Forest alone stores over 1.5 billion metric tons of carbon and sequesters millions more annually.

Claims that the Roadless Rule impedes wildfire management are not supported by the evidence. The rule explicitly allows for wildfire prevention, suppression, and hazardous fuels reduction. In fact, nearly 2 million acres of roadless areas have undergone fuel treatments in recent years. Forest Service data also show that roadless areas account for a significant share of fuel treatment activities relative to their forest coverage. Research further indicates that wildfire risk is comparable inside and outside of roadless areas and that roads are not necessary to maintain forest health.

Moreover, scientific studies demonstrate that wildfire ignitions occur far more frequently in roaded areas due to human activity. By limiting road construction, the Roadless Rule helps reduce ignition risks from sources such as vehicles, campfires, and other human causes.

Finally, the economic benefits of the Roadless Rule are substantial. By avoiding the construction and maintenance of new roads, the rule saves taxpayers billions of dollars. The Forest Service already faces a road maintenance backlog of nearly $6 billion across its existing system. Expanding road networks into remote and often economically unviable areas would only increase these costs. At the same time, protected roadless areas support recreation, tourism, and outdoor economies, while safeguarding clean water and subsistence resources that communities rely on. When it comes to outdoor recreation, roadless areas encompass more than 25,000 miles of trails, 8,500 climbing routes, 1,000 miles of whitewater, and more than 10,000 miles of mountain biking trails across the country, all of which support a $1.3 trillion outdoor recreation economy. Additionally, hunters and anglers across the nation access these public lands where backcountry provides ample fishing and hunting. The Roadless Rule protects drinking water in 354 municipal watersheds, saving downstream communities millions of dollars in water filtration costs.

After 25 years of successful implementation, the conclusion is clear: the Roadless Rule is effective, widely supported, and essential to responsible forest management. Rescinding it would undermine decades of progress and impose unnecessary environmental and fiscal costs.

We respectfully urge the Department to end its unjustified rescission of the Roadless Rule.
title: Larsen Joins 167 Lawmakers Demanding the Trump Administration Halt its Roadless Rule Rollback

East Hartford, CT – Today, Rep. John B. Larson (CT-01) filed an amicus brief to the Supreme Court of the United States with a bipartisan, bicameral coalition of 261 lawmakers in United States Postal Service v. State of California, urging the court to reject President Trump’s unconstitutional order aiming to take control of the mail-in voting process. His unconstitutional order follows his threats to “nationalize our elections,” and a push from Republicans in Congress to pass the so-called “SAVE America Act” that would create more barriers for Americans to vote and empower the Department of Homeland Security to purge voters from the rolls.

“Whether it is his discriminatory ‘SAVE Act’ or his unconstitutional executive order to take control of mail-in voting, Donald Trump is determined to get in the way of a free and fair election this November,” said Larson. “The Constitution clearly grants the states the power to administer elections, but this president sees our laws as mere suggestions standing in the way of his power. We already know that he sent ‘DOGE’ into Social Security to alter elections and his cronies at the Department of Homeland Security have pressured states to purge eligible citizens from the voter rolls. I am proud to join my colleagues at the Supreme Court to block his latest attempt to mess with the midterms from seeing the light of day. We must all band together so every American can cast their ballot free from fear or intimidation.”

In the court filing, the lawmakers argue that Trump’s Executive Order violates the separation of powers and Article I of the U.S. Constitution, which gives the states and Congress exclusive authority over election administration. The President’s order attempts to give the Postal Service control over who can vote by mail, empowering Trump officials to have the final say over who is eligible to cast a ballot. One-third of Americans are expected to vote by mail in the upcoming midterm elections—a voting practice Donald Trump himself used as recently as August 2026, when the president voted in Florida’s Republican primary.
title: Larson Joins Brief Urging Supreme Court to Block Unconstitutional Trump Order Attacking Mail-In Voting

Washington, D.C. — Today, Representatives Scott Peters (D-CA) and Gabe Evans (R-CO) introduced the Certainty in Litigation for Electric Asset Reliability (CLEAR) Act of 2026, legislation to streamline the buildout of big power line projects. The CLEAR Act would resolve ambiguity in current law so that Department of Energy (DOE)-coordinated transmission projects follow the clear standards of the Federal Power Act instead of traditional judicial review.

In California alone, 201 of the 501 transmission projects approved since 2000 are still stuck in the permitting process, and 89 of those remain delayed. Meanwhile, California's electricity prices have nearly doubled in the past decade, and the state now ranks second highest in the nation for residential electricity rates. Every year a transmission project sits in limbo is a year Californians, and ratepayers across the country, continue to foot the bill for an outdated, overburdened grid.

"Californians pay some of the highest electricity rates in the country, and part of the reason is that we can't get transmission projects through the litigation process and built on time," said Rep. Peters. "Our grid is too old and too slow to meet our skyrocketing energy demand. We can't wait years for badly needed infrastructure to be built. The CLEAR Act would accelerate the review process for large energy infrastructure projects and establish clear rules for stalled transmission projects, giving developers and local stakeholders the certainty to plan along with relief for ratepayers from rising costs."

“As America’s demand for energy continues to rise, it is crucial that we find new and innovative ways to successfully transfer power in an affordable, safe and timely manner. The CLEAR Act will boost energy production, cut red tape and expedite project timelines, and reduce costs related to transmission projects across our country. I’m proud to help lead this important legislation, and look forward to continuing to prioritize permitting reform as I work to make energy and life more affordable for Coloradans and our nation,” said Rep Evans.

The CLEAR Act would align judicial review standards for DOE-coordinated transmission projects with those already used for hydropower and natural gas pipelines under the Federal Power Act, ensuring projects are built on time, without unnecessary legal delays.

The Federal Power Act governs the regulation of electricity and interstate power lines, and it empowers the DOE to act as a coordinating entity between Federal agencies, states, and local governments. However, for DOE-coordinated transmission projects, parties have up to six years to sue, which drags cases through multiple, lengthy legal battles. This leads to confusion and uncertainty for companies who want to plan and invest with confidence, or local stakeholders who want to engage efficiently in the review process.

Under the CLEAR Act, projects would have to follow Federal Power Act judicial review standards, including:

A 120-day statute of limitations for filing suit

A requirement that petitioners participate in the environmental review process before litigating, improving upfront engagement and making projects better during the review process, instead of on the back end; and

Direct elevation of challenges to the U.S. Court of Appeals, ensuring stakeholders can reach a final decision faster

Read a one-pager on the CLEAR Act here and bill text here.

Background:

As leaders of the Problem Solvers Caucus’ Permitting Energy & Environment Working Group, Reps. Peters and Evans have led major bipartisan efforts in Congress to streamline the federal permitting process for energy and infrastructure projects.

They are the original authors of the CERTAIN Act to accelerate energy and infrastructure projects by enforcing strict application timelines. This ensures energy projects move forward quickly, preventing agencies from delaying reviews. It also stops Administrations from canceling permits that were already approved legally. Their bill has been supported by almost 40 organizations, made up of the people who build, power, and maintain America's infrastructure.

###
title: Peters, Evans Unveil Bill to Address Transmission Project Bottlenecks and Lower Electricity Costs

Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Committee Rosa DeLauro (CT-03) and Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Agriculture Sanford D. Bishop, Jr. (GA-02) requested that the Government Accountability Office (GAO) investigate how the Department of Agriculture (USDA) is handing out over $12 billion in trade-war relief through the Farmer Bridge Assistance and Assistance for Specialty Crop Farmers programs.

A 2021 GAO report found that a similar agricultural tariff relief program – administered under President Trump’s first term – disproportionately favored the largest agribusinesses and foreign-owned conglomerates.

“Last year, many members of Congress wrote to President Trump and USDA urging this Administration to ensure any agriculture trade relief program included guardrails and mechanisms to direct funding to producers who truly needed relief rather than simply enriching the largest agribusinesses or foreign-owned conglomerates, and to provide transparency into the process for establishing and executing the program,” the lawmakers wrote. “While USDA has provided some insight into their method for calculating payment rates and the geographic distribution of payments, many of our key recommendations aimed at increasing transparency, protecting taxpayer dollars, and ensuring relief gets where its most needed remain unfulfilled for both programs. Therefore, we ask GAO to conduct a review of the FBA and ASCF programs…”

The full letter can be found here and below.

Cosigners include Representatives Becca Balint, Christopher Deluzio, Shomari Figures, Hank Johnson Jr., John Larson, Bennie Thompson, and Jill Tokuda.

Ms. Orice Williams Brown

Acting Comptroller General of the United States

U.S. Government Accountability Office

441 G Street, NW

Washington, DC 20548

Dear Ms. Williams Brown:

We are writing to request that the Government Accountability Office (GAO) conduct a review of the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Farmer Bridge Assistance (FBA) and Assistance for Specialty Crop Farmers (ASCF) programs. These programs are expected to distribute over $12 billion to American farmers to provide relief from the consequences of President Trump’s reckless tariffs and trade wars, yet USDA has not been sufficiently transparent and only has provided limited information about these payments and their recipients. Congress must be able to conduct proper oversight of these funds, and the American people deserve a fulsome understanding of how USDA is spending their hard-earned tax dollars.

Each year, USDA distributes billions of dollars to agricultural producers, from small family farms to large corporations and trusts. According to USDA’s Economic Research Service, small operations tend to produce a larger share of commodities not covered by government payment programs, which are generally geared towards larger-scale row crop producers (e.g., corn and soybeans).[1]

Over the past 19 months, President Trump’s trade policy has jeopardized the livelihood of producers, particularly small farms and specialty crop producers, as a result of higher input costs due to tariffs and closed-off export markets. In December 2025, the Administration announced the FBA as a relief program for producers impacted by the president’s own trade wars. Through the FBA, USDA will provide up to $11 billion to row crop producers.[2] In February 2026, USDA announced the availability of $1 billion through the Assistance for Specialty Crop Farmers (ASCF) Program for specialty crops, sugar, and commodities not included in FBA.[3] When payment rates were announced in May, that number increased to $1.625 billion.

Last year, many members of Congress wrote to President Trump and USDA urging this Administration to ensure any agriculture trade relief program included guardrails and mechanisms to direct funding to producers who truly needed relief rather than simply enriching the largest agribusinesses or foreign-owned conglomerates, and to provide transparency into the process for establishing and executing the program. While USDA has provided some insight into their method for calculating payment rates and the geographic distribution of payments, many of our key recommendations aimed at increasing transparency, protecting taxpayer dollars, and ensuring relief gets where its most needed remain unfulfilled for both programs.

Therefore, we ask GAO to conduct a review of the FBA and ASCF programs to address the following questions:

To what extent did USDA incorporate lessons learned from the Market Facilitation Program (MFP), including recommendations from multiple GAO reports, regarding the process for setting up and executing the FBA and ASCF?

The 2021 GAO report on the MFP—a similar agricultural tariff relief program launched during President Trump’s first term—noted that UDSA’s methodology overestimated the harm of tariffs to 14 out of 29 commodity crops, resulting in disproportionate payments within and across crops and geographic regions that, by and large, went to the biggest players in the agriculture industry. GAO also pointed out that USDA developed the MFP with little transparency, preventing the Department from receiving outside input on how to improve its methodology.

To what extent did USDA implement “Grow American” requirements (e.g., those outlined in the Buy American Agriculture Act) as part of the FBA and ASCF to ensure taxpayer dollars go to supporting American farmers and not disproportionately to large agribusinesses or indirectly to foreign-owned conglomerates?

What factors did USDA consider in determining the amount available, payment rates, and maximum payment limitations for the FBA and ASCF programs?

What was the distribution of payments under FBA and ASCF by type of producer (crop type, size of farm, and annual farm income)? By payment size categorized by tranches of $25,000 up to maximum payment amount (e.g., $0-25,000, $25,001-$50,000, etc.)?

What proportion of recipients had a net farm income for 2023 of less than $250,000, as recorded in the data in the Economic Research Service publication ‘‘Farm Income and Wealth Statistics’’ as of December 3, 2024 (with such information being collected at the time of application for aid?

What steps did USDA take to ensure that proper payment amounts went out to eligible producers through the FBA and ASCF programs?

What challenges did USDA face in administering the FBA and ASCF programs and what actions has USDA taken to address these challenges?

Thank you for your assistance in this matter.
title: DeLauro, Bishop Request GAO Investigate Trade-War Relief for Farmers

NORWICH, CT – Today, Congressman Joe Courtney (CT-02) joined a bipartisan group of 261 current and former Members of Congress in officially filing an amicus brief to the U.S. Supreme Court challenging the legality of President Trump’s Executive Order seeking to restrict mail-in voting ahead of November’s midterm elections.

“Nearly a third of all voters in 2024 – including many military servicemembers – cast their votes using mail-in ballots with only a 0.000043% rate of fraud, according to analysis by the nonpartisan Brookings Institution,” Courtney said. “President Trump’s Executive Order to put new restrictions on mail-in voting is a blatant and unconstitutional attempt to purge millions of Americans’ ballots. With some states already beginning to mail out ballots for the November election, the Supreme Court must immediately reject the President’s order and protect our vote.”

In the court filing, the Members argue that Trump’s Executive Order 14399, “Ensuring Citizenship Verification and Integrity in Federal Elections,” and the USPS rule, “Ballot Mail for Federal Elections,” which resulted from Executive Order 14399, violate the separation of powers and usurps Congressional authorities outlined in Article I of the U.S. Constitution, which gives the states and Congress exclusive authority over election administration.

Washington, D.C. –Today, Congressman Jerrold Nadler (NY-12) joined Mayor Mamdani to announce the release of more than 170,000 pages of City records documenting the government’s response to the attacks on September 11, 2001 and the aftermath related to the environmental hazards at and around Ground Zero. His remarks can be viewed HERE and read below:

"Thank you for having me here today.

"We are here today to remember the innocent lives that were devastated in the days,

weeks, and months following the deadly terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001.

"We are here to honor the heroes who ran toward the towers as the planes struck,

who combed through the rubble to save survivors, and who worked tirelessly to

clean up the wreckage.

"We are here to honor the men, women, and children who did not know the danger

they were facing as they slept in their homes, went to school, and returned to work.

"When our communities were at their most vulnerable, people turned to trusted

sources—including their government—to guide them through this crisis.

"Government officials betrayed that trust by suspecting, and later knowing, the

environmental hazards from the catastrophe and failing to tell the public.

"The air was unsafe. It was filled with toxic substances that sickened the people

who breathed it in. And 25 years later, our neighbors and heroes are still falling

seriously ill because of these toxins.

"My colleagues and I who represented Ground Zero and the surrounding

communities immediately warned local and federal officials about the health risks

posed by the toxins in the air.

"I was screaming at the top of my lungs to protect our communities, my constituents. But officials like EPA Administrator Christine Todd Whitman and Mayor Guiliani, denied claims like mine, saying the air was “perfectly safe." Blasphemous.

"The failure of government officials to share this information with the public and

adequately respond to the danger has had devastating—and, in too many cases,

fatal—consequences.

"Now, we and the public know that City Hall, led by former Mayor Giuliani,

predicted that thousands of responders and community members would face

devastating long-term health consequences from these toxins. Despite this, he

stayed silent on the hazards.

"Eventually, the air became safe to breathe again. But officials continued to

withhold the truth about the environmental hazards from the people who had been

exposed.

"Their decision to deny the toxicity of the air that people had breathed in was a slap

in the face of the heroes and community members who were exposed at Ground

Zero and in schools, offices, and homes throughout the surrounding area.

"By hiding the truth, our fight in Congress to secure funding to address the health

needs of 9/11 victims was an uphill battle. As a result, too many people faced

unnecessary delays in accessing the healthcare they needed—sometimes with fatal

consequences.

"For years and across multiple City Hall administrations, I have led leaders in

Congress to demand the release of these files. I am glad that this is finally

happening.

"The damage to the health of 9/11 victims, and the suffering they have endured and

will continue to endure, cannot be erased. But I am grateful to the Mamdani administration, specifically to Steve Banks, and to Speaker Menin, Councilmember Brewer, Ben Chevat of 9/11 Health Watch, and Kimberly Flynn of 9/11 Environmental Action, for making today possible. Thank you for your commitment to release these files so that victims and their loved ones can finally have the transparency they deserve.

"Officials in the future will know that actions have consequences—the truth will always come to light.

"I am proud to be here today as we take this monumental step towards justice.

"My heart is with those who are sick today. My heart is with those who have lost

loved ones. My heart is with our community who still reels from the pain."
title: Nadler: Government Officials Betrayed The Public In The Aftermath Of 9/11

Washington D.C. – Today, on Labor Day, Congresswoman Norma Torres (CA-35) introduced the Better Pay for American Workers Act, legislation to raise the federal minimum wage from $7.25 per hour to $20 per hour by 2029 and ensure wages keep pace with the broader economy.

The federal minimum wage has remained at just $7.25 per hour since 2009, even as families face rising costs for housing, groceries, health care, utilities, and other necessities. Since 2009, grocery costs have skyrocketed by 60% and rent has more than doubled, up 110%, and yet Republicans in Congress have blocked multiple efforts to raise the federal minimum wage. This comes as President Trump’s Iran War has caused diesel prices, critical for the delivery of everyday goods, to jump to a record-high of $5.85 a gallon nationwide.

“Working people are doing everything right and still struggling to keep up,” said Congresswoman Torres. “Seven dollars and twenty-five cents an hour simply does not cut it in today’s economy. If you work hard and put in a full day’s work, you should be able to afford a roof over your head, food on the table, and the basic necessities your family depends on.”

“Americans should not have to work multiple jobs just to make ends meet,” Torres continued. “While even $20 an hour is not enough, we need to take a step in the right direction toward a living wage, and it is past time for Congress to stand with working families, raise wages, and give Americans a better chance to get ahead.”

The Better Pay for American Workers Act would raise the federal minimum wage to $15 in 2027, $17.50 in 2028, and $20 in 2029. Beginning in 2030, if the national median hourly wage increases, the minimum wage would increase by the same rate, preventing the minimum wage from falling behind again.

Unlike Congress in Washington D.C., California has taken steps to ensure workers earn a decent paycheck in our state. California’s current minimum wage is $16.90 an hour, and is set to increase to $17.40 beginning January 1, 2027, higher than any current statewide minimum wage. California has also raised the minimum wage to $20 an hour for fast-food workers, and $25 an hour for healthcare workers.

Rep. Torres’ bill would ensure the federal minimum wage catches up to California and eventually surpasses it in 2029. In the Inland Empire, the estimated living wage is $28.26 per hour for a single adult with no children, underscoring the growing gap between wages and the cost of living.

BATAVIA, Illinois — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi today joined Batavia Mayor Jeffery Schielke and local leaders to present $250,000 in federal Community Project Funding he secured to help build a new, dedicated segment of the Fox River Regional Trail, improving safety for pedestrians and cyclists while expanding access to the Fox River.

The new segment will run along the west side of the Fox River between the river and Batavia’s wastewater treatment facility, replacing a section where trail users can be routed off the dedicated path and alongside the roadway. The project will add new safety and guidance features, improve connectivity along the regional trail, and provide better access to and views of the riverfront. The Fox River Trail stretches from Oswego to Algonquin and serves more than 100,000 Fox Valley residents.

“More than 100,000 people across the Fox Valley use the Fox River Trail, and they deserve a safe, reliable route. I’m proud to have secured $250,000 to help Batavia build this new dedicated trail segment, improve safety for pedestrians and cyclists, and make it easier for families to enjoy the Fox River,” said Congressman Krishnamoorthi.

Yesterday, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries joined Rep. Steven Horsford (NV-04) and local labor leaders for a press avail, where he emphasized that House Democrats remain committed to standing up for the men and women of organized labor in the face of Donald Trump’s extreme attacks and destructive policies that are making life more expensive for everyday Americans.

LEADER JEFFRIES: These are very challenging times right now in the United States of America, as the people of Las Vegas are experiencing. We’re in the midst of a Trump slump and unprecedented extremism that has been unleashed on the American people from the very beginning of this toxic administration. Donald Trump promised that costs would go down on day one. Costs haven’t gone down. Costs have gone up in the United States of America. Life is way too expensive. There are far too many people in this city, in this state and all across America who are working hard, they’re playing by the rules, but they can’t thrive and they can barely survive. That should not be the case here in the United States of America, the wealthiest country in the history of the world. But everyday Americans, working class Americans and middle class Americans are being left behind.

As House Democrats, we believe that in this country, in America, when you work hard and play by the rules, as is the case with all of the workers supported by these great unions here today and the unions all across America, that when you work hard, and when you play by the rules, you should be able to live an affordable life, a comfortable life and a good life. And we know what that good life should look like: a good-paying job, good housing, good healthcare, a good education for your children and then when it’s all said and done, a good retirement. That’s the good life.

And as we kick off this Labor Day weekend, let me be clear, no one has done more to bring that American Dream to life than the men and women of organized labor. So House Democrats will continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with you. And we will prioritize pro-union legislation and ensure that when we take control of the majority, we advance bills like the PRO Act so we can protect the right to organize for the American worker all across the United States of America. We’re going to work hard and fight for an affordable America. We’re going to fight to lower the high cost of groceries and gas and housing. House Democrats, we also believe that in this great country of ours, access to high-quality and affordable healthcare can’t simply be a privilege available only to the wealthy, the well-off and the well-connected. Access to high-quality and affordable healthcare needs to be a right available to every single American. And that’s what these unions do such a tremendous job fighting to achieve.

We also believe that immigration enforcement in this country—and we have a broken immigration system—should be fair, just and humane. That’s not what’s taking place right now, which is why we continue to aggressively push back against ICE and its attack on the American people, its attack on law-abiding immigrant families, its attack on workers all across the United States of America. And our commitment as House Democrats is that we’re going to do everything we can to get ICE under control here in the United States of America.

And lastly, among the many priorities that we know we need to push back on, is the fact that not only have Republicans failed to do anything to lower the high cost of living here in the United States of America, their toxic policies have actually made life more expensive, which is why we’re going to fight hard to end the Trump tariffs that have been costing everyday Americans thousands of dollars per year and at the same time, do everything in our power to stop Donald Trump’s reckless and costly war of choice in Iran.

And so, I’m so thankful to be joined here by my good friend, classmate and brother, Steven Horsford, and by all of you, appreciative of the work that you do on behalf of the hardworking men and women here in Las Vegas and throughout Nevada, and committed to being in this fight with you, shoulder to shoulder, over the next 60 days and beyond, and confident that as long as we continue to show up and stand up and speak up for what we know is right, we’re going to win the day and win the week and win the month and win the year, win the hearts and minds of the American people and on November 3, re-elect Steven Horsford and win back control of the United States House of Representatives.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Don Davis (NC-01) announced that Christian Barber has joined his team as Press Secretary and Digital Manager for North Carolina’s First Congressional District.

Barber is a graduate of the University of North Carolina at Charlotte’s Belk College of Business, where he earned a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration with a major in Marketing.

Before joining the congressional office, Barber served as an AmeriCorps Next Step Advisor with the Carolina College Advising Corps at West Charlotte High School, where he helped students prepare for their next steps after graduation through college enrollment, workforce employment, and military enlistment.

He previously supported marketing and communications efforts at UNC Charlotte, with a focus on photography, digital content creation, and visual storytelling.

In his new role, Barber will lead the Congressman’s press and digital communications efforts, helping communicate the office’s work to constituents across eastern North Carolina and ensuring residents remain informed about issues and initiatives affecting their communities.

“Christian brings a strong combination of education, communications experience, and a commitment to serving others,” said Congressman Don Davis. “His work helping young people prepare for life after high school and his experience in marketing and digital content, will be valuable assets to our team. I am excited to welcome Christian aboard and look forward to the energy, creativity, and perspective he will bring as we continue telling the story of eastern North Carolina and the work we are doing on behalf of its people.”

Barber said he is honored to join the Congressman’s team and serve the people of North Carolina’s First Congressional District.

“I am grateful for the opportunity to join Congressman Davis’ team and serve eastern North Carolina,” said Barber. “Public service has shown me the importance of listening, communicating clearly, and ensuring people have access to the information and opportunities they need. I look forward to helping tell the stories of the East and keeping the people of North Carolina’s 1st Congressional District informed and connected to the work of our congressional office.”

As Press Secretary and Digital Manager, Barber will work closely with the Congressman, congressional staff, local communities, and media outlets to communicate the office’s legislative priorities, constituent services, district activities, and accomplishments.

Representatives Budzinski and Sessions joined Bell for the tour, which was led by Postmaster General Steiner

Congressman Bell has been outspoken about postal issues in the St. Louis region and recently introduced the St. Louis Postal Accountability and Reform (STL Up To PAR) Act

Residents of the region have complained about mail delays that have impacted prescription medication, bills, ballots, and more

Congressman Bell: “We’re not here to criticize what is going right, we are here to figure out how to fix what is going wrong”

Washington, D.C. — Today, Representatives Wesley Bell (D-MO-01), Nikki Budzinski (D-IL-13), and Oversight and Government Reform Subcommittee on Government Operations Chairman Pete Sessions (R-TX-17) toured the United States Postal Service (USPS) St. Louis Processing and Distribution Center (P&DC) to better understand some of the postal issues impacting the region.

Postmaster General David Steiner led the tour. Steiner has been serving as Postmaster General since May 2025.

“We’re not here to criticize what is going right, we are here to figure out how to fix what is going wrong,” said Rep. Bell following the tour. “This isn’t a partisan issue – mail delays aren’t dictated by your political allegiance, which is why it is so important that these issues are being addressed in a bipartisan fashion. I look forward to working with Chairman Sessions and Congresswoman Budzinski to fix the postal problems people are facing here in St. Louis and across the nation.”

Congressman Bell has made it a priority in Congress to address the postal issues in the St. Louis region. Two audits by the U.S. Postal Service Office of the Inspector General (OIG) in 2025 found longstanding operational challenges that have caused persistent mail delays for residents across the St. Louis region. To address some of the issues detailed in the report, Rep. Bell introduced the bipartisan St. Louis Postal Accountability and Reform (STL Up To PAR) Act, with Congresswoman Ann Wagner (R-MO-02). The bill directs USPS to submit a report to Congress on mail and package delivery service performance in the St. Louis region. The legislation is not designed to penalize USPS, but to give both Congress and constituents a clear picture of where things stand and where work remains.
title: Congressman Bell Tours St. Louis USPS Facility with Postmaster General Steiner and House Oversight Members

WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), a senior member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, today sounded the alarm as the Trump Administration continues to threaten the deployment of ICE, CBP, or other armed federal agents at or near polling places during the 2026 midterm elections, warning that their presence could intimidate voters and suppress lawful participation.

In a letter to Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, Krishnamoorthi demanded a definitive statement of DHS policy after Mullin’s latest comments again left open the possibility of ICE appearing at polling places. President Trump has also said he would “do anything necessary” when asked whether he would send ICE or the National Guard to voting sites.

In the letter, Krishnamoorthi writes:

“With early voting and Election Day fast approaching, voters should not have to wonder whether federal immigration agents could appear at or near their polling place while they are casting their ballots. The presence of armed federal agents at or near a polling location—even when ostensibly responding to a separate law-enforcement matter—could create confusion, fear, or intimidation and could discourage eligible voters from exercising their constitutional right to vote.”

Krishnamoorthi warned that the threat is no longer theoretical. Republican candidates in Georgia, Maine, and Michigan have publicly discussed sending law enforcement, including ICE agents, U.S. Marshals, retired police officers, and the National Guard, to polling places in November. One candidate for governor of Maine has said he intends to ask the Trump Administration to send ICE agents and U.S. Marshals to voting sites.

The letter also points to the extraordinary volume of DHS records concerning possible federal deployments at election sites. ICE and CBP have told a federal court that they identified more than 127,000 pages of potentially responsive records concerning possible deployments of federal agents near polling places, ballot drop boxes, or election offices, yet neither agency had produced a single page as of the most recent filing.

Federal law sharply restricts the presence of armed personnel at polling places and separately prohibits federal officials from intimidating voters. Krishnamoorthi noted that election officials in at least eight states have already moved to establish buffer zones and other restrictions on federal agents near polling places in response to the Administration’s refusal to rule out such deployments.

Krishnamoorthi writes:

“The Department cannot simultaneously maintain, on one hand, that ICE has ‘no reason’ to be near a polling place, and on the other, that its Special Response Teams stand ready to deploy there. As the Department's Secretary, you are uniquely positioned to end this ambiguity.”

Krishnamoorthi is demanding that DHS provide:

A definitive, unqualified statement of Department policy on whether ICE, CBP, or any other DHS component will deploy personnel to, or within sight of, any polling place, ballot drop box, or election office during the early voting period or on Election Day 2026.

All guidance, directives, memoranda, or operational plans — including any related to Special Response Team deployment — concerning the presence of DHS personnel at or near polling locations for the 2026 elections.

A precise definition of the “specific threat” standard you have described publicly, including who within the Department is authorized to determine that the standard has been met and what review, if any, occurs before agents are dispatched to a polling site.

A status update on ICE's and CBP's document production in the pending Democratic National Committee FOIA litigation, including a timeline for completing review and release of the identified records.

Copies of any communications between Department leadership and the White House, the Department of Justice, the Department of Defense, or outside political advisers regarding the potential deployment of federal personnel to polling places in 2026.

Confirmation of what guidance, if any, the Department has issued to field offices regarding compliance with state buffer-zone laws that restrict federal agents' proximity to polling places.
title: Krishnamoorthi Sounds Alarm as Trump Administration Continues to Threaten to Deploy Armed Federal Agents to Polling Places

PITTSBURGH, PA – September 4, 2026 — Today, Congresswoman Summer L. Lee (PA-12) joined Trust for Public Land (TPL), Greenfield PreK-8 Neighborhood School, and community leaders to celebrate the opening of a new community schoolyard. The Congresswoman secured $400,000 in FY26 community project funding to support the transformation. The new schoolyard showcases how transforming paved and underused schoolyards can expand access to parks, create places for children to learn and play, and help neighborhoods become more climate resilient. The event, hosted at Greenfield Elementary, included a brief speaking program and a walkthrough of the new community schoolyard with students and parents.

During her remarks, Rep. Lee highlighted her Revitalizing America’s Schoolyards Act, legislation to help schools nationwide transform their schoolyards into vibrant, nature-rich spaces for learning, play, and community use. She introduced the bill in April 2026 with Senator Martin Heinrich from New Mexico.

“Greenfield Elementary’s transformed schoolyard is a powerful example of what public investment can mean for a community: a safe place for children to play, a green space where families can gather, and a third space where neighbors can connect with one another and with nature,” said Rep. Lee. “I’m proud to have supported this incredible transformation with $400,000 in federal funds and to have introduced the Revitalizing America’s Schoolyards Act to help communities across the country follow Greenfield’s example and transform schoolyards into greener, healthier, more resilient spaces for generations to come.”

“Greenfield shows that a schoolyard can be so much more than a place for recess—it can be a park, a classroom, a gathering place, and a tool for building healthier, more resilient neighborhoods,” said Danielle Denk, Director of the Community Schoolyards Program at Trust for Public Land. “These spaces also give children more opportunities to put down their screens, get outside, and connect with nature and one another. Congresswoman Summer Lee’s leadership in advancing the Revitalizing America’s Schoolyards Act recognizes the power of these spaces and the need for investment to help communities across the country transform asphalt into vibrant places where children and families can connect with the outdoors.”

“We are grateful to Congresswoman Summer Lee for securing this important investment, which will transform Pittsburgh Greenfield’s schoolyard into a space shaped by student voice and designed to support learning, play, connection and well-being,” said Pittsburgh Public Schools Superintendent Dr. Wayne N. Walters. “We appreciate Congresswoman Lee’s partnership, her advocacy for our students and her recognition of the important role our school spaces play in supporting students and strengthening communities.”

Greenfield is a powerful local example of what public investment can accomplish. Led by Trust for Public Land’s Community Schoolyards program, the project transformed the schoolyard into a greener, more welcoming space with new play equipment and connection to nature. The project will serve Greenfield’s students and more than 2,500 neighbors within a 10-minute walk.

The project also illustrates the role schoolyards can play in addressing extreme heat and building climate resilience. Students at Greenfield helped develop the design through 8 weeks of participatory design, with focused STEAM lessons focused on climate and health challenges facing their community.

Photos from the event can be found here.
title: Rep. Summer Lee Celebrates New Schoolyard Supported by $400K in Federal Funds, Highlights Bill to Transform Schoolyards

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Yesterday, Representatives Suhas Subramanyam (D-VA), Ted Lieu (D-Los Angeles County), and Joe Neguse (D-CO) introduced the No Pardon Paydays Act.

Trump has handed out blanket pardons to January 6th insurrectionists and those who padded his pockets – including those who engaged in acts of violence. Many of the January 6th insurrectionists who received pardons have since committed new crimes.

The No Pardon Paydays Act would prevent corruption in the pardon process by requiring the Pardon Attorney to submit a review to Congress of any criminal history of the pardon recipient. It would also prohibit pardon recipients from making high dollar contributions to political committees associated with the President who granted the pardon.

“Time and time again, trump uses pardons as favors for his pals and donors. This blatant corruption is dangerous to our democracy and our communities,” said Congressman Lieu. “I am pleased to partner with Rep. Subramanyam on the No Pardon Paydays Act, which would mitigate the perverse practice of paying for Presidential pardons. You should not be able to buy your way out of justice, no matter how much money you donate to the President.”

“This administration is the most corrupt in modern American history. Every American is paying the price while this administration lines their pockets and dishes out favors to their friends. We refuse to stand by and watch this unfold. There must be consequences for this corruption while we work to restore the American people’s trust,”

said Congressman Subramanyam.

“Donald Trump has repeatedly abused the presidential pardon power to give get out of jail free cards to violent, convicted felons who assaulted Capitol Police officers on January 6th, and benefit close political allies and the members of his inner circle. This cannot stand. That’s why I’m proud to join Rep. Subramanyam’s effort to put a commonsense check on presidential pardons, ensuring regardless of who’s in the White House, the power is used fairly and responsibly,” said Congressman Neguse.
title: REPS LIEU, SUBRAMANYAM, AND NEGUSE INTRODUCE THE NO PARDON PAYDAYS ACT

WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) participated Thursday in the first stop of Indian American Impact’s national listening tour in Norcross, Georgia, where South Asian elected officials, community leaders, and residents gathered to address the rise in hate, harassment, and violence targeting South Asian Americans. The Georgia gathering followed Wednesday’s national roundtable on Capitol Hill and focused on what communities are experiencing and how federal, state, and local leaders can strengthen prevention, reporting, and accountability.

“The rise in hate, harassment, and violence against South Asian Americans demands a response across the country,” Krishnamoorthi said. “After bringing South Asian leaders together in Washington, we are continuing that work here in Georgia with community members and public officials to improve prevention, reporting, and accountability for hate crimes. South Asian Americans have built their lives here, raised their families here, and strengthened communities across this country. We have to stand shoulder to shoulder against hate and violence whenever our communities are targeted.”

The listening session included Krishnamoorthi, Virginia Lieutenant Governor Ghazala Hashmi, Georgia State Senator Sheikh Rahman, Georgia State Representative Akbar Ali, Indian American Impact Executive Director Chintan Patel, SAATH founder Rohan Soni, and community leaders and advocates from across Georgia. Participants discussed what South Asian Americans are seeing and experiencing, how government is responding, and what additional steps could help communities confronting hate and discrimination. The Georgia gathering marked the beginning of Indian American Impact’s national listening tour, which is intended to hear directly from community members about their experiences and what additional steps are needed to confront hate targeting South Asian Americans.

Earlier this year, Krishnamoorthi reintroduced the bipartisan Hate Crimes Commission Act, which would establish a bipartisan commission to examine what is driving hate crimes, including the role of social media and technology, assess barriers to complete reporting, and identify successful prevention and response strategies.
title: Krishnamoorthi Continues National Push to Combat Rising Hate Against South Asian Americans at Georgia Event

Washington, DC. — Representative Dave Min (CA-47), a member of the House Oversight Committee and its Subcommittee on Economic Growth, Energy Policy, and Regulatory Affairs, slammed Republicans for using a hearing titled “No Flame, More Pain: How State and Local Bans on Natural Gas Increase Costs” to defend aging gas infrastructure and attack cheaper, cleaner energy alternatives.

WATCH HERE

During the hearing, Representative Min pushed back on arguments about the intermittency of renewable energy, pointing to innovations in battery storage technology. Energy expert Dr. Pete Wyckoff reinforced Representative Min’s argument noting that battery storage is becoming “cheaper and cheaper”.

Republicans also invoked China's growing energy influence while arguing for greater investment in fossil fuels. Representative Min called out the flagrant contradiction, noting that over 80% of China’s new energy capacity last year came from renewable sources and warning that China is gaining global influence by exporting cheaper renewable energy and battery technology around the world.

“As we move forward, it is clear that renewable energy is the future. It is going to be cheaper and in many places it is already cheaper,” said Rep Min. “And doubling down on aging oil and gas infrastructure is like doubling down on the horse and buggy or wood burning stoves.”

Rep. Min also highlighted the Trump Administration's war on clean energy, including an agreement to reimburse TotalEnergies for relinquishing offshore wind leases after the company invests roughly $1 billion in U.S. oil and gas production. While China races to dominate the global clean energy sector, Rep. Min warned that Republican policies are leaving the United States further behind.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04) led 27 of his colleagues in a letter to Education Secretary Linda McMahon demanding she provide answers and transparency about the growing federal student loan default crisis as nearly a record of 10 million borrowers enter default under the Trump Administration.

The members warn that as millions of Americans struggle to keep up with student loan payments while also facing the rising costs of housing, food, healthcare and other basic necessities, the Department of Education, under Secretary McMahon’s leadership, has failed to protect borrowers as she focuses on dismantling the Department and undertaking big changes to the federal student loan system.

The members also raised concerns about changes to federal repayment options enacted under H.R. 1. Several existing repayment plans are being phased out and they worry that these changes could result in higher monthly payments or reduce access to affordable repayment options for some borrowers.

The Members emphasized that default can have serious and long lasting consequences for borrowers, including damaged credit, wage garnishment, seizure of tax refunds, and barriers to homeownership and economic mobility. These outcomes disproportionately affect low income borrowers, first-generation college students, borrowers of colors, and borrowers who attended institutions with historically lower completion rates.

“Student loan default should not become an inevitable consequence of pursuing higher education,” the lawmakers wrote in the letter. “Borrowers deserve accurate information, meaningful assistance, and a fair opportunity to remain in good standing with their loans.”

The letter is co-signed by Representatives: Henry C. "Hank" Johnson, Jr. (GA-04), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Jonathan L. Jackson (IL-01), Judy Chu (CA-28), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Alma S. Clarke (NY-09), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Nydia M. Velázquez (NY-07), Adelita S. Grijalva (AZ-07), Sylvia R. Garcia (TX-29), Greg Landsman (OH-01), James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11), Brittany Pettersen (CO-07), Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Paul D. Tonko (NY-20), Donald S. Beyer Jr. (VA-08), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), and Dave Min (CA-47).
